“I have to go back to my apartment today.” Lena said, not expecting Kara’s dramatic groan.

 

“Whyyy? You don’t even live there,” she whined, face-planting the couch cushions.

 

“Yes I do!” Kara snorted and lifted her head to shoot her a pointed look. “Whatever,” Lena huffed. “I need more clothes, I’m running out.”

 

“You haven’t worn anything of yours in days, you can just keep wearing my stuff.” Kara argued.

 

“Yeah, ‘cos I have like three outfits here and one of them is covered in brick dust.” Kara sat up and grabbed the hem of the sweatshirt she was wearing, tugging until Lena fell back onto the couch.

 

“C’mere.” Kara pulled at the sweatshirt again. Lena laid back, half in Kara’s lap. “Just wear my stuff,” she pouted.

 

“I’ll be gone for like half an hour.” Lena rolled her eyes.

 

“Too long,” she whined.

 

“Darling,” she drawled.

 

“Wifey,” Lena fought the smile creeping onto her face.

 

“Stop.”

 

“Hero!” Kara called. Lena heard him get up from his bed.

 

“Don’t you dare!” Lena sat up, Kara wrapped her arms around Lena’s torso, keeping her trapped.

 

“Hero, she’s going to leave us again!” Hero didn’t understand what she was saying but he did understand the wrestling match that was going on.

 

“Don’t bring him into this!” Lena fought her hold and spun around, pressing her hand against Kara’s mouth. Hero climbed onto the couch and stuck his head in-between theirs, he whined softly. “I’ll be half an hour,” she said firmly, she could feel Kara’s pout beneath her hand. “Don’t pout.”

 

Kara’s phone began ringing and Lena removed her hand so she could answer it. “Danvers,”

 

“Kara, I need you to come in right away.” Winn said.

 

Kara rolled her eyes and groaned internally. “Winn, it’s my day off,” she whined.

 

“I know, and I’m sorry, but I need your expertise.” He replied.

 

“What is it?”

 

“I can’t explain over the phone. I need to show you, I really think it’s something big.” Kara didn’t want to go into the office, she wanted to stay in the peaceful bubble of domestic bliss, but Winn was her friend and she didn’t want to brush him off again.

 

“Okay, I’m on my way.” Kara put the phone down. “Looks like you’re off the hook, I have to go into work,” she sighed.

 

“Oh, Hero now look at who’s leaving.”

 

“Don’t even start.” Kara pointed. “I gotta go get changed.” Lena followed her upstairs.

 

“Nope, not that one.” Lena said from where she was lounging on the bed.

 

“Y’know, I’m going in for like a hour, it’s not fashion week.” Kara grumbled, Lena grabbed the shirt and threw it over her shoulder.

 

“Darling, let me just remind you who you’re dealing with. Also, how was that shirt not thrown out with the others?” Lena pulled out one of her nice, white shirts, navy pants and the matching waistcoat. Kara shrugged on the shirt and Lena kissed the exposed skin.

 

“You know, this isn’t helping me get dressed.” Lena continued her ministrations.

 

“But, this is much more fun and you’re already half way undressed.” Lena purred. She kissed Kara’s chest and sucked on her collarbones. Kara moaned and tipped her head back when Lena scraped her nails down her back and pulled at the waistband of her underwear.   

 

“We can’t, babe.” She felt Lena smile against her skin, she pressed open mouth kisses up her neck and behind her ear.

 

“Yes, we can.” Her smoky voice surrounding Kara, she licked the shell of her ear. She was in real danger of giving in.

 

Lena sucked on her earlobe and Kara’s eyes fluttered shut.

 

“Yes, we can.” Kara conceded, she lifted Lena and threw her onto the bed.

 

Half and hour later and Kara was finally dressed. “You’re gonna get me in so much trouble,” she said, shoving her feet into her shoes.

 

“You do realise you risk that every day?” Lena replied, she was curled around her pillow, sheets pooled around her waist, the pale skin of her back was so tempting.

 

“And, it’s so worth it,” Kara bent down and kissed her. “I’ll be back soon.”

 

“This means I get to go back to my apartment without all the hassle?” Lena said.

 

“I mean, they’ll be no hassle from me,” Kara said, raising her eyebrows. Hero was already on edge now he knew Kara was leaving.

 

“Shit.”

 

__________

 

“Where have you been?” Winn whisper-shouted.

 

“Traffic was a bitch.” Kara said, hiding her grin. She pulled up a chair and sat down at his desk. “Tell me what you got, Winny.”

 

“Okay, so, I couldn’t find anything solid on Lena Luthor. No, Lena Luthor’s that would interest us in any way.” Kara took a deep breath, she had a feeling this wasn’t going to be good.

 

“So, I ran the name Luthor through all known criminal data bases. A couple of hits, petty crimes, parking tickets. No one relating to a Lena Luthor though. Then, I thought about all the reasons someone may catch our attention: saw something, knew something, did something or said something.” Kara swallowed.

 

“You think she’s a journalist.”

 

“Well, I did. I ran the name through the National and International news database, couldn’t find anything. So, I searched the name Luthor again. I trawled through hundreds of articles and I found this,” he handed her a copy of a small article.

 

STILL MISSING: BABY GIRL LUTHOR.

“What is this?” Kara asked.

 

“Read the last paragraph.”

 

Police have no leads as to who may have taken the baby, but they are very worried about the health of the child and how the current weather conditions could be detrimental to the her survival. The child’s mother is desperately pleading for anyone with any information, as to the whereabouts of her daughter, to come forward. She told her doctor today, that she wished to call her baby girl, Lena.

Kara fought the urge to gasp, fought against every instinct that screamed at her and managed to keep her facial expression neutral.

 

“When was this article written?”

 

“October 28th, 1993.” Kara bit the inside of her cheek to keep herself from exploding, those sick fuckers kidnapped her and then exploited her mother’s grief and named her on the same day she went to the press to plead for help. Kara’s blood was boiling, she clenched the fist that was out of Winn’s view. “So, you think we’ve solved a twenty-eight year old kidnapping?”

 

“Well, you mentioned her name, do you know where she is?” Winn asked excitedly.

 

Kara avoided the question, “hang on a minute. A baby went missing, how was this not front page news? Why wasn’t there a full scale man-hunt?”

 

“She was a teenage, single parent in a small, very religious town.” Winn looked down, “they didn’t want to ‘promote that kind of behaviour’.” Kara’s stare hardened, “those were the actual words written by the grandparents on the police report.”

 

“They were going to make her give up the baby?”

 

“They were going to try. The mother was the one who contacted the press and from what I can tell, she never gave up looking for her daughter.” Winn pulled up her file, Lillian Luthor: there were multiple articles written about the disappearance of her daughter but only one mentioned her full name and none of them made front page news.

 

“Okay, give me the details, Winn.” Kara had to make sure that this was her Lena and not another child somehow.

 

“Well, the baby was born October 24th, 1993. She was almost a month premature and weighed just 4lbs 2oz, that’s why they were so concerned about her health, the weather conditions were cold and wet, they were afraid that even if they did find her, she probably wouldn’t survive anyway.” Winn swallowed thickly.

 

“She was taken the day after she was born. No witnesses, no CCTV, no suspects. The police searched everywhere they thought she could possibly be and the only thing they found was her hospital bracelet.” Winn handed her the photo: it had her last name, her mother’s name and her date of birth written on it.

 

“Do the police still have this?” Winn shook his head.

 

“A few years after the police closed the investigation, the mother requested to have it back. They gave it to her, of course, it was the only thing she had left of her daughter.” She could see that Winn was affected by this, cases involving children were always hard, no matter how old they were.

 

“Let’s take a break. Go get some water or a cup of coffee, take five minutes.” He nodded and stood up, “this is really good work, Winn.” Kara went to the bathroom and splashed water on her face. How was she supposed to explain this to Lena? She refused to admit it, but she was still suffering from the affects of telling Kara about her past. The nightmares were rare now but no less terrifying for either girl. Lena was worse than her when it came to bottling things up and Kara was afraid that this would destroy her.

 

Then something else popped into her head, if Lena was kidnapped, how many of the other girls were really ‘adopted’?

 

Kara read through the whole article while she waited for Winn. “Who was the doctor that the mother spoke to?” Kara asked, everything she knew about this organisation had given her a hunch.

 

“Um,” Winn looked through the files. “She was a locum, Dr Whitmore. She arrived shortly after the baby was taken to cover staff sickness and was assigned to Lillian.”

 

“When did she leave?”

 

“Two days after the article was published.” If Kara was right, this “locum” was one of the women Lena was raised by and she was sent in to gather information and keep tabs on the police investigation.

 

“Do you think you could find any other baby girls that were kidnapped in the same year whose names would also have been announced in the press?” If Kara was right, then everything those poor girls were brought up to believe was built on lies.

 

“I can write a program that will do that, but it may take a while.”

 

“Do it, I’ll see what else I can find.” Kara pulled out her phone.

 

LL: I thought you said you’d be an hour :(

 

KD: Sorry, babe. This is going to take a while I think.

 

LL: Hero’s gonna be pissed.

 

KD: He’ll get over it.

 

LL: Let me know when you’re on your way back, I’ll make dinner.

 

Kara smiled weakly at her phone and threw herself into her work so she would be distracted, Lena deserved her best on this one.

 

She delved into Lillian Luthor, wanting to get a feel for the woman and needing to rule out her parents involvement. She checked Lillian’s internet history, “she has an account with multiple missing person websites.” Kara searched Lena and Lillian’s name but nothing came up. Why would you make an account and then not post anything about your daughter?

Kara searched through the site records and found that Lillian had posted multiple times about Lena, listing the details of her daughter, begging for any information. Each and every post was flagged and pulled down by the site administrators.

 

“Winn, I’m gonna send something over, can you find out why it was taken down?” Kara asked, she sent over everything she had and looked into who Lillian was now.

 

She moved out of her small town not long after Lena was born, she went to college and worked to pay her way through law school. She now worked as a business attorney for a high profile tech company. Lillian got married but kept her maiden name, Kara wondered if that was because she still had hope that Lena would find her someday.

 

There was nothing to suggest that she ever went through such a heartbreaking event. Well, now I know that bottling up emotions runs in the family. Lillian suffered with her pain on her own.

 

“Okay, apparently they were taken down for violating the community guidelines.” Kara rolled her chair over, “but I don’t know how. They’re the same kind of content and format as everything else on the site. She even copied another person’s post and just changed the details to fit her own circumstances and it was still taken down.”

 

“Can you trace the IP address of who took it down?” Kara asked, he nodded and Kara watched him work.

 

“Well, they definitely weren’t taken down by any of the administration, but I can’t trace the IP address, it changes with every post, bouncing around the world: some of these are Russian, Chinese, Swiss. Whoever did this knew exactly what they were doing.” Winn said.

 

“Someone was intentionally trying to silence this woman.” Kara said, she did a quick google search of Lena’s name but couldn’t find anything on her disappearance or Lillian even talking about it.

 

She carried on looking into Lillian and found that she had three email accounts: a work email, a personal email and a third. Kara looked into it, the third email was linked to one website. Kara searched the website and found something that almost looked like Lillian Luthor’s personal diary.

 

Kara felt like she was intruding somehow.

 

“Look at this,” she ushered Winn over, not taking her eyes off the screen. “She’s been writing blog posts and letters to Lena for years. On her birthday, Christmas, important milestones.” Kara pinched her brow, this was far from the incapable, young mother Lena’s boss had made her out to be.

 

Winn worked on writing his computer program and Kara read through the entirety of Lillian’s website. She held back her tears, she could feel the pain she was expressing, Lillian still missed her daughter after all this time.

 

She cleared her throat, covering her sniffle. “It’s been a long day, Winn. I’m going to head home.”

 

“Me too, I finished the program so I’ll run it before I leave and we can go over the results tomorrow.” Kara nodded and stood up.

 

“Good job today.”

 

Kara cried as soon as she got in her car. Lena was never meant to be there, none of them were. These people preached about how they were there for a higher purpose that these girls somehow owed them for saving their lives. It was all a lie.

 

“Hey,” Kara greeted Hero, tiredly.

 

“Hey!” Kara looked over and saw Lena’s smiling face. “How was your day?” Kara forced a smile onto her face. She silently walked over to where Lena was stood and scooped her up in a tight hug, inhaling her scent.

 

“What’s this for?” Lena asked, hugging her back.

 

“Missed you,” she mumbled.

 

“I missed you too.” Kara let her go and kissed her, cupping both of her cheeks. “Are you okay?” Lena frowned.

 

“Uh huh, of course.” Kara gave her a wide smile and Lena eyed her warily.

 

“Oh, I have a surprise! You’re gonna love me,” she squealed, forgetting all about Kara’s strange behaviour.

 

“Already do, thanks for noticing.” Kara teased. “What is it?”

 

“So, I was doing my laundry earlier-”

 

“Wait, you do laundry?” Kara frowned.

 

“I’m sorry, do you think fairies wash my clothes?” Kara snorted.

 

“Now, there’s a sight for sore eyes, you don’t do anything like that here.” Lena’s mouth formed the perfect ‘O’ and Kara laughed.

 

“Well, I don’t live here, you can do your own housework.” She turned in a huff, Kara grabbed her waist and pulled her back, kissing her neck.

 

“Finish your story, babe.” She kissed the side of her head.

 

“Oh yeah, so I was checking the pockets and look what I found in my jeans.” Lena pulled out the pendent Kara had given her.

 

“No way!” Kara inspected it and it was indeed the same one, not that she doubted Lena. “I thought you threw it off a cliff?”

 

“So did I! I guess even drunk me wasn’t ready to let it go just yet.” When Lena had stumbled, trying to get to her feet, she’d slipped the necklace into her pocket and swapped it out for a rock, it was a practised move she could execute even blind drunk. She couldn’t remember much about that night, but she vividly remembered throwing something off the cliff and woke up to no pendent around her neck.

 

Kara clasped it around her neck and Lena felt complete again. “Beautiful.” Kara mumbled.

 

“Come on, dinner’s almost ready.”

 

“I reckon two more months and I could have you fully domesticated.” Kara teased.

 

“Don’t push it,” Lena warned.

 

For those few minutes, Kara’s mind was on nothing but that moment, it was bliss. But, while she was getting changed, it all came flooding back to her.

 

Now, they were sat next to each other eating dinner and Kara just felt sick. “What’s wrong?” Lena asked, “do you not like it?”

 

Tell her. Tell her. Tell her.

 

“Nothing, sorry. The food is great, I just have a bit of a headache, I’ve been staring at a screen all day.” She gave Lena a small, reassuring smile.

 

Coward.

“I’ll get you some aspirin.” Lena put her plate down and kissed her forehead. She needed to tell her, they promised each other there’d be no more secrets.

 

“Thank you,” Kara said when she returned.

 

Kara used the excuse that she couldn’t tell her after dinner because Lena turned into the ever loving and doting girlfriend. She cleared away their plates and pulled her against her against her body and Kara tucked her face into her neck.

 

Tell her. Tell her. Tell her.

She was going to, she really was and then Lena started massaging her scalp and she just couldn’t get the words out. Instead, she pressed kisses to her neck and enjoyed the quiet time, tears stung behind her eyes.

 

“You wanna go lay down properly?” Kara nodded.

 

Lena pulled her to her feet and gave her a quick peck before leading her upstairs. “Lena, wait-” it was now or never. “I have to tell you something.”  

 

“I hate those words, nothing good ever starts with that sentence.” Lena teased lightly, Kara looked down and swallowed hard. Lena then realised that this was serious, she sat down on the foot of the bed. “What is it? What’s going on?”

 

“Back at the beginning, when I was investigating you, I asked a friend to look into you. He’s better with computers and I figured if I couldn’t find anything, he definitely could and… he did… find something.” Kara fidgeted back and forth.

 

“That’s impossible,” Lena said calmly. “I don’t leave anything behind, I don’t have a trail.”

 

“It’s not something you left behind.” This was quite possibly the worst thing she’d ever had to tell someone. “He found a news article about a young mother whose baby was stolen from the hospital the day after she was born…” Lena had a deep, confused frown set in her brow. “The police hit a dead end, right from the beginning they had no leads as to where she was or who took her.” Lena waited patiently and Kara sighed. “I have strong evidence to suggest that child was you, Lena.”

 

Lena stared at her blankly for a second, “good one.” She chuckled, “not that funny though.”

 

Kara frowned, her head jerked as if she’d been slapped. “Why would I joke about that?”

 

Lena stood up, “I don’t know, you’re mad at me for questioning your decision to stay at the CIA?”

 

“I’m not mad at you! Even if I was, do you really think I would make up some story to get back at you?” Kara wasn’t going to get mad, she refused to lose her cool.

 

“I don’t know, but I don’t believe it.” Lena said, she stood and walked down the stairs.

 

“Wait, where are you going?” Kara reached out for her, but Lena brushed her off.

 

“To think.”

 

“You’re not even gonna hear what I have to say?” Lena grabbed her jacket and walked out of the door.

 

Well, Kara wasn’t expecting that, she thought that Lena would be upset, angry even. She never thought that Lena wouldn’t even consider what she’d said to be true. She wasn’t angry or upset, she was just confused.

 

Kara got ready for bed but she couldn’t sleep until she knew Lena was home.

 

__________

 

Lena wandered around aimlessly, it was late and the park was empty. She sat on a bench and pulled out her phone.

 

“Hey, Lee! What’s up?” Sam answered.

 

“Not much, I just needed to hear a familiar voice.” Lena said. “What are you up to?”

 

“I just finished an assignment. I’m being sent to The Academy next week to help out with the next stage of training.” She replied.

 

“Easy work,” Lena commented.

 

“I know, but Helena is driving me mad already and I’m not even there yet.”  She grumbled.

 

“Come on, lay it on me.” Lena said. She brought her knees up to her chest and listened to Sam rant about everything.

 

“What’s going on with you?” She asked once she’d finished.

 

“Did you ever ask anyone where you came from?”

 

“Well, when a Mommy and a Daddy love each other very much-”

“Oh, shut up.” Lena scoffed, rolling her eyes.

 

“My Mom gave me up for adoption, Nyssa picked me up from the orphanage and took me to The Academy.” She said, simply. “Why do you ask?”

“No reason, we were just never allowed to speak about it.” Lena said, nonchalantly.

 

“That’s because we left those lives behind.” Lena hummed.

 

“I know.”

 

“Is someone putting ideas in your head?” Lena hadn’t had a chance to have a real catch up with Sam about everything that had happened with Kara, and now didn’t seem like the right time.

 

“No, of course not. It’s just one of those things that popped into my head while I was bored.” Sam seemed to accept it. “Do you ever think about our childhood?”

 

“Sometimes. I try not to think about it though.” She paused for a second. “You’ve been asking me some really cryptic questions lately, what’s going on?”

“Well, you’re the only person I can ask this stuff, the only person I trust who understands exactly how I feel.” Lena fiddled with some dust on her jeans.

 

“What I mean is, you never used to ask this stuff.”

 

“Well, getting to have a taste of what everyone else has, it just makes me a little jealous, I guess. Don’t get me wrong, I’m still dedicated to the cause but I just…” She sighed again.

 

“You want it to be over.”

“Yeah.”

 

“To tell you the truth, I do too.” Sam admitted.

 

“Pfft, you just want a candy cottage.” Lena teased.

 

“Umm, it’s gingerbread cottage, decorated with candy. Get it right Lena, or do I need to tell the story again?”  Sam chided.

 

“God no.” She groaned and heard Sam’s chuckle. “It’s late, I should probably let you go.” Lena said.

 

“Alright well, call me if you need me.”

“I will, night Sammy.”

 

“Night, Lee.” Lena always felt better after speaking to Sam, not that she couldn’t speak to Kara, it was just that Sam had been through the same experiences she had.

 

Lena walked back to Kara’s apartment, slowly. Whatever “evidence” the CIA had fabricated may have Kara convinced, but Lena knew where she came from. She knew that Talia would never lie to her.

 

She crept through the door and quietly locked it. She got ready for bed, making sure not to disturb Kara. Lena crawled into bed and snuggled up to Kara’s back, she pressed a kiss in between her shoulder blades and looped an arm around her waist.

 

Kara smiled, she didn’t say anything, she was just happy that Lena was home.

 

__________

 

Kara woke up the next morning to the smell of coffee. She rolled over and buried her face in Lena’s stomach, she was resting against the headboard with a mug in her hand. Lena stroked the hair away from her face and looked into Kara’s sleepy blue eyes.

 

“Hi,” Lena said.

 

“Hey,” Kara smiled.

 

“Listen, I’m sorry about last night, I just needed some space to think about things.” Kara stroked her hip in small circles.

 

“I get it.” Kara said, her voice still thick with sleep.

 

“It’s not that I don’t believe you, I believe that you think what you were told is true. But, I don’t believe it.” She cleared her throat, “my upbringing may not have been ideal, but they never lied to us. I know where I come from.” Kara could hear the tremor in her voice.

 

She’s in denial. Of course, she’s in denial.

 

Kara could have shown her concrete proof that she had been kidnapped as a baby and Lena would have argued vehemently. It was a coping strategy, Lena had been through so much in the past few weeks that she probably couldn’t take much more.

 

“Okay.” Kara said, “obviously I didn’t mean to upset you, but we agreed on no more secrets and I couldn’t keep it from you.” Lena nodded.

 

“I appreciate it, but it’s not true and I don’t want to talk about it again.”

 

“Got it.” Kara nodded, “did you make me coffee?”

 

“Duh.” Kara sat up and Lena handed her a mug, “I love you.”

 

“I love you too,” Kara pecked her lips.

 

__________

 

Kara had said she wouldn’t talk about what she’d found with Lena, but she wasn’t going to stop her investigation. In some way, Kara felt like she was betraying her trust, but Lena and the rest of those poor girls deserved to know the truth.

 

For Lena’s sake, she needed to make sure this was watertight, there could be no doubt.

 

The pair worked silently, spending the day trawling through public records. Kara sifted through hundreds of missing person reports, looking for the same MO. She found three possible cases, but there was only one person who confirm it.

 

“Okay, I have twenty-three unsolved disappearances for that year across the country.” Winn announced.

 

“How many had a female locum show up around the same time the disappearances occurred, say three days either side?” Kara asked.

 

Winn typed something into the computer. “Six. Amelia McNeil, Samantha Arias, Leslie Willis, Carley D’Angelo, Sara Lance and Martha Scott.”

 

Kara didn’t know any names of the girls Lena grew up with, she was very specific about leaving names out.

 

“Can we expand the search to the rest of the world?” Winn nodded.

 

“Only to public news records, anything else and we’ll have to go through Interpol.”

 

“Do it.” There were thousands of disappearances and using the locum filter only narrowed it down by a fraction. They spent hours trawling through records identifying possible disappearances that could have been connected.

 

“Just explain to me why are we doing this? We don’t have any leads on who took these kids.” Winn said.

 

“I want to know how many people are involved.” Kara mumbled, not looking up from the screen.

 

“But, if you know where Lena Luthor is, she could give us everything we need.” Winn made a great point and Kara ignored it.

 

“I don’t know where she is.”

 

“But, she must be alive, else how did you get her name?” Kara was starting to get a little annoyed at the incessant questioning.

 

“Like I said, it was just a name that came up while I was investigating something else.” Kara shrugged, “I couldn’t find anything, so I asked you.”

 

“So, if the name came up, that implies she’s still alive. There has been no sign of these girls since they went missing, we need a team on this.” Kara shook her head.

 

“J’onn would never authorise that, this is all circumstantial.” Kara said. “And even if we did, this is a case for the FBI and Interpol, we’ll be pulled off before we could get anywhere. This stays between us for now.” Kara was right, this technically wasn’t a case for the CIA and she was in enough trouble already.

 

“Are you kidding? We have a lead in over thirty missing person cases, twenty-eight years after the police failed. Kara this is huge!” Winn exclaimed.

 

“It’s late, Winn. I’m tired and I want to go home.”

 

“Yeah, of course, me too.” He looked disappointed.

 

“You’ve done a really good job here, Winn.” Kara squeezed his shoulder on the way out. “We’ll get there.”

 

Kara got a call later that night. “Whassit Winn?”

 

“Sorry to wake you Kara, but there have been developments.”

Stay safe and stay happy!

Kara left her warm bed and her sleepy Lena to go back to the office at 2am. She picked up Big Belly Burger on the way and traipsed into the office, yawning.

 

“Hey,” she greeted. Winn spun around, he clearly had not left the office when Kara had, he was running on coffee and desperation. She placed the bag down in front of him and he moaned, “dig in, buddy.” He tore through the wrapping and shovelled half a double cheeseburger into his mouth.

 

“Ohm ma goth,” he groaned. Kara smiled and left him finish his food before she prompted him as to why she was here. “So, I was heading out when another file popped up, from three years ago.”

 

“Three years?” Winn nodded.

 

“So, I wrote another program and I put in all the details we know so far. I set the dates from 1980 to last year.” Kara frowned.

 

“You think there’s more?”

 

“A lot more.” Winn said. “So, we know about the thirty or so baby girls who were taken in 1993, nothing of significance happens for another four years and then suddenly, thirty again in 1997. In 2001 another thirty are taken, 2005 another thirty. And so on, and so on.” Winn finished his explanation and Kara realised just how deep this went.

 

It was clear to her now why they were never allowed to show their face, go to the hospital or leave the organisation. If their real names appeared on any kind of government document, the whole operation would be blown. Restricting the access of medical records and controlling every aspect of their lives, kept them isolated so that they would never feel like they had the freedom or the capacity to survive on their own. It was another example of the control they had over the girls.

 

It was smart in a disgusting, baby snatching kind of way.

 

“How has no one noticed?”

 

“Because, they were taken from countries all over the world. “No, but that’s why they made Curious George, so I could learn.” Kara said matter of factly.

 

“Right, so shall we go?” Kara nodded.

 

“Do you wanna take Polly?”

 

“Sure.” Lena took the bunny and they walked out together.

 

“There are probably more animals here, but I could only find these two.” Kara said, clearly downtrodden.

 

“Don’t worry, I sent everything I found to animal welfare already.” Kara raised her eyebrows. “Well, if I send it from these computers, it’ll look like someone blew the whistle rather than, someone broke in and stole a monkey and a rabbit.” Kara was impressed.

 

“You’re so smart.”

 

“I know.” They made their way to the parking lot and were met by flood lights and a squad of security guards with weapons.

 

“Do you think they know who we are?” Kara spoke out of the corner of her mouth.

 

“I think they know we’re not who we said we were.” Lena whispered back.

 

“Bean bags hurt like a bitch,” Kara murmured. Lena squinted and saw she was right, they weren’t carrying assault weapons, they were carrying shotguns and they definitely weren’t standard issue. Amateurs then.

 

“Put the monkey and the rabbit on the floor and step away.” The voice was emphasised by a megaphone.

 

Lena looked at Kara: Stanley was stood on her shoulders, tiny hands on her head. She looked down at the rabbit nestled in her arms. Lena slowly crouched down, “Lee, no.” She heard Kara’s tiny protest. She placed the bunny on the floor and pulled the pin of the smoke grenade in her tool kit.

 

“Run!” She hissed, lobbing it into the crowd.

 

“Grenade!” The team split and dived behind cover. Lena scooped the rabbit back up and they tore back through the building.

 

“What’s the plan, Lee?” Kara yelled, now cradling Stanley.

 

“This was my plan. My plan was to get us out of there!” Lena yelled back.

 

“Great plan! Now what?!” Lena skidded to a halt and looked around.

 

“Staircase!” They darted up the stairs to the second floor. “Take her.” Lena handed her Polly, “and these,” she slipped the car keys into her pocket. “Get to the fire escape and wait there,” Kara climbed out of the window with both animals. Lena slid over to the window facing the front of the building, it wouldn’t be long until the police arrived.

 

She pulled her weapon and expertly fired at the floodlights, the men scattered again, taking cover. Lena emptied another clip onto the crowd, firing at the cars this time. “Go!” She hissed. Kara used the sound of the gunfire to cover the sound of her heavy footsteps down the fire escape.

 

Lena watched as Kara scurried across the parking lot, Stanley clinging to her head now. Once she made it to the van, Lena made her move, she reloaded her gun and hurried down the fire escape.

 

The guards were just starting to regroup when Kara sped out of the parking space, side door wide open. They scattered again, diving to avoid the speeding car. Lena had to sprint from where she was to be able to meet her, she dived at full stretch and slid into the van on her belly. Kara crashed through the security barrier and onto the open road.

 

“You okay?” She called back.

 

“Yeah,” Lena panted.

 

Eventually, Lena regained her composure and slid the door shut. She climbed over the seats and took Polly from where she was resting on Kara’s lap. The animals seemed remarkably unaffected to say they’d just been involved in, what was essentially, their own kidnap and reckless driving.

 

They dumped the van and switched to Kara’s SUV. “You wanna get some food?” Kara suggested.

 

“Yeah, I could eat.” Lena said. They went to the drive-through at Big Belly Burger, ignoring the funny looks and accepting the adoration towards the animals. They continued on to the all-night supermarket and Kara hurried back with a bag of carrots and- “is that a mango?”

 

“They didn’t have any bananas,” Kara shrugged.

 

They sat in the parking lot, eating their food. It was quite a sight to behold: Kara was happily munching on her burger, humming a happy tune while a small monkey sat on her shoulder, it almost looked as if he was dancing while he tucked into his mango. Lena stared straight ahead, nibbling on her fries with a fluffy, white bunny gnawing on a carrot in her lap.

 

“Some date night, huh?” Kara said, laughter gracing her tone. Lena looked over, Kara was biting back a smile, Lena’s mouth split into a wide smile and they broke into a fit of giggles.

 

__________

 

“You know we can’t keep them, right?” Lena said, he voice barely above a whisper.

 

“I know,” Kara sighed, “they could be traced back to us.”

 

“It was a nice thought, maybe in the future.” Lena said, Kara smiled at the faint glimmer of a future together.

 

“Yeah, plus Hero would be furious if I came home with two new competitors for my attention.” Lena stroked Polly’s soft fur and Kara cradled Stanley. “Can you find the nearest animal shelter?” Lena nodded.

 

They walked through the entrance of the animal shelter, “It’s 1am, do you think that they’ll be anyone around?” Lena said.

 

“I have no idea.” Kara rang the bell at the entrance desk. “Hello!” She called, “why would they leave the door unlocked?” Just then a sleepy looking lady emerged from the office at the back.

 

“Hey, um, we have some animals we’d like to… drop off.” The woman gave her a sleepy glare, Lena awkwardly placed Polly on the top  of the desk. “This… this is Polly.”

 

Kara placed her arm on the desk and Stanley scampered down her arm and howled in greeting. “This is Stanley.” Kara shot the woman a smile.

 

“We can’t take the monkey,” she grumbled.

 

“What? Why? He’s great. Look at that face!” Kara exclaimed.

 

“We don’t take exotic animals. You’ll have to call PETA, they’ll send someone out to examine it-”

 

“-Stanley”

 

The woman looked up, “Stanley. They will then find a place for him.”

 

“Huh, well, it seems like you know a lot more about that then us sooo,” Lena grabbed Kara’s arm and ran out the door.

 

“I love you guys! His favourite food is mango!” Kara yelled as they ran. They got into the car and sped away.

 

“I miss them already,” Lena said, quietly.

 

“I know, but you’re right, we can’t look after them properly. I barely look after Hero,” she joked.

 

“Thank god for dog walkers and sitters.” Lena commented.

 

“I seriously need to give that girl a raise.” Kara made a mental note to do just that.

 

The drive home took a couple more hours and by the time they got in, it was almost dawn. Kara collapsed onto the bed, “we did good tonight.” She mumbled into the pillow.

 

“We did.” Lena groaned, she stretched her arms above her head, relishing in the feeling. She got undressed and climbed into bed, she nudged Kara with her foot, “is that where you’re gonna stay?” referring to the starfish taking up most of the space.

 

“No.” She paused, “just five more minutes.” Eventually, Kara got ready for bed and climbed into bed behind her. She reached out and felt Lena’s soft, bare skin, “mmm, what are you wearing?” She lifted the blankets, “not a lot apparently.” Kara smirked, Lena was in nothing but her underwear, Kara shuffled over to her.

 

“Don’t.” Lena murmured, closing her eyes. Kara’s head popped up and she looked down at her, “you can sleep on your side of the bed.” She said.

 

“Why?” She whined.

 

“Because, I don’t want you to touch me.” She stated, simply.

 

Kara huffed and moved backwards, “I thought you said date night went well.”

 

“It did. Just think how good it would have been if you hadn’t pulled that stunt in the control room.” Kara sighed, why did I ever think I could one up her?

Kara considered her options for a fraction of a second: go to bed horny and without cuddles or… Kara grabbed her hips and pulled her to the centre of the bed, “Kara!” She squealed. Kara tore her panties off and dived between her legs, “fuck!”

 

Kara dragged four orgasms out of her before Lena pushed her head away.

 

“So, do I get a cuddle now?” Lena made a non-committal noise. “Oh, stop being grumpy.” Kara grabbed her waist and squeezed, Lena jerked and Kara grinned before pulling her backwards into her arms.

 

__________

 

Kara groaned when her alarm blared the next morning, she didn’t get nearly enough sleep last night and she could feel the headache building behind her eyes. She rolled over and pulled a pillow over her head to block out the light.

 

Lena placed her mug down on the night stand, “come on, darling. You still have to go to work today.” Kara grumbled, it was probably something sarcastic. Lena pulled the blankets off of her and laughed at the overzealous whine. She straddled Kara’s hips and dug her palms into her back, massaging the tense muscles, she knocked the pillow off her head.

 

“This isn’t making me want to get up,” she mumbled. Lena placed a kiss between her shoulder blades, she pressed her thumbs into Kara’s lower back and enjoyed the deep moan she elicited.

 

“I made coffee?” Lena offered.

 

“Nope.” Kara said.

 

“I got you some aspirin for the headache I know you’ll have?” Lena moved up to massage her shoulders.

 

“Nope.”

 

“I made breakfast?” Kara cracked one eye open.

 

“What did you make?”

 

“Pancakes.” Lena whispered into her ear.

 

“Hmm, I could eat pancakes.” Kara stretched.

 

“Well, that was easier than I expected.” Lena kissed her neck, cheek and then her ear.

 

“Don’t count this as a win just yet, you still have to get me dressed and out of the door.” She dragged herself out of bed.  “So, good luck with that.”

 

“Okay, let’s just start with pancakes and go from there.” Lena pushed her towards the stairs and Kara begrudgingly did as she was told.

 

Lena managed to get her to eat and get dressed without much trouble, it’s was probably because Kara didn’t have to make any of the decisions. Lena adjusted her tie and straightened her jacket, “how do I look?” Kara said.

 

“Perfect.” Lena said, pecking her lips.

 

Kara grinned, “you know, I could just take a sick day.” She took Lena’s hands and mustered her very best puppy dog eyes.

 

“Go to work.”

 

“I still have some holiday time left?” Kara said as Lena guided her down the stairs.

 

“Go to work.”

 

“I could just blow it off and stay here with you guys? “ Kara looked back with a hopeful look in her eyes.

 

“Kara, my sweet, darling Kara,” she cupped her face and pinched her cheeks. Kara’s eyes lit up. “Go to work.” She whispered, patting her cheek with finality.

 

“Fine.” She grumbled, “I love you,”

 

“I love you too. I’ll see you later, be good.” Lena kissed her deeply and pushed her out of the door.

 

Kara grumbled all the way to work.

 

Winn greeted her with a cup of coffee, good coffee, rather than the crap they serve in the office. She smiled and then frowned, “what’s this for?”

 

“It’s a thank you for the other night,” Kara raised an eyebrow, “okay, the feds are coming to pick up the files today.”

 

“Well, thanks for the coffee.” He nodded.

 

“For what it’s worth, I really wanted to keep this one as well.” She gave him a small smile and walked into her office, growling as soon as she shut the door.

 

She knew that the FBI wouldn’t get anywhere, the only reason Kara knew what was going on was because Lena had told her. She had absolutely no idea who was running the whole operation and the feds had even less to go on.

 

If Kara didn’t do something, Lena would never accept the truth.

 

She searched for Lena’s friend and the only Sam she could find was Samantha Arias: she was taken a few months before Lena and her birth parents now lived in Arizona with a second daughter, Ruby. 

 

Kara spent the day trying to find any kind of lead, but these people were good. It made sense, Lena was a expert in evasion and no doubt she’d been taught that by the same people who had taken her in the first place.

 

Kara had hit a wall, she was trying not to get angry. She was working really hard on not losing her temper: she counted to ten, counted back from ten and then took a few deep breaths. But, this was Lena and the thought of someone hurting her made her blood boil, so when none of those techniques worked, she played Tetris.

 

She knew exactly when the FBI agents entered the office. For starters, the whole office stopped and secondly, they dress like funeral directors. Okay, so I may have dressed like that at some point, but now I have my own personal shopper and stylist.

Kara stood and leaned against the doorway, watching as J’onn greeted them. Kara eyed them warily, she knew exactly what he was going to do. “Danvers, can you fetch the files from my office, please.” He could have asked someone else to do it: someone who wasn’t the head of the team, someone who wasn’t the furthest away from his office, but he was clearly trying to show her who was boss. Classic power move… Huh, I never would have guessed that before, Lena really is rubbing off on me.

He might be making a move, but Kara could make her own damn move. She casually strolled to J’onn office, taking her sweet time, no urgency whatsoever. She effortlessly lifted the boxes off the desk and walked back over. One of the agents reached out and Kara dropped them into his arm. J’onn glared at her with that permanently fixed frown on his faee.

 

“Good luck,” she said with a sweet smile.

 

She walked back to her office and closed the door behind her. She knew he was furious but technically she didn’t do anything wrong.

 

Kara thought about what she was going to do and, as always, something Lena had said stuck in her mind.

 

She had an idea.

 

If she did this, it would cause chaos: she would probably lose her job, there would be a huge target on her back and Lena, well Lena would never speak to her again. That was the risk she would have to take because she couldn’t keep pretending like everything was fine and there was no way that she was allowing them to kidnap another round of children.

 

She knew she had to give it one last shot with Lena, try to get her to believe she was telling the truth.

 

__________

 

“Hey, you made it all the way through the work day! I’m proud of you.” Lena greeted when Kara walked through the door that night.

 

“Annnd, I finally picked up the doughnuts I promised!” Kara announced, holding up the box. Kara skipped over to her and Lena tipped her head back so Kara could kiss her.

 

“Thank god, I was starting to think I was losing my touch.” She teased. Kara hopped the back of the couch and Hero crawled across Lena’s lap to greet her. “How was your day?”

 

“It sucked. What about yours?”

 

“Really good actually. Very productive,” she said.

 

“You’re such a suck up,” she teased. “I achieved a new high score in Tetris.”

 

“Oh, good to see that you’re working hard to protect the country.” Kara scoffed.

 

“Well, when you put it like that it doesn’t seem as impressive.” She grumbled and Lena giggled. “Can we have a proper date night, tonight?”

 

“I can’t tonight, I have to go back to base.”  

 

“What? Why?” She really didn’t want Lena to go, the closer she was, the stronger their hold over her. She’d have to move up her schedule, she’d planned to have a fun date night and then try to talk to her about everything.

 

“It’s just a check in, make sure I’m still alive, still on task sort of thing,” she shrugged, “I’ll be back in a few days.” Deep down she was slightly worried because this time she would have to tell Talia that Kara had refused and she was unsure of how she would react.

 

“Why can’t they just call?”  

 

“Well, they might brief me for another mission.” Lena suggested.

 

“So, you’ll potentially be gone for longer than a few days?” Kara pried.

 

“What’s wrong?” Lena frowned.

 

“Nothing, I just… I don’t like it when you leave.” Kara mumbled.

 

“Darling,” Lena kissed the side of her head. “I always come back, don’t I?”

 

“When do you leave?” She pouted.

 

“Soon.” Kara whined, “I have to start packing.” She whined again, Lena stood up and cupped her cheeks, kissing Kara deeply. “It’ll be okay.”

 

Kara followed her up the stairs and sat on the bed, Lena started packing her bag. “Why are you packing everything? You don’t need this many t-shirts.” She complained.

 

“I’m just taking everything so I can swap out some clothes.” Kara waited for her to turn around and then launched the pile of t-shirts into the bathroom.

 

“You should bring all your clothes here,” she suggested.

 

“Not enough closet space.” Lena said, grabbing her underwear.

 

“I’ll buy a bigger one.” Lena turned and eyed her warily. “What?”

 

“You’re being weird.” She dumped everything in her bag and turned around again. Kara immediately grabbed them and shoved them under her pillow, Lena whipped around and Kara casually flopped back onto the pillow and shot her a smile. “What are you up to?”

 

“Nothing.” Kara stood up and swept her up in a hug, “I don’t want you to go.” She mumbled into her neck.

 

“I don’t want to go either, but I won’t be gone for long, I promise.” Lena held her tight and stroked her hair, “me and you, remember?”

 

“Me and you.”

 

“Against the world.” Lena finished, kissing her on the neck. Kara nodded and sat on the edge of the bed fiddling with her t-shirt. Lena tossed her pants into her bag, Kara swiped them and slid them under the bed. She then threw her socks at Kara so she could put them in her bag and Kara, launched them off the balcony one by one.

 

Lena ended up with absolutely nothing in her bag.

 

“All packed?”

 

“I think so,” Lena said. “Oh, I need to get some stuff from the bathroom.” Kara internally freaked out, she spun her around and kissed her passionately, pushing her up against the closet door. Lena’s gasp, shortly turned into a moan and she melted into the kiss.

 

Kara sucked her bottom lip and bit down, Lena groaned and Kara slipped her tongue into her mouth. “Kara,” she gasped, “I have to go.” Lena made a weak attempt at pushing her away, Kara lifted her and carried her over to the bed. “Kara,” she whined.

 

Kara grinned, capturing her bottom lip and tugging it between her perfect teeth. Lena gave in, looping her arm around her neck and pulling her deeper.

 

Just as things were getting interesting, Hero came bounding up the stairs with a pair of socks in his mouth. He jumped onto the bed, delighted with the new game Kara had unintentionally created.

 

Lena broke the kiss to look at what he’d found, “Hero, where did you get these from?” He barked happily, wagging his tail. Lena grabbed her bag and slowly turned her head towards a sheepish looking Kara. “I knew you were up to something!”

 

“Why do you always rat me out!” Kara aimed towards her dog.

 

“Don’t blame him! Where is all my stuff?” She glared intensely at Kara.

 

“Um,” she squirmed. “I may have hid it all over the apartment.” Kara looked down at her hands.

 

“Go and get all of it, now.” Kara would have normally froze at the look she was giving her but, she had never moved so fast in her life. Lena had managed to get her shirt and pants off during their make-out session, which meant she had a great view of Kara scurrying around in just her underwear. “You can re-fold it all and pack it again.” Lena said, her eyes were hard and unforgiving, her lips formed a thin line. Kara swallowed and nodded.

 

Kara gathered all of her clothes and re-folded every item perfectly, she placed it neatly in her bag, “thank god, I hate packing.” Lena said from where she was laid on the bed.

 

“What?”

 

“You didn’t think I’d notice that there was nothing in my bag?” She raised an eyebrow, knowingly.

 

“You- you…” she pointed at her, “with the… the-” she gestured to her own eyebrows. “I… What?!” Lena laughed. “Right!” Kara zipped up the bag and threw it off the bed. She crawled back on the bed and grabbed hold of Lena’s ankles pulling her down, “you owe me.”

 

__________

 

Lena was all packed and ready to go. It was now or never for Kara. “Can I talk to you before you leave?” Kara took her hand.

 

Lena knew exactly what she was trying to do. “Please don’t, Kara.” She begged, squeezing her eyes shut. They just had a perfect evening together, why did she want to ruin it? Kara cupped her face and connected their foreheads.

 

“I know it’s hard to hear. I know you don’t want to believe it, but they’re lying to you. They’ve been lying the whole time.” She said.

 

Lena turned her face away. “Stop,” she whispered.

 

Kara pressed her lips against her ear, “baby, I wouldn’t lie to you about this.” Lena shook her head. “I need to show you something,” Kara squeezed her shoulders. “Look at me, please.” Lena’s eyes darted over for a second, “will you wait here?” She gave a small nod and Kara kissed her cheek, jaw and beneath her ear. “Thank you, thank you, thank you. I’ll be right back.”

 

Kara ran up the stairs to grab the copy she’d made of Lena’s file. When she came back down, the door was wide open and Lena was gone. She sighed and collapsed back onto the couch.

 

LL: I’m sorry. I love you, but I don’t believe it.

LL: I’ll be back soon.

 

If you come back at all. Kara had only one option left and it wasn’t going to be pretty.

 

__________

 

Lena got back to HQ, dumped her stuff in her room and went straight to Talia’s office. “Little Spider, it’s been a while.” Lena smiled. “So, I’m itching to hear how you’re getting on?”

 

“I offered Kara the job and she declined,” Talia looked deflated and then she looked royally pissed off. “She said, she’d rather stay at the CIA and see what information she could gather.” Talia looked up.

 

“Intriguing.” She hummed, “so, what have you learned so far?”

 

“They’re looking into a string of kidnappings,” Talia frowned.

 

“Oversees, I’m guessing?”

 

“Domestic, dating back twenty-eight years.” Lena watched her reaction.

 

“That doesn’t seem like something the CIA would be interested in? The FBI, I’d understand, but the CIA deal with threats to national security.” Lena nodded, well that confirmed it, Kara had been lied to.

 

“It seems like Kara may be feeding you false information,” Talia leaned back in her chair, she could see the cogs turning in Lena’s mind.

 

“I think the CIA have twigged that she knows they ordered her parents death, I’ve tried to get her to leave but she doesn’t know they’re trying to sabotage her.” It all made sense now, Kara’s attitude towards her job had clearly changed since Lena had told her the truth and the CIA must have figured it out.

 

“They’re clearly not as dumb as they seem. You need to convince her to leave that place, or they will end up destroying her and if they find out about you, they’ll end up targeting you as well.” Lena nodded.

 

“I can do it.” Sometimes, all she needs is to talk to Talia and everything becomes clearer.

 

“Good. Now, I want you to get a full medical check up before you leave.” Lena confirmed, she stood up and paused for a second.

 

“Hey, can I ask you something?” Talia nodded.

 

“I know we’re not supposed to ask, but I wanted to hear my story again.” Lena looked down and up again, widening her eyes the way she did as a child.

 

“Okay, Little One, sit down.” Lena smiled and sat back down. “So, it was an awful night, the thunder was so loud it shook the windows of the nursery, which is not great when you have twenty-nine sleeping babies.” Lena chuckled lightly, “I got a call from a nun who was staying at the church to make sure that no damage was caused by the storm. She told me that a baby was left abandoned on the doorstep.”

 

“They knew that we adopted children, I was a little apprehensive, it was a really cold night, okay. But, something told me I had to go. When I got there, you were screaming louder than the sound of the thunder-”

 

“No, I wasn’t.”

 

“You were. Seriously, it was impressive. You were so small, like teeny tiny small and you were almost blue. The blanket you were wrapped in was soaked. We dried you and I held you close to warm you up, eventually you stopped crying. I carried you back to the nursery and kept a close eye on you.” Lena smiled.

 

“We gave you the last name Luthor because of the Lutheran church I got you from. So, you were baby girl Luthor for a while and you required a lot of attention. Every night for almost a week, I laid you on my chest and read to you. Every time, I said the main characters name you kicked your legs and made this soft, cooing noise. That’s how you decided your name would be Lena Luthor and you’re probably the only child here who has chosen their own name.” Lena let out a breathy laugh.

 

“Do you still have the book?” Lena asked.

 

“The Crowned Beauty?” She nodded. “Yeah, I have a copy in my quarters, I’ll get it to you before you leave.”

 

“Thank you, I think I’d like to read about my namesake.” Talia nodded and Lena left to get checked out.

 

__________

 

Rhea hurried down the corridor and entered Talia’s office, “have you seen it?” She gasped.

 

Talia didn’t look up from her tablet, “see what?” She finally looked up, a disapproving look on her face.

 

“I’m sorry to barge in, but you need to look at the news outlets in America right now.” She urged. Talia immediately brought up the news and skimmed the breaking news article.

 

Federal agent reveals that the FBI and Interpol have set up a unique task force to investigate multiple kidnappings dating back almost three decades…

Investigators believe that some of them may still be alive…

All of the baby girls were snatched just days after they were born…

Cases include: Samantha Arias, Joanna Malone, Andrea Rojas, Pamela Isley and Julia Freeman.

“Shit.” Talia said. “We need to contain this: gather all the staff we have here, call every active and sleeper agent back and get Lena in here!” Rhea nodded and marched out of the office. “Well played, Danvers.” She hummed.

 

__________

 

Lena was half way through her check up when all the staff disappeared from the room. She thought it was a little strange, but she waited, swinging her legs back and forth.

 

Her phone started vibrating. “Hey Sammy, to what do I owe this pleasure?”

 

“Lena, what’s going on?” She choked out.

 

Lena frowned, “Sam? Are you okay? What’s wrong?” When it came to Sam, Lena was incredibly protective. She hated to see her upset.

 

“I sent you a link,” she gasped. Lena opened the message and quickly skimmed the article, Sam sobbed in the background. She reached the end and her blood ran cold, she knew exactly where this had come from.

 

“Sam, it’s okay. It’s a lie, it’s not true. Someone is doing this out of spite.”

 

“How did they get my name?”

 

“The adoption records, we must all have some kind of record.” Lena reassured her, “don’t believe it. We know what’s real, we lived it, we know the truth.” She heard Sam take a shaky breath.

 

“I know. I know what’s real. I just got a little overwhelmed. It’s just… you were asking all those questions and… I was afraid you knew about it.” Sam was still struggling to get her words out.

 

“Oh, I know where it came from and don’t worry, I’m going to fix it.” She promised. Rhea came barging into the medbay a second later, “Sam, I gotta go. I’ll sort this.”

 

“Talia wants to see you.” Lena swallowed hard but followed her.

Lena took a few deep breaths and listened to the phone ring.

 

“Hey, babe! I didn’t think I’d hear from you for a while!” Lena clenched her fists and thought about what she was going to say. “Babe?”

“What did you do, Kara?” She said lowly.

 

“What do you mean?”

“Don’t even try to pretend, just tell me the truth.” The line went deathly silent.

 

“I didn’t have a choice, you wouldn’t listen to me!” Kara tried to defend herself.

 

“So, you thought the best thing to do was to leak information to the press?” Lena accused.

 

“I didn’t know what else to do.” She whispered. “I’m sorry.”

“You don’t understand the damage you’ve caused, do you? Do you know how much trouble I’m in? How-”

 

“Are you okay?!” She asked urgently. “Do you need me to come get you?”

Lena growled, “you don’t get it! I’m not a damsel in a tower, I don’t need to be rescued! I don’t need you to save me.” She spat. “Do you realise that there is now a target on your back?” She was done listening to Kara trying to push this narrative on her.

 

“I don’t care, I can handle myself. What I can’t handle, is you pretending this isn’t real. I get that you’re in denial, but you need to wake up!” Kara was desperately to get through to her. “Are you coming back?”

“I don’t know.”

 

“I love you and I’m sorry.” Kara sounded defeated. “You’ll always have a place here.”

 

Lena hung up the phone.

 

“She’s really hung up on you.” Talia said, clearly impressed. “You’ve done a good job with that one.”

 

“Of course, I’ve got her wrapped around my little finger,” she smirked devilishly.  

 

“So, we’re all agreed?” Talia said, looking between Rhea and Lena, they both nodded.

 

“Kara Danvers threatened the structure of this entire organisation.” Rhea said. “She has to die.”

 

“Do you accept this mission, Little Spider?” Talia looked at her, her intense gaze burrowing into her.

 

“Let me see, she manipulated me, lied to me and tried to destroy my family.” Lena narrowed her eyes. “Oh yeah, and I’ll make her suffer.” There was a darkness in Lena that Talia hadn’t seen in a while, not since Lena had been sent to assassinate Kara Zor-El.

 

Her Lena was back.
