Warnings: brief mentions of implied suicide

The night was dark and cold, rain cascaded down, ricocheting off the pavement before her. Lena pulled her hood over her head, her body was numb and she didn’t know whether it was from the cold or the situation she was about to face. She stared at the window, waiting, contemplating, there was still anger stewing in the pit of her stomach.

 

“Go over your orders, Little Spider.” Talia’s low voice filled her ear.

 

“Kill Kara Danvers.” Lena replied simply.

 

“Good, now follow through with the final preparations and check in within eighteen hours. If you fail to do so, you are on your own. If you are captured, you are on your own. If you are killed you will be buried in an unmarked grave. Do you understand these terms as I read them to you?” Talia said.

 

“I do.” Lena was tired of being treated like she was expendable, she was a human being.

 

“Good luck, Little Spider, may you go forth and conquer,”

 

“Endure and thrive” Lena finished. The line clicked and she was on her own, as always.

 

Lena had thought about nothing but the mission since she left Talia’s office. She had made her decision and she shuddered at the thought of the consequences.

 

The water was just beginning to seep through the last layer of her clothing when the light switched on.

 

Time to go to work.

Lena pulled out her gun and checked the clip before loading one in the chamber, she tucked it into her waistband and crossed the street. Lena climbed the fire escape, the rain crashing down disguised the sound of her footsteps; she was usually especially heavy-footed to alert Hero, but now she was aiming for subtlety.

 

She paused, thinking about whether this was something she truly wanted to do. Whether there was any other option.

 

She climbed through the window and dropped to the floor. Hero’s head shot up and he scampered out of his basket to greet her, wagging his tail incessantly. “Hey, buddy,” she said softly.

 

Kara emerged from the kitchen, a clear look of surprise on her face. Lena stood slowly and pushed her hood down, drops of rain trailing down her face. Kara looked hesitant at first, but then she strode over, “I know you probably hate me, but I need to do this.” She wrapped her arms around Lena and squeezed tightly. “I thought I’d never see you again,” she breathed.

 

Lena breathed her in, Kara’s warm, spicy scent comforted her way more than it should have. Kara let her go and gave her that soft smile, “you’re soaking wet, what have I told you about this jacket?” She let out a small chuckle, but Lena just looked at her, her eyes were cold and dark.

 

“I’m sorry, Lena. I’m so so sorry, I just- I thought …” Kara looked down and shook her head, “I’m just really sorry.” The corners of her mouth turned down, “I know I made a huge mistake and I’m so sorry.” She frowned when Lena didn’t respond. “Please, say something.” Kara’s voice wobbled.

 

“I’m listening.” Lena finally said.

 

“Really?” Lena nodded.

 

“But.” She narrowed her eyes, “if you ever use my personal relationships against me again, I will walk straight out of that door and you will never see me again.” Kara looked down, ashamed with the way she’d used Sam.

 

“I’m sorry, I was desperate to get your attention and I didn’t do it in the right way.”

 

“I understand why you did it, but don’t ever use Sam like that again.” Kara nodded, “go get whatever you have to show me.”  

 

Kara scrambled to get her bearings, she hadn’t thought Lena would ever hear her out especially, after what she’d done. “Um, okay. Give me a minute, um, do you want to change into something less… drippy?” She smiled, looking at the small puddle forming at Lena’s feet.

 

Kara grabbed Lena’s file from her desk and waited on the couch.

 

Lena grabbed some clothes from the closet and went to get changed. She stared at herself in the bathroom mirror, she splashed some water on her face and took a deep breath. She wasn’t ready to accept it, but she needed to figure out what the truth was and she was running out of time.

 

Lena came down the stairs a few moments later, she looked soft and small in Kara’s clothes; well, she’d taken everything she owned with her.

 

Lena sat down next to her and clasped her hands together. “This it?” She asked, looking at the file on the coffee table.

 

“Yeah, um, I’ll… talk you through it?” Lena gestured for her to go ahead. Kara swallowed and opened the dossier. “So, this is a picture of your hospital bracelet, it has your last name, how much you weighed when you were born and your date of birth… which is October 24th 1993.” Kara paused and watched her reaction, Lena didn’t even look at the picture she just stared at Kara. “This was one of the only leads the police had, they found it a few days after you were taken. It had been cut off and discarded in a wooded area a mile or so away from the hospital.”

 

“Um, this was the article that first captured our attention,” Kara read it out loud, looking up occasionally, Lena showed no emotion she just continued to look at Kara. “T-this article was published on October 28th 1993, it was the first time that your name was announced to the public. It also happens to be your Name Day… but, you know that obviously.” Kara couldn’t figure out what Lena was thinking and it was starting to make her feel uncomfortable.

 

“They referred to a doctor in the article. She was a locum who arrived a couple of days after you were born and she left two days after the article was published. A female locum appeared at every hospital where a baby girl was taken and she was always assigned to the parents of the baby.” Kara didn’t even want to look up at her, she thought this would illicit some kind of reaction, but now she was afraid that her Lena was gone, replaced with a cold, robotic machine.

 

“Um, this…” She looked up into Lena’s intense gaze, “this is the missing person’s report that your mother filed after you were taken. The police struggled to find any leads after they found your hospital bracelet…” Kara trailed off, Lena leant forward and Kara recoiled slightly.

 

“Um, I also found a web-”

 

“You know, I’ve been able to tell when you’re lying since the first day we met?” Lena finally said.

 

“W-what?”

 

“You have a really obvious tell.” She said, bluntly.

 

“No, I don’t!” Her right eye twitched subconsciously, it was small but, as always, Lena caught it. She gave Kara a small, genuine smile and Kara felt her stomach flip. “How did you know?”  

 

“I realised that I couldn’t tell if they were lying or telling the truth.” Lena looked down at her hands. “I asked my boss to tell me the story of where I came from and how I got my name. Every time I’ve asked before, she’s told me how I was abandoned at a church and the pastor called her to come pick me up. This time, she told me that it was a nun that called, to me that’s a pretty significant detail to get wrong, or deliberately change. I knew then, that she had always been lying. The whole thing was one big, elaborate lie.” Kara inched closer to her, she reached out and took her hand.

 

“I knew from the beginning that you were telling the truth, but I figured the CIA were pulling your strings. I didn’t want to believe it was true. I could accept what happened to me because I thought it was meant to be. I thought I had to repay these people for raising me, giving me a life and a purpose. Now I know my whole life was a lie and I don’t have a real place in the world, I’m just a puppet.”

 

“No, no, no.” Kara said, she moved until she could gather Lena in her arms. “You are no one’s puppet and you will always have a place here, you know that… We’re a family, you, me and Hero.” Lena let out a weak laugh. Kara cupped her face and kissed the side of her head. “I have one more thing that I have to show you.” Kara pulled out a thick wad of paper and set it in front of her.

 

“Your mother, Lillian, was blocked from mentioning your name online. It seems you get your smarts from her because she set up her own website and… she wrote to you, almost every day.” Lena’s eyes widened, “she never gave up on you.”

 

“What- um… what do they say?” Lena wiped her eyes.

 

“I think you should read them,” Kara whispered. “I know you hate emotions and stuff, so I’m gonna go out, get some food and leave you to it.” Kara kissed her forehead and got up to leave.

 

Lena waited until she heard the lock click, her hand ghosted over the booklet.

 

She took a deep breath and picked it up.

 

Lena,

My therapist suggested that I write all my feelings about what happened in a letter to you. It was supposed to help me “move on”, I stopped going after he used that term. But, I liked the idea of writing to you and hopefully one day you’ll understand that I never stopped thinking about you.

So, it may have got a little out of control, I think I was supposed to write one letter and I ended up writing letters for over twenty years, I used this as my personal journal. It may be a little excessive, but I wanted you to know that I never forgot and you always had a place in my life.

I thought I would post my writings on this website in the hopes that they would find you one day.

All my love,

Mom

 

Lena could already feel the emotions that were stirring inside of her, she didn’t want to put herself through this but she knew this would be her one and only chance to learn about her real mother. Hero sensed her uncertainty and climbed onto the couch next to her, crawling into her lap. She carded her fingers through his fur and turned the page.

My darling Lena,

When I first found out I was pregnant, I was terrified: I was a sixteen-year-old girl and I was afraid that this one mistake would ruin my life. Soon, that feeling grew into the most intense feeling of love I have ever experienced. My parents tried to convince me that I couldn’t handle a baby, that I would mess it up and I would have no future.

To this day, nothing has brought me the same level of happiness that I felt when I saw you for the first time, you were my best mistake and my greatest achievement.  

 

I was only allowed to hold you for a few minutes because you were so small, the nurses had to take you away to make sure that you were okay. But, I remember the first time you opened your eyes, they were so full of light and life and I knew from that moment that I would do anything for you. I made a promise that I would always protect you, and I failed.

Every day I wish I could go back to that day and fight to hold onto you, I wouldn’t have let them take you from me again. We were robbed of so many moments, so many milestones: your first laugh, your first word, your first steps. I missed it all.

I was encouraged to move on, forget all about you and start a new life. That was never an option for me. I may have started a new life, but I always imagined how you would fit in, what you would be doing if you were there, what you’re doing now.

Whatever you’ve done, whoever you have become, I know I will be proud.

My sweet baby girl, as time goes on, I can’t always remember what you looked like, but I will always remember those beautiful eyes: so innocent and full of hope.

I will never stop looking for you.

All my love,

Your Mother

 

Lena tried to bite back her tears, this was the first of many and she was already afraid that she wouldn’t be able to make it the whole way through. Fortunately, they weren’t all that emotional.

 

My darling Lena,

Sometimes, when I’m having a bad day, I like to talk things through out loud and I imagine what you would say to me… is that weird? Oh, who cares you’re always on my side anyway.

All my love,

Your Mother

She enjoyed that one, it made her chuckle.

 

My darling Lena,

I’ve decided to go to college to study law! I’m telling you first because once I do, I won’t change my mind. I’m scared and nervous and excited all rolled into one, but I want to make a better life for myself, for us. I want everything to be perfect for when you come home.

I’m going to do it. I’m going to apply.

All my love,

Your Mother

 

Lena read all about her experience at college, the ups and downs, the laughs, the late night study sessions, every time she almost quit. Lena felt like she lived it all with her.

 

My darling Lena,

I have my first interview at a law firm today. I’m nervous, but if the last seven years have taught me anything, it’s that I need to have confidence in myself. I’m a damn good lawyer, hell they’d be lucky to have me!

All my love,

Your Mother

P.S. I got the job!!!

Lena grinned and felt her chest swell with pride, she may have missed out on a life with her real family, but reading through these letters made her feel like she was apart of it all.

My darling Lena,

 

So, we had a new guy join the firm today, his name is Lionel and he took my coffee mug.

 

I hate him.

For starters, he’s arrogant, he’s got this smug smile and nothing to back it up with. Seriously, the guy is an idiot.

Don’t worry, I’ll keep you up to date.

 

All my love,

Your Mother

My darling Lena,

I put salt in my coffee mug because Lionel keeps using it. Watching him spit out his drink during a board meeting was incredibly satisfying and worth the loss of my favourite mug.

All my love,

Your Mother

Lena read through every single letter, they weren’t always long and detailed, sometimes they weren’t about anything at all. But, every single letter was there to make Lena feel involved, to remind her that her mother never stopped thinking about her.

 

My darling Lena,

I hope you’re having a good day.

All my love,

Your Mother

My darling Lena,

So, Lionel and I were sent out on a business meeting today, some company tried to sue one of our clients, it was a whole thing. Anyway, we got sent out to smooth things over and this guy almost lost the whole case for us because he didn’t do his research! I had to save his ass, again. God, he infuriates me!

I’m writing this at my desk because I just needed to get it all out and you’re a great listener!

All my love,

Your Mother

Lena smiled softly, it reminded her of the way her relationship with Kara began… except there were definitely stronger feelings of hatred… and a lot more violence.

 

My darling Lena,

Lionel broke my coffee mug… I hate him. I hope you’re having a better day than me.

All my love,

Your Mother

My darling Lena,

Soooo, Lionel bought me a new coffee mug… I like it better than my old one. Don’t worry I didn’t tell him that, I’m not dumb. He also bought me flowers to say sorry and asked me out to dinner tonight.

Why do I feel like a giddy schoolgirl with a crush?

All my love,

Your Mother

Lena learnt all about how they fell in love and the romantic way in which Lionel proposed in Paris.

 

My darling Lena,

Not a day goes by where I don’t think about you. I miss you every day. No one knows that I write these letters to you, I don’t think anyone could really understand unless they’ve been through the same thing, but I know that you are alive. It sounds crazy, but I can feel it, call it mother’s intuition.

I know you’re out there somewhere and I still believe that some day I’ll find you again.

 

All my love,

Your Mother

 

Then there were letters like these, times when she could feel her mother’s pain, where she had nothing else to say but how much she missed her daughter, even after twenty-eight years. It was heartbreaking. While Lillian had been living with this since the day her baby was taken, Lena was experiencing it all in one go. The grief and the heartache crashed over her and if she hadn’t been able to feel the warmth and the love from her mother’s words, she was sure it would have broken her.

 

My darling Lena,

Today is my wedding day. Wow, that feels  weird to say. I wish you were here, sweetheart. I think you’d like Lionel, he’s smart, funny, caring. I mean the only downside is he’s a huge Star Wars nerd, seriously what is it with those films?

Honestly, he’s a good man and I like to think you’d like him as well.

I was nervous when I woke up this morning and then the concierge dropped off a package. Lionel sent me a bracelet engraved with your name: even if you’re not here physically, you’ll still be with me today and always. Suddenly, the nerves disappeared and I knew I made the right choice.

I won’t bore you with the details now, I’ll wait to bore you in person.

All my love,

Your Mother

 

She had a whole new life now and yet, she still thought about Lena.

 

My darling Lena,

Happy 18 th  Birthday Sweetheart!

I hope today is filled with love, laughter and chaos. I hope it’s everything you ever dreamed off.

I used to imagine how we would celebrate your big day. I used to imagine that we would have a birthday tradition, something cheesy and cliché: like I would make your favourite dinner… and ruin it because I can’t cook. We would end up ordering pizza and watching your favourite film, maybe go out for ice-cream.

I’d imagine that on this particular day, we’d argue about it, you’d say you’re too old for it. I’d argue that it’s our tradition. I’d give anything to even be able to argue about these things with you.

Today is not a sad day, today is a day of celebration as you are welcomed into adulthood. You get to choose what you will be and I’m sure that it will be something extraordinary!

Enjoy your big day and I will make sure to have a huge slice of cake along with you!

All my love,

Your Mother

 

Every birthday, every Christmas, every main event that Lena missed, Lillian remembered.

 

She read through every single letter, through her blurry vision, wiping her eyes every so often. She waited a few minutes after she finished the final letter, trying to compose herself.

 

LL: You can come in now.

 

Kara opened the door and crept inside, “she really wanted me.” Lena whispered.

 

“She still wants you.” Kara corrected. Lena brought her fist up to her mouth and bit down on her knuckles, tears threatening to spill down her cheeks. “Oh, babe.” Kara hurried over and placed the pizza boxes on the coffee table before she gathered Lena in her arms.

 

“She hates Star Wars too,” Lena took a shaky breath.

 

“I know,” Kara cooed. “It’s okay, I can forgive the poor taste of your family.” Lena let out a small chuckle.

 

“I don’t know why I’m crying, I don’t even know this woman.” Lena heaved through gulps of air, but she couldn’t regain her composure. Her throat burned as she tried to force down the tears, she held her breath attempting to stop the hiccuping and grasp control of her breathing.

 

This isn’t my life. No matter how badly she wanted it, this wasn’t her life and not every story needs a happy ending.

 

“Stop it.” Kara squeezed her sides and Lena took a breath. “Of course you know her, you just read about her entire life. Your Mom wrote to you almost every single day, somehow she managed to include you in every moment of her life.” Lena’s eyes stung and she clenched her jaw, swallowing hard.

 

“Stop.” Kara said, she brought her thumbs up to massage Lena’s jaw until it loosened. “it’s okay to feel something, there’s still strength in emotion, it doesn’t make you weak.” Kara swept her up and held her tight, Lena curled up in her lap, making herself as small as possible. “I’ve got you.”

 

“Even after all this time, she still hasn’t lost hope.” Lena had lost all hope, only she knew how tonight would end and this just served to remind her what she truly was. Someone else’s property.

 

“Well, that’s a mother’s love, it’s powerful, infinite and unconditional.” Just like my love for you. 

 

__________

 

“You didn’t have to wait outside,” Lena said, throwing her crust back in the box.

 

“I didn’t want to barge in.”

 

“I appreciate it, but you do know that you actually live here?”

 

“You live here too,” Kara shrugged, “and this is your safe space.” Lena stopped, she couldn’t even come up with a response to that.

 

“My mother… she said she was proud of me.” Kara took a bite of pizza and waited for her to continue. “If she knew who I really was, she wouldn’t be proud of me.”

 

“Of course she would, you’ve survived so much-”

 

“Think back to when we first met and you didn’t know me, if I’d told you everything I’d done, would you be proud?” Lena asked.

 

“That was a completely different situation, this doesn’t compare to that. I’m proud of you every day and she will be too.” Kara said.

 

Lena stayed silent, the heavy weight of the inevitable sitting on her chest, bubbling in the pit of her stomach. “So, now you know everything… and you hate your job and I hate my job, what’s the plan?” Kara said, changing the subject quickly.

 

“Haven’t thought of one,” she said, mindlessly picking at the pepperoni.

 

“Well, I have.” Lena looked over, “I had a lot of time to kill sitting out there.” Kara gestured to the door.

 

“Tell me.”

 

“We pack up the car and go.” Kara said simply.

 

“Wow, and that took you almost two hours?” Lena teased.

 

“No, shut up. There’s… more.” Kara said, staring at her pizza.

 

“Go on,” Lena prompted.

 

“You’ll make fun of me.” Kara looked down and shovelled the whole slice into her mouth, cheeks stuffed and yet there was still a look of sadness on her face.

 

“I’m sorry, I won’t make jokes. I’ll just sit and listen.” Lena promised, “please?”

 

Kara chewed quickly and swallowed, she sat up properly. “Um, so, we pack up the car and get out of here, just keep driving, no plan, no destination, just us and Hero. At some point, when the trail goes cold, we’d head oversees.” Lena lost all interest in her food, completely invested in Kara’s world.

 

“I thought about the house we’d live in: something rustic, made of stone and solid oak, a wall of glass so that we can admire the view. We’d get rid of the planters and the flower beds of course. Replace them with a vegetable patch, I guess. You could grow all that gross stuff you like to eat.”

 

Lena smiled, Kara had brought home flowers one day when Lena was upset and she’d recoiled at the sight of them. In fact, Kara swore that she almost burst into tears. Kara had panicked at first, but then Lena explained her reaction and it gave her an idea; she grabbed Lena’s hand and Hero’s lead and dragged them out of the door. When Kara gave the bunch of daffodils to the little old lady who fed the birds, Lena almost cried happy tears at the smile it put on her face.

 

“We’d live somewhere secluded, no one knows who we are, where we came from. Somewhere in the mountains, Scandinavia might be nice, Northern Lights on our doorstep.”

 

“Yeah?”

 

“Uh huh, we would be Kara and Lena Erikson.” Kara said.

 

“We’d be married?” She asked, surprise in her voice.

 

“Yeah, obviously I would get the fake ID and the visa because… hello,” she gestured to her face, “blonde hair, blue eyes, duh.” Lena nodded, smile etched on her face. “I’d easily pass as a native.”  

 

“Very stereotypical-”

 

“-so then I marry you out of pity and for the green card.”

 

“Ahh, of course.” Lena slapped her palm against her forehead.

 

“Obviously, they’ll be the pitter-patter of tiny feet,” Lena’s eyes widened in fear, “ducklings everywhere.” Her face split into a wide smile. “We could take Hero on walks in the woods and I’m pretty sure I could find another hot spring.” Lena giggled.

 

“It sounds perfect.”

 

“Right? Just you, me and a shit ton of baby animals. We can go right now, come on.” Kara said, she stood up and took Lena’s hand.

 

“Kara, I can’t do that, I can’t do this…” She sighed, her hand slipped away from Kara’s and she rubbed it over her face. It was time for her to destroy everything she’d worked so hard to build.

 

“What do you mean?” Kara frowned.

 

“Do you want to know the reason I’m here?” She asked. “The reason they let me go after what happened.”

 

“What is it?”

 

“I was sent here to kill you,” Kara frowned and sat back down. “But, I came here to determine who was telling the truth. And now… Kara, I’m here to say goodbye.” She tried to reach out for her but Kara shook her head.

 

“No. No, that’s not fair. You can’t- no, I’m not doing this again!” She stood and backed away from her.

 

“Kara, I don’t have a choice! If I don’t go back, they’ll just send someone else to track us down and if they fail, they’ll send someone else and so on.” Lena held out her hand and Kara stared at it warily. “You don’t understand, they have unlimited resources and they’re relentless, wherever we go they will find us.” Lena stood and moved closer to her. “My story doesn’t have a happy ending, but yours still can. You can still have the life you dreamed of-”

 

“No, I can’t. You don’t get it, I didn’t have a life before you! I can’t lose another person, I can’t lose you!” Kara’s voice wobbled and her eyes brimmed with fresh tears. “Please, Lena!” She begged.

 

“Kara, living on the run is not a life!” Lena argued.

 

“I don’t care! I want to be with you!” Lena struggled to find her words. “And you had the audacity to call me a coward,” she spat. Lena knew she didn’t mean it, Kara’s first reaction is always to attack, it’s the only way she knows how to protect herself. It’s easier to express anger and hate than to show her fear at the thought of losing her love.

 

“Please, don’t make this harder than it already is. I don’t want to end this on a fight.” Lena pleaded with her.

 

“Oh god, you’re serious aren’t you?” Kara pinched the bridge of her nose and chuckled weakly. Lena bit her lip, “you know… after everything we’ve been through, I never thought it would end like this. I never thought you’d just give up.”

 

“I’m not giving up-”

 

“Yes, you are! You said we were a team. You and me.” Hot tears rolled down her cheeks, Lena couldn’t help but follow suit, her chest tightened at the sight.

 

“Darling-”

 

“No,” Kara ground out. “I love you and that’s how I know we can find another way, because I would do anything for you.” Kara had hold of her arms, concentrating on every word, putting every ounce of energy she had into this fight. “Tell me you love me.” Kara demanded.

 

“I love you.” She said, she stepped closer to her and they were now toe to toe, she cupped Kara’s cheek. “Darling, that’s why I have to leave, to protect you.” Kara broke down. “Shh sh shh, Kara, it’s okay.” She tucked Kara’s face into her neck and held her tightly. “It will be okay.”

 

“Tell me you’re staying.” She mumbled.

 

“Kara,” she sighed.

 

Kara pulled away from her, “tell me you’re staying. That’s the only way this will ever be okay.” She wiped her cheeks, “I’m not going to let you leave. Not again.” She sniffled and grabbed her hands, “we can figure this out. I know we can.” Those piercing, blue eyes searched her face. Lena saw the pain and despair she was suffering. She gone from complete elation at seeing Lena again, to complete and utter devastation and Lena couldn’t bare to see that.

 

“Okay,” Lena whispered.

 

“Okay? Okay, as in you’re staying?” Lena nodded, Kara surged forward and kissed her. “I love you,” she mumbled against her lips.

 

“I love you too.” Lena replied. They stayed standing, holding each other until they calmed down and the tears stopped. “Everything will be okay.” She murmured, stroking her hair.

 

“We need a plan.” Kara said after a little while.

 

“I need a drink first.” Lena headed over to Kara’s makeshift bar. She grabbed two glasses and the bottle of scotch Kara had bought for her Name Day.

 

“How long do we have before you’re expected back?” Kara asked, she watched as Lena poured two glasses.

 

“Twelve hours.” She said, taking a small sip.

 

“I can get us out of the US in ten. I have a guy who can get us new identities-”

 

“What about Hero?”  

 

“He’ll be coming with us, don’t worry. I have cash stashed in a few places, it will keep us going for a while.” Kara explained, she took a gulp of her drink to settle her nerves. “Once everything has settled down, we’ll get out of the country. They won’t find us, I promise.” Lena nodded and watched as Kara finished her glass. “We need to start packing, bet you’re annoyed you took everything with you,” Lena chuckled. “It’s okay, you can have some of my stuff.”

 

“Thanks.”

 

“Um, first…” She topped up their glasses. “A toast, to our happy ending.” Kara shot her that endearing smile.

 

“To our happy ending.” Lena raised her glass, Kara finished hers in one gulp.

 

Lena neglected her own, she swallowed hard and waited.

 

“Come on,” Kara stood and immediately reached up to hold her head, “whoa, head rush.”

 

“Maybe you should sit down,” Lena said. She grabbed Kara’s hand but she resisted, pulling Lena to her feet instead.

 

“No, m’fine. Come on, we have to pack now. I can buy you more clothes later.” Kara tried to tug her away, but she felt woozy again. “What’s going on?”

 

“I’m sorry,” Lena whispered. Kara slumped against her body, Lena cradled her for a moment before laying her back on the couch.

 

“What’d you do?” Lena cupped her face.

 

“I’m so sorry,” she whispered.

 

“No. No, no, no, no, no. Lee, please.” Kara begged, quickly realising what had happened. She’d fallen for it again and tears quickly spilled down her cheeks, she knew now that it was only a matter of time. “Don’t do this,” she desperately fisted her hands in Lena’s shirt.

 

Lena squeezed her eyes shut and took a deep, shaky breath. “Kara, I love you more than I could ever put into words, you saved me, helped me figure out who I am.” Lena pressed their foreheads together. “Now it’s my turn. My turn to save you, so just let me okay? Stop being so stubborn,” she joked weakly.

 

Kara was really trying to fight it, “not like this, please. I don- I don’t want you to go.”

 

“Shhh, it’s gonna be okay. I’m going back and I’m going to refuse the mission-”

 

“No,” Kara choked.

 

“It’s okay,” she said firmly. “I know how to survive and I’ve made up my mind. I’m not gonna let anyone hurt you.” Kara’s grip weakened and Lena took her hand, “I’m gonna miss you so much.” Lena’s voice cracked, “I’m gonna miss your smile,” she brushed her thumb over her lips. “And your beautiful, blue eyes.” She looked up, but Kara’s eyes were glassy, she was desperately trying to fight the effects, but she was succumbing to the sedative. “I’ll miss having to save your ass every other week,” she let out a small chuckle.

 

“Stay.” Kara mumbled, lips forming a trembling pout, tears streaming from the corners of her eyes. She brought her hand up to brush the tears from Lena’s cheeks, still incredibly gentle even though she was clearly sluggish. “Please.”

 

Her hand dropped, she tried to say something else but it came out as a indiscernible mumble.  

 

Lena kissed her cheeks, chin, forehead, nose and finally her mouth. Her own lips trembled, “I love you.” She whispered, but Kara was already asleep.

 

Hero wandered over and licked Kara’s hand, he looked up at Lena. “Hey, buddy.” He rested his head on her lap, “will you look after her for me?” He sighed, “you’ll always be my best boy and I love you.” She kissed his head.

 

Lena gathered her things and collected the gun she’d stashed in the bathroom, she avoided looking at Kara the whole time, afraid that if she did she’d never be able to leave.

 

__________

 

Kara woke up with a pounding headache. There was a few seconds of pure bliss where she forgot about everything that happened the night before.

 

Then it all came flooding back.

 

Kara covered her face with her hands, “Lena?” She called. She was met only with silence, “Lena, please.”

 

Nothing.

 

Kara sat up and caught sight of the envelope on the coffee table.

 

My sweet, perfect Kara,

I love you, I don’t think I could ever describe just how much.

I’m sorry things had to end the way they did. I wanted nothing more than for you to be my happy ending, I don’t think that’s something I’ll ever deserve.

But, you, my darling, you deserve everything.

You know, the best part of my day was always waking up with you. I’ve never had any regrets, but I regret not telling you just how much you mean to me. Then again, we were never that good with feelings.

You have taught me that I don’t need to compromise to please other people, I can be myself. I never had that freedom: I was taught to be the blank page and to tailor the story to someone else’s desires.

Our story, will always be my favourite and I couldn’t have asked for anything more than you, my perfectly, imperfect Kara.

I know you’re angry at me and I know I hurt you, but I need to ask you for one more thing. You need to get as far away from here as possible, take Hero and go, don’t tell anyone, just go. Please.

I’m going to do whatever I can to get them to leave you alone, but I want you to get somewhere safe, start a new life.

One day, you are going to meet someone who will be able to give you everything.

I will always love you,

Lena

“I already had everything.”

 

She tilted the envelope and Lena’s necklace slid out: it was a heavy, uncomfortable, almost awkward in her palm. It was right when she bought it, perfect when Lena wore it and now, staring down at the small, silver pendent she just felt hollow. It wasn’t meant for her.

 

Kara stared down at the note, she couldn’t even cry it was as if she’d lost part of herself.

 

The best part of herself.

 

She looked over at Hero who hadn’t moved from his basket.

 

“Whaddaya say buddy, do we just let her go?” He made a soft, discontented noise. “Yeah, my thoughts exactly."

 

__________

 

Lena made it back to HQ just in time and Talia immediately called her into the office. “So, how did you do it?” Lena shuddered for a moment.

 

She placed her gun on the desk and looked Talia straight in the eye, “I can’t do it.”

 

“What?”

 

“I got there, but I just couldn’t do it, I couldn’t kill her. I refuse.” Lena swallowed hard. Talia leant back in her chair, she narrowed her eyes.

 

“What changed? You were so fired up, I saw the real Lena. My Lena.” She inspected her nails, looking unaffected.

 

Well, if I’m gonna die, I’m going out fighting.

“She told me the truth.” She said simply, "showed me what life is really supposed to be like, what my life was supposed to be like. Showed me who I can really trust.” Lena leant forward on the desk, letting her know exactly what she was implying.

 

Talia actually smiled at her.

 

“Well, well, well, you’ve become quite the insubordinate lately-”

 

“Oh, shut up! You don’t get to tell me what to do any more, I have the files of every single girl, past and present and I will release them.” Lena growled. “This whole construct will fall apart around you.”

 

Talia folded her arms and clenched her jaw, trying to figure out whether Lena was bluffing. This was the first time Lena had truly seen her look frazzled, her muscles tensed and strained. “What do you want?”

 

“I will keep my mouth shut and do whatever you ask for the rest of my life, as long as you leave Kara alone. She made a mistake, she doesn’t know what she’s messing with. She’ll leave us alone, I promise.” Lena said.

 

“What’s to stop me from killing you and then killing her?” Talia said.

 

“Even if you made up that whole story, I can see that you still care about me, you always cared about me. Please.” Lena almost begged.

 

Talia thought for a moment, she stared at the girl. Lena had always been special to her, she’d always felt drawn to her, that was why she’d picked her in the first place. She knew that Nyssa would be annoyed and Lena had a slim chance of survival, but she had a strong feeling when she looked down at the baby sleeping soundly. She’d taken a chance on her then and if it meant that Lena would stay as her valuable asset, she was willing to take a chance on her again. “Okay, Lena. You have yourself a deal.”

 

“Thank you,” Lena said, she breathed a sigh of relief, her whole body relaxing. There was a knock at the door and two agents came in.

 

“Oh, good. Thank you for being so prompt. Can you take Lena to a holding cell?” Talia ordered, she didn’t look at Lena, dialling a number on her phone. “Prep her for a reset.”

 

Lena didn’t fight it, she hadn’t negotiated her refusal into the deal. She had actually wanted a reset because Talia wouldn’t allow her to be in the same country as Kara again, let alone see her and Lena was done being a pawn in the game. If she couldn’t take the queen, she’d take herself out of the game once and for all.

 

“Rhea, it seems we still have a pest control problem, get me Huntress.” Talia said, clinical as always. Talia took a chance on Lena and that had paid off, but she wasn’t a woman who often gambled. Kara still posed a significant threat and Talia played to win, which meant that Kara still had to die.

 

“No, wait!” They took hold of her arms and hauled her up. “Do what you want to me, but please don’t hurt Kara! Please!” Talia looked at her, Lena looked like a desperate, as if she was pleading for her own life, tears filled her eyes and she tried not to let them fall. Oh, she fell in love. 

 

She held up her hand and the girls stopped struggling to control her. “Oh, Lena.” She said softly, she stood from behind her desk and cupped her chin, Lena still had a glimmer of hope left in her eyes. “If I do that, how will you learn?” Lena realised then, Talia will always be one of those cruel, heartless monsters who haunted her every waking moment

 

“No! No, please!” Lena screamed.

 

“Take her.” She waved her hand and Lena felt the needle penetrate her neck. The last thing she saw was Talia’s smug smile as she sat back down at her desk.
