24. Chapter 24

Notes for the Chapter:

Happy Friday!

Thank you all so much for the amazing support shown for this story, it really is quite unbelievable at times! I still can’t believe we made it to chapter 24…

I hope you all had a great week and I hope you enjoy the chapter!

Kara swallowed the aspirin for her headache and got in the shower, she turned the temperature down and relished in the icy water. Her body and mind were shocked into consciousness. She knew she needed to act quickly, she didn’t know long it had been since Lena had left, she didn’t know where she was or whether her plan had even worked.

 

This wasn’t the way things between them were going to end, Kara didn’t believe it. The both deserved better.

 

She switched off the water and stared at herself in the mirror, Lena’s pendant hung from her neck. It was temporary, a reminder of what she was fighting for.

 

Hero was laying on her bed, waiting for her. “Don’t worry, Hero. I’m going to bring her home, I promise.” She could see that he wasn’t happy, she stroked his ears and he wagged his tail slightly.

 

The issue Kara was having was how little Lena had actually told her about where she was from. Well, that was the point, Lena didn’t want to be found, she wanted to keep Kara as far away from her life as possible.

 

But that wasn’t an option any more.

 

Lena was all about detail and if Kara was going to pull this off she needed to think like Lena. She grabbed her notebook and went over everything she knew about Lena, any small detail that may be significant. She wrote it all down and pulled out the information that she believed would be of major significance.

 

Lena’s favourite food is perogie, Kara had done her research when she made them for her Name Day, she knew the dish had Eastern European origins. Kara’s theory was that it must be an extremely common dish where Lena was based since it was a tradition for every girl to have them on her Name Day. She would have thought that it was an odd dish to choose if they were situated out of Europe.

 

Even if she was in Eastern Europe, that was still a huge area to narrow down. Perogie is common in Hungary, Ukraine, Russia, Poland, Romania and more. Including, some parts of Central America.

 

So that was a dead end and she moved on quickly. She went down her list, researching every scrap of information she had.

 

Nothing came of it.

 

Kara’s phone buzzed on the desk J’onn J’onzz calling… Kara declined it.

 

She couldn’t even calculate how long it took Lena to get back from HQ to Virginia because she never announced that she was coming home, she just showed up at Kara’s apartment. She was so unbelievably clever and it was incredibly infuriating at times like this.

 

Lena had said she’d seen bears, wolves and moose when she was gallivanting around the forest. But, a quick google search proved fruitless, turns out lots of countries have all three of those.

 

J’onn J’onzz calling…

She was beginning to get extremely frustrated. It just proved how good Lena was at keeping her at arms length, not that she blamed her, but it would have been really nice if she’d messed up just once. Lena didn’t make mistakes and she didn’t give things away easily.

 

Kara sat back in her chair and sighed, Hero wandered over and climbed onto the chair with her. He wasn’t a lap dog in any way but try telling him that, he sat on her lap and looked at her expectantly, “I’m trying my best buddy, but I’m not as smart as her. Hell, I wouldn’t be surprised if she has me micro-chipped alongside you.” She chuckled weakly. She looped her arms around his body and he rested his head against her, it was comforting but it was also a solid reminder that their anchor was gone.

 

She wished Lena was here, she’d know exactly what to do, she’d come up with a smartass explanation and Kara would be left dumbstruck.

 

But, she wasn’t here and Kara was defeated.

 

The after effects of taking the sedative last night was catching up to her and no matter how much coffee she drank, she was still groggy and couldn’t keep her eyes open.

 

__________

 

Soft, delicate hands stroked her cheek, “I know you’re awake, darling.” Kara could hear the smile tilting her voice.

“Five more minutes?” Kara mumbled, smile ghosting her lips. She was warm and content, Lena’s body pressed up against hers.

“I wish we could stay like this forever, but you have work to do, or are you giving up?” Kara frowned.

“I’m not giving up.”

Lena’s ministrations continued, lulling Kara back to sleep. “It seems to me like you are.” Lena picked up the pendant that rested against her chest, “is this coming back to me, or is it going to simply be a token to remember me by?” She let it drop back to Kara’s chest and it felt like the thud had knocked the air from her lungs.

Kara still refused to open her eyes, allowing Lena’s smooth, husky voice to surround her. “I’m trying.”

“Are you? The Kara Danvers I know is smart, stubborn and relentless.” Kara felt the gentle press of her lips, she pulled away before Kara could kiss her back. “Open your eyes, darling.”

Kara shook her head, “I don’t want you to go.” Kara’s voice cracked.

“I miss those beautiful eyes, please my darling.” Kara could never deny Lena what she wanted.

Instead of Lena, Kara was staring up at the ceiling. Instead of warm and content, she was freezing having left the window open and there was a painful crick in her neck from her head being tilted back for so long.

 

She got up and Hero followed her to the kitchen, Kara made another pot of coffee and grabbed a heat pack for her neck. She checked her phone, seven missed calls from J’onn, Kara shrugged it off.

She sat back at her desk and got to work. It may have been a figure of her own subconscious, but dream Lena was right, she wasn’t trying hard enough and if the real Lena was here she wouldn’t dare give Kara the right answer. No, she’d lovingly take pleasure in seeing Kara struggle to work it out herself, giving her constant encouragement and reassurance.

 

She scanned her notebook again.

 

There must be something. Think Kara.

 

The guards. They employed guards to keep the girls hidden and Lena had said that they scared visitors away, giving the mountain a haunted reputation.

 

This could be it.

 

There were hundreds of websites about haunted sites all over the world, apparently it was quite the hobby for some people. There were a few mountains that met her criteria and one that stuck out to her, locals said that they told their children the horror stories of the mountain, ghostly noises coming from the trees, Lena said the guards hid in the trees and made noises, footsteps crunching through the snow. Not to mention the three hikers who had gone missing, never to be seen again, that must have been before they started the non-violent approach.

 

It was rumoured that only wild animals were brave enough to roam those parts, which made it even more dangerous, if not its ghostly reputation, then the wolf packs and vicious bears would keep people away.

 

This was definitely the place

 

Góra Ghuli: Mountain of Ghouls.

 

Then it hit her, she knew exactly where that creepy, cult-like slogan came from. Maybe I really am an idiot.

 

****

 

Kara and her team were being transported back to base ready to shipped back out. They had been sent to The Democratic Republic of Congo to help deal with a rebel insurgency. In Kara’s opinion, it wasn’t too big of a threat and they dealt with it easily.

The sun was high in the sky, beating down on them. The heat was rancid and Kara was looking forward to nothing more than dumping all of her equipment as soon as they got back to base. She was riding shotgun, the rest of the team were in the back, “I’ve been given intel about a roadblock on the route back, so they sent a new one through.” Watson said, it was a courtesy more than anything, Kara was the commanding officer after all.

“What’s the roadblock for?” She asked, mindlessly staring out of the window.

“Just a regular stop and search, but we don’t want to be sat in that.” He said. He took a left turn away from their planned route, it was a good hour longer than the original.

Kara slid the metal hatch across, “hang in there guys, we have to take a little detour, we’ll be back soon.” There was a collective but understandable groan from the chorus in the back. “I know, I know.”

The road was bumpy and rough, these trucks were not built for comfort and the journey was painful for all those involved. Kara stared out of the window, trying to ignore the heat and the less than ideal driving conditions. They drove through what looked like an abandoned industrial complex, the country had recently relocated a lot of their industry into the larger cities, leaving empty factories and mills.

This place was virtually abandoned which is why Kara found it strange that there was a van parked outside one of the factories, “just slow down a bit, Watson.” He did as he was asked. The van was brand new, all black with tinted windows. “Is that odd to you?”

“A little.” As they cruised by, Kara just caught a glimpse of someone being dragged round to the back of the disused factory.

“Pull up over there.” Kara ordered, pointing a few meters ahead of them.

“What?”

“Just do it.” He did as he was told, Kara climbed out of the truck and rounded the back, she opened the doors and met the confused faces of the soldiers in the back. “I believe there’s a potential threat to life so gear up.”

They knew better than to argue and hopped out of the van one at a time, “Clarkey, Doc you’re with me. Hewitt and Sharpe you’ll go round the back. Kane, make sure that van goes nowhere and cover the front.” They all nodded. “Watson, keep the engine running and call it in.” He waved from the window.

The team got into formation, Kara leading from the front. They crept onto the site, Kara motioned for the van to be checked first. The surrounded the vehicle, covering any exit points. When the doors were pulled open, they found it to be empty, Kane stayed behind and Kara motioned for the rest of the team to follow her. She gestured to Hewitt and Sharpe, the pair broke away, shuffling towards the back of the building.

There was a shutter at the front of the factory that was a couple of inches off the ground. Kara stepped back, motioned for Clark to check the side doors and got down on the floor: she could see two sets off feet, one was standing and the other was sat on a chair. Kara closed her eyes, she could hear someone talking on the phone.

“Target is secured. Send the ransom demand.”

“Hostage situation is confirmed. Two people, one is female, the other is unknown. Hostage is being held on a chair in the centre of the room. Kidnapper potentially armed and to be considered extremely dangerous.” Kara relayed all the information that she had.

Clark came back from his scouting trip. “Both side doors are locked, the only exits are the front and the back.”

Kara nodded, “on my command, Clark raise the shutter, Alex cover him.” They both nodded. “On my command, Sharpe and Hewitt enter through the back.”

“Copy that.”

Kara checked her weapon, adjusted her stance slightly and took a breath. “Three… two… one. Go go go!” Clark threw open the shutter and Kara moved in.

The kidnapper looked shocked, eyes wide. “Hands in the air!” Kara yelled, she noted the gun she was clutching in her right hand. The woman froze, Kara could see her considering her options. “Hands in the air!” She repeated, Kara could hear crying, but her eyes never left the woman in front of her.

The woman raised the gun and Kara fired three shots into her chest. She fell to the floor, motionless. Alex hurried over to inspect, what Kara now realised, was a child screaming and crying. She couldn’t be much older than ten.

Sharpe found and old sheet and covered the body, “good call, Cap.” Clark said, clapping her on the back.

“Thanks.” Alex approached her next, “is she okay?”

“Yeah, no visible injuries, obviously she’s in shock. But get this, her father is Jumane Babatunde.”

“The President?” Kara frowned, Alex nodded. “Where was her security team?”

“All dead.” She murmured, they both looked down at the covered body. “Whoever she was, she was clearly a professional.”

Kara hummed, “she didn’t want to live.”

“Definitely not. It was a good call.”

Kara waited until the girl was escorted out of the building before she inspected the body: no ID, not that she expected it but she did have a small tattoo on the top of her forearm. It looked like Arabic, Kara took a picture so she could investigate it further.

Kara forgot about what happened, everything moved so quickly and there wasn’t really time to think before the team were shipped out on another assignment.

It wasn’t until a few weeks later when the kidnappers identity was finally discovered.

“Nyssa Al Ghul?!” Alex exclaimed.

Kara nodded, “uh huh, apparently so.”

“The Al Ghul’s are nasty pieces of work. Ra’s Al Ghul was the head of a huge criminal organisation but his daughters fell off the grid shortly after he died.” Alex said.

“It was believed they were both dead too, it’s been over two decades since either of them have been seen.” Kara explained.

“Well, you better hope Talia is dead, they’ve always been a vengeful family.” Kara waved her off.

“Oh, let her try.”  Kara scrolled back to the photo she took of Nyssa’s tattoo, her interest was peaked again and she had it translated.

“Endure and thrive.”

****

Kara leaned back in her chair, “well, looks like Talia Al Ghul is about to get what’s coming to her.” Hero trotted over to see what all the fuss was about, “I’ve got it buddy, I know where she is.”

 

Well, this was a slightly bizarre turn of events, but it made sense in Kara’s head and she wondered if Talia knew what she’d done. Kara was very much looking forward to driving that dagger into her heart.

 

Kara went to bed that night, fully aware of what she was facing now and with a lead as to where Lena was. Laying in bed, she read through Lena’s letter again, begging her to run and hide. Kara was no coward and if they wanted her, they would have to come and get her.

 

Little did she know, there was an assassin waiting on her doorstep

 

__________

 

Helena Bertinelli was exceptionally well trained and from what she’d been told, this particular mission was going to be simple. She’d arrived late in the evening, no real time to prepare, but she knew what she was doing and was well informed as to what she was up against.

 

Kara Danvers: ex-Marine and currently a mediocre CIA agent. Talia had been keeping tabs on her since her parents death and she had been slightly underwhelmed. Kara had been in her prime when she was a Captain in the forces: her mind was sharp, unrelenting focus, a force of pure strength, speed and her hand-to-hand was unmatched. Yet, once she’d left, she’d become lazy and arrogant, putting in minimal effort and expecting the same results she used to get. That’s why she’d lost every bout against Lena.

 

This would be simple enough, just another feather in her cap and a chance to wipe out a threat to the World Killers. Helena thrived on this kind of pressure.

 

Helena waited a couple of hours after the apartment went dark, just to make sure Kara would be asleep.

 

She made her way to the back of the building and forced the back entrance, knowing that it wasn’t covered by CCTV. She carried a collection of different knives on her belt, she would prefer her bow but it wasn’t practical for close combat. Guns were good, but too loud. Helena liked to be precise and she thought of her work as an art form.

 

She skipped up the steps towards Kara’s apartment, she easily picked the lock and made her way inside. Helena slid a four inch, serrated blade from her belt.

 

She heard a low growl and searched for the location of the dog, it barked, the door slammed behind her and her arm was twisted behind her back. The blade slipped from her hand and was suddenly pressed against her throat.

 

“This is the best you’ve got, really?” The assassin grunted lowly and struggled against the hold. ”I wouldn’t do that if I were you.” Kara said lowly.

 

Kara had put sensors on every single entrance to her building and her apartment. She was alerted as soon as the door had been forced. She had learnt from the previous assassin who broken in every other visit.

 

Kara would usually attempt to get information out of a captive, but lets face it, she wasn’t going to give anything up. She slid the knife through the belt around Helena’s waist and cut it away from her, she pushed the sharp tip into her back and Helena walked forward and sat in the armchair across from her.

 

Kara pushed the coffee table back slightly and sat opposite her. She knew it was a dangerous move, but she felt sorry for the unlucky assassin.

 

“You seem a little shocked, did you think it would be easy?” The assassin gave her nothing back. “Let me guess, I’m arrogant, self-involved and I make stupid mistakes. Granted, you can have the last one I do make stupid mistakes, but your boss has made the worst mistake by sending you.” Helena sent her a smirk. “You see I like to think of myself as a nice person, merciful even, so I’ll give you a chance to beg for your life.” Kara gave her a sweet smile.

 

It was a dangerous move, she knew it was but she didn’t really care.

 

Helena sighed and rolled her neck, Kara smiled. “My guess is that you’re not one of the regular assassins, Talia wouldn’t send someone-” Helena’s eyes widened, “-oh yeah, I worked that bit out and I know she wouldn’t send someone that I have information on, that I could potentially “corrupt” by explaining the truth about what she did. So, that makes you one  of the big four right? You put those poor girls through hell to fight for a goal that isn’t even feasible!” Kara stood up and turned around, tucking Helena’s knife into her waistband.

 

“Did you take any of them? Huh, did Talia drag you in on the plan?” She didn’t really expect an answer.

 

“Are you quite finished?” Helena drawled. She hopped up from the armchair while Kara’s back was turned and glided across the coffee table before launching herself at Kara, a knife that was hidden on her body held tight in her fist.

 

Well, I can’t say I didn’t give her a chance.

 

Kara spun, already expecting the attack. She avoided the flying punch, grabbing the assassin by her arm and using her other arm to fling her over her shoulder and onto her back. Helena grunted as she hit the hard wood floor, knife falling from her grasp.

 

“Now, that wasn’t very clever.” Kara fisted her shirt and hauled her up onto the coffee table, one-handed. Helena struggled, punches flying everywhere. “Yeah, you were one of those girls once and you betrayed each and every one of them by not telling them the truth!” Kara growled through gritted teeth.

 

“Well, I am sick and tired of everyone else getting what they want. Talia doesn’t get to win this time.” Kara pulled the knife from her waistband and drove it through her chest.

 

It was instantaneous, virtually painless.

 

She grabbed Hero and locked her apartment, she’d deal with that later.

 

__________

 

Kara dropped Hero off at the sitters that morning and headed into work, she needed to get confirmation for a few things before she moved onto the next stage of her plan, Operation: Destroy the weird assassin cult, save the children and get Lena back (not “save” because she’s not a damsel in a tower). I’m gonna have to come up with a snappier name.

 

Kara spent her day cooped up in her office, compiling a file on Talia Al Ghul and the rest of her family. The crucial piece, that may have made her squeal a little: Talia Al Ghul owned Góra Ghul, she’d inherited it from her late father. The mountain was located in the south of Poland and that was her next stop.

 

She was on her way out when, “Danvers!” J’onn called. She sighed and walked into his office. He shut the door behind her and she stood in front of his desk, “sit!” He ordered. Kara did as she told, rolling her eyes.

 

“Kara,” he sighed, “I’m suspending you, pending investigation.”

 

“What?” She exclaimed.

 

“Kara, I have tried with you and I don’t know what has been going on these past few months but this is not the Kara Danvers I know.” She was starting to get really sick of that term.

 

“I am exactly who I need to be.” She said, “at least I have integrity.” She muttered.

 

“Kara! You spoke to the press! you’ve been AWOL for the past week or so. I have no other choice. You wanna talk about integrity, I’ve been talking to Winn and I’m going to ask you this once. How long have you been involved with Lena Luthor?” That felt like a sucker-punch and suddenly she couldn’t speak. “Well, that says it all.” He laced his fingers together and leaned forward on the desk.

 

“J’onn, I know where those missing girls are.” She said.

 

“Then you can send all the information you have to the FBI before you leave.” He said, he face was unforgiving.

 

“No,” she growled. “It was our case first and, yet again, we have made more progress than they have.” Kara argued. “Talia Al Ghul is involved.” That got his attention for second.

 

“What do you want?”

 

“She owns a mountain in Poland, I’m requesting a flyover to confirm whether or not the girls are there.” She said.

 

“Talia Al Ghul is not someone I want to go toe to toe with without something concrete, so what do you have?” He asked.

 

“Well, nothing concrete but I know I’m right.” He sighed.

 

“I’m sorry, Kara but the decision is final.” She slammed her fist on the table.

 

“You want to talk about what the CIA has done to me?” J’onn leant back, he knew precisely what she was talking about. “Exactly! This whole place owes me! I’m not going to lose anyone else. So, you can file your paperwork do whatever you want, I don’t care any more!” Months of pent up frustration burst out of her. She pushed her chair back and stood, she reached for the door handle.

 

“Kara,” he called, she stopped. “It’s almost clocking out time and you know how I like to get home in time for dinner with the family, I’m not sure I’ll be able to file the paperwork today,” he picked at his sleeve nonchalantly, “it probably won’t be registered for at least another twenty-four hours. So, I guess, you have until 5pm tomorrow to get what you need.”

 

Kara turned and gave him a small smile, “thank you.”

 

“And for what it’s worth, I didn’t know about what happened to your parents until you mentioned it a few weeks ago, that part of your file was restricted when you placed on my team.”

 

Kara didn’t know whether she believed it, but she was grateful that he had given a head start.

 

“Oh… um, also, someone tried to kill me last night so there’s a dead assassin in my apartment, could you…?”

 

“I’ll get someone out as soon as possible.” He sighed.

 

“Much appreciated.”

 

Kara left the office and J’onn cracked a smile. “Now that’s Kara Danvers.”

 

__________

 

Kara basically cleaned out the armoury. She hadn’t made a plan yet so she took everything she could possibly need. She even managed to secure a jet from Virginia to Poland which was a lot quicker (and cheaper) than flying commercial.

 

She made a quick stop on the way to the airstrip, “hey buddy,” she greeted Hero who came bounding over to her. “I won’t be gone for long, I promise. When I come back, I’ll bring your favourite person and all the treats you could ever want.” She kissed his head and stroked his ears a final time before saying goodbye.

 

Poland was cold, especially in the winter, but Kara was used to harsh conditions and she was well prepared. Her access code still worked and she was able to get into one of the CIA safe houses just outside of Sanok, the small town closest to Góra Ghuli.

 

When she was in the Marines, she was good at coming up with plans but there was also always people around to bounce ideas off. This wasn’t a military mission and she was up against an unknown number of enemies. While she had background knowledge on Talia, she had no clue as to how many assassins she would face. All she had was a list of names, no background, no pictures, she didn’t even know how many of the missing girls were still alive.

 

She had to act quickly, but the plan had to be watertight.

 

If she messed this up she could potentially lose Lena.

 

Admittedly, Kara had lost a lot of confidence in herself over the past few years. She’d been by herself for so long that she was her biggest fan and her own worst enemy, she hid behind that wall of arrogance and self-importance because she didn’t want anyone to see that under the surface, she was frantically trying to keep herself afloat.

 

Kara had always believed that the best version of herself was when she was a soldier: she was courageous, strong, disciplined and capable. Right now, she was alone, scared and she had no plan. She might not have the weight of the world on her shoulders, but she was carrying the weight of her world. The only person she could rely on right now was herself and she couldn’t trust herself to come up with a simple plan.

 

While she was serving, she was apart of a team, never alone. In the CIA, even if she was alone on a mission she could always radio for support and the operations were always planned out, there were rare occasions where she had to think on her feet, but instinct always kicked in.

 

Even when she was with Lena, she relied on her quick thinking to save them both and she would cover her nerves by teasing or flirting with her so she didn’t feel so scared.

 

How was she supposed to pull this off when she didn’t even believe she could do it?

 

Kara had simply lost faith in herself.

 

It was the final round and Kara was out for the count.

 

She sat on the floor and cried, feeling completely and utterly hopeless.

 

She didn’t know how much time she’d wasted on her own pity party, but her phone lit up with a notification and Kara looked at her lockscreen, it was the picture of Lena and Hero napping on the couch. Lena never allowed her to take pictures, she said that she couldn’t risk her picture getting out. Of course Kara took a few on the sly and buried them deep in Hero’s folder on her phone. She swiped through them, Lena was never looking at the camera, but Kara always wondered if she knew.

 

Kara’s favourite was her most recent snap: Lena had just woken up, she was mid-stretch arms above her head there was a smile ghosting her lips and her sleep shirt had ridden up exposing the slightest hint of her toned stomach, dark hair stark against the white sheets, creamy thighs on display as her legs tangled in the sheets. Kara loved her so much and that photo completely shocked her back to reality.  

 

That was the reason she was here, that was what she was fighting for.

 

She’d lost sight of that for a minute, but that fire inside of her was re-ignited and blazing.

 

She got up and grabbed her journal, starting her plan of attack. She knew there must be some kind of alarm system or sensors to alert the guards that there was someone on the property, Kara just had to figure out where they were and avoid them.

 

Kara decided that the best thing she could do was use some of Lena’s detailed, tactical thinking with a Danvers twist.

 

__________

 

She waited until night fell and moved up to the base of the mountain.

 

Lena would have hacked the system and shut down the sensors, Kara bypassed all the technical stuff and knocked out the power for half the grid. She didn’t know how long she had until it was fixed or if they had a back up power supply. That was the Danvers twist, flying by the seat of her pants and with a little bit of luck.

 

This was it, she took off running up the trail, wanting to get as far up the mountain as possible tonight.

 

Kara stayed away from the road, assuming that there would be a rotation of guards soon and she didn’t want to be caught. Kara ran continuously for close to thirty minutes, she sat down and leaned against a snow bank, breathing hard. She kept as quiet as possible listening for any indication that her presence had been noticed.

 

Thankfully, she remained undetected.

 

Kara roamed the surrounding area, looking for a place to take shelter for the night. She found a small cave a few meters above the ground in the rock face. It was a little tight but that suggested that nothing else inhabited the crevice. There was a small lip that just covered the entrance which meant she was almost completely hidden, it was kind of perfect.

 

She’d only packed the essentials for her journey from the safe house to the mountain, she didn’t want to be bogged down by heavy equipment, she needed to stay undetected and so carrying multiple weapons wasn’t plausible. Pulling out her journal, as she’d done so many times when oversees, she jotted down her thoughts and feelings getting everything out. Kara went over her plan again, going through each and every point to make sure that she didn’t make any mistakes before trying to get some sleep.

 

She buried herself in her sleeping bag and stared up at the sky; she pulled Lena’s t-shirt out of her bag (completely essential) and breathed in the scent.

 

Kara kept going over things in her head, is she going to make things worse for Lena? Does Lena even want Kara to come after her? Was she even capable of pulling this off? All she seemed to do was mess things up recently. The letter Lena had left seemed final: Lena wasn’t coming back and Kara couldn’t accept it.

 

On the other hand, she knew how Lena felt about her, knew that the only reason she’d left was because she wanted Kara to be safe. Kara had a taste of what life would be like without Lena and she was miserable. She’d also had a glimpse of their future and Kara wanted it, wanted nothing but Lena.

 

She reached up and held the pendant around her neck. She couldn’t live with herself if she didn’t at least try. They saved each other, that’s just what they did.

 

Kara wrote everything down, she liked to organise her thoughts and feelings this way. It was the easiest way she’d found to process everything that ran through her head and it always settled her nerves. The conclusion she eventually came to:

 

I’m deeply, undoubtedly, irrevocably in love and I’ll do whatever it takes to get Lena back.

Kara fell asleep reasonably quickly after that, clutching Lena’s t-shirt close to her chest.

 

__________

 

Kara shook her head slightly, the hair in her face tickled her nose. Lena’s small chuckle rumbled in her chest, their bodies were pressed together in a tight hug and Kara could feel Lena’s laugh. It made her smile, “my perfect Kara,” she whispered.

“I’m not perfect,” she replied. “I’m struggling Lena.” She admitted, she felt her hand come up to the back off her neck, fingers threading through her hair and scratching her scalp softly.

“You’re doing so well, you’re so close.” Kara knew it wasn’t real and her breathing increased as she tried to cope with yet another taste of what she’d lost. “Shh, darling. You can do this, you’re stronger and smarter than you think.”  

Kara felt the sting of tears filling her eyes, an awkward lump lodged in her throat. “I believe in you, Kara.”

She felt Lena pull away, Kara tried to hold onto her but she slipped out of her grasp easily.

__________

 

She woke up early the next morning and gnawed on a protein bar, attempting to settle her stomach. The next stage of Operation: Slay the dragon lady, save the villagers, kiss the princess: (still not quite right) find their base of operations.

 

She blended in well to the surroundings, her white tactical gear perfectly matched the blanket of snow on the ground. She scurried away from her hiding spot and took cover behind a large tree, she was well aware that there were armed guards stationed in the area and they knew this place far better than she did.

 

There were no public records or maps that contained details of the mountain, Talia had kept everything well hidden. What she did know was that before Ra’s Al Ghul bought the land, the mountain was home to a World War Two military base, used to house and train soldiers. Kara knew there was no point wandering around, wasting energy looking for a building that, quite frankly, could be anywhere.

 

The base was her best bet and she needed to pinpoint the location.

 

The trees were tall and provided a lot of coverage, Kara concluded that would be the safest and most viable option for any possible reconnaissance.

 

She pulled out a length of rope and threw it over the lowest branch, seventeen feet above her. She gripped both sides and pulled herself up easily, she hauled herself up and over the branch and then reeled in the rope so it wouldn’t be noticed by any unwanted parties.

 

There were multiple thick, strong branches that gradually became thinner and weaker the higher she climbed. She distributed her weight evenly across the delicate branches, wobbling slightly, she crouched down in order to stabilise herself. She took a deep breath, tightened her core and stood, taking her hands off the supporting branch and standing up straight.

 

From the top of the tree she could see the top of what looked like a watch tower. Kara had seen enough in her time that she recognised it easily. That signalled to her that there was some kind of fortress a few miles west of where she was, well hidden in the thickness of the surrounding forest.

 

“Well there it is,” she muttered. “Now, just an entire team of guards to get past.” She took note of the coordinates and shimmied back down the tree. There was a distinctive sound in the distance of snow crunching underfoot, Kara crouched down to avoid rustling the trees too much.

 

She watched as two heavily armed guards patrolled underneath her, they were dressed in tactical snow camouflage; not dissimilar from what Kara was wearing herself carrying MP7’s. Now, she had to make a decision: take them both out now or let them go and possibly run into them later on.

 

Kara hooked her arms around the final branch and smoothly rolled over, gently lowering her body until she was hanging just above them and dropped. She landed on the first guard who collapsed to the floor with a grunt, the second immediately went to attack. Kara blocked his punch, twisted his arm behind his back and slammed his head against the tree trunk. Both were incapacitated easily.

 

Kara dragged them away from the path and rolled them down into a snow bank.

 

She continued west, padding through the snow. It was crucial that she stayed low and slow, keeping her movements light, so she could hear anyone approaching and, so she wouldn’t be heard herself.

 

Two more sets of footsteps approach, Kara flattened her back against a tree and heard the two men laughing and joking. One set of footsteps jogged away and she heard the second man clear his throat. She peaked out from her hiding place and saw that the guard was alone; she whistled lowly and heard him whip around.

 

That distinctive click of the safety being removed should have sent a shiver down her spine, but Kara wasn’t afraid any more. He slowly crept deeper into the forest. Kara waited until she saw the barrel of the gun, she stepped out driving her right elbow up to push the gun towards the sky. She then slammed her left fist into his underarm and he crumpled, his weapon fell to the floor, his body shortly after.

 

Kara hurried over to the next man who was casually relieving himself against a tree. She glided across the snow and hit the unsuspecting guard in the back of his head with her gun.

 

Her confidence grew with each and every tag team that Kara faced. She didn’t let it go to her head, she stayed calm, she wasn’t going to celebrate anything until she had Lena safe in her arms again.

 

It took the whole day and by the time Kara made it to the army base it was pitch black. She made it inside the compound relatively easily, the doors had been modified and fitted with electronic locks which weren’t working because the electricity was still out.

 

She attached a silencer to her pistol, she didn’t want to kill any of them, it wasn’t their fault that they had been forced into this life; plus there were children as young as four here somewhere. The gun was a last resort, she promised herself that she wouldn’t use it unless she had no other choice.

 

She crept along the long corridors, staying alert and listening for anything that would suggest she was about to run into trouble.

 

It was eerily empty, this was supposed to be the head quarters of a highly trained group of assassins and Kara had yet to come across anyone. That had her on high alert.

 

She continued on and opened a door at the end of the corridor, unbeknownst to her, she stumbled into the nursery: six rows of five beds. She immediately holstered her weapon and observed the room, they were all alive and well, she let out a sigh of relief.

 

“Don’t you dare touch them.” A voice growled lowly, Kara slowly turned around and met a hard stare, behind a gun pointed at her head.

 

Kara raised her hands in surrender, “I’m not here to hurt anyone.” Kara whispered. The woman cocked the gun, her grip on the weapon was strong and steady, knuckles white. “Let’s not do this here, not in front of them.”

 

“Why not? They’re gonna see it at some point.” She shrugged.

 

“They don’t have to, they could go back to their families, be normal kids.” Kara said. “Don’t let them suffer through the same thing you had to, Sam.” She knew exactly who Sam was just by her voice.

 

Kara slowly reached her hand down and slid her gun from it’s holster, Sam watched her every move closely. She held it out for Sam to take, a peace offering of sorts. Sam stepped aside and gestured for Kara to move out of the door, she kept her hands up until they were both back in the corridor.

 

“In there.” Sam nodded her head to the door down at the end of the hallway. “What the fuck are you playing at?” Sam yelled when the door was shut.

 

“Where is Lena?” Kara yelled back.

 

“You really think I’m going to tell you after what you did to her? The only reason I haven’t killed you is because you helped save my life.” They stared intensely at each other, challenging the other to break first. Sam’s eyebrows were pinched together and Kara watched the muscles of her face tense as her jaw clenched. “I suggest you leave now before I change my mind.” Sam said through gritted teeth, fighting every instinct she had to kill her.

 

“No.” Kara said firmly, jaw clenched. “I’m not leaving without Lena.”

 

“She’s not here dipshit!” Kara frowned, her mouth gaped as she tried to form a coherent response. She’d worked everything out she’d found Sam and the missing girls, this was it. It had to be the place!

 

“Wh-what? No, this has to be the right place!” She said, desperately.

 

“’Fraid not.” Sam gave her a smug look, lips pulled into a thin line. “Just go home Kara, she doesn’t want you.”

 

“Yes, she does. We love each other.” Sam scoffed and Kara looked a little shaken. Sam relished in the disheartened look, this was the woman who had broken the heart of her best friend and now she wanted to come crawling back? Over her dead body.

 

“It’s infatuation not love. Lena agrees, that’s why she’s not going back.” Sam said as if it was obvious.

 

Kara was a little taken aback, a few months ago she may have believed what Sam was saying. But, she knew Lena and she knew what they shared: a deep, unwavering love for each other. “I’m not leaving those girls here. I won’t allow them to go through the same suffering.”

 

“Quite the hero aren’t you?” Sam growled.

 

“You know I’m right.” Kara said, she could see in Sam’s eyes that she was considering what Kara was saying. She silently pleaded with Sam, she didn’t want to have to force the information onto her, she’d seen first hand how it had affected Lena.

 

“No,” She shook her head. “I know what’s real.” Kara sighed, so much for the easy way.

 

“Your name is Samantha Arias.” Kara took a step towards her. “Your birthday is June 17th 1993 and let me guess, your Name Day is June 22nd.” Sam’s grip on the gun faltered.

 

“Stop.”

 

Kara continued her advance. “Sam, you were born in Colorado, you were taken from the hospital, from your mom and dad, two days after you were born.”

 

“Stop it!” Kara slipped the gun from her hands.

 

“Your parents names are Patricia and Matthew Arias. You have a younger sister, her name is Ruby.” Kara watched as tears filled her eyes.

 

“It’s not true.” Sam whispered.

 

“It is true!” Kara yelled. “I’m not here to ruin your life Sam, I’m here to find Lena, expose Talia’s lies,” Kara pointed in the direction of the nursery, “and take those girls home. That’s it.” Kara said.

 

“I told you, Lena’s not here.” She said lowly. “I haven’t heard from her since that news article was released.” Sam sighed.

 

If Kara was to make Sam an ally, she needed to honest. “She was sent to kill me, but she refused the mission.”  Sam’s gaze hardened.

 

“Why was she sent to kill you?” Her voice was dangerously low.

 

“Because I was the one who released those names to the press.” She said, honestly. Sam lunged at her, Kara wasn’t expecting it at all and Sam’s fist slammed against her jaw.

 

“You fucking asshole!” She screamed, throwing swift kicks and hard punches. She was so fast that Kara couldn’t anticipate them at first, she just kept taking hit after hit. Kara grunted in pain, Sam’s strikes started to become sloppy, she was blinded by her tears. Kara managed to catch one of her flying fists, she spun her until her back was against Kara’s front. She held her wrists and Sam let out a gut-wrenching scream.

 

Kara stepped back until her back hit the wall and she slid down until they were both sat on the floor.

 

Sam leant forward and cried into her hands, her whole body shaking. Kara gave her the space she needed to come to terms with the information she’d just been told, Kara scooted away from her and carefully pulled her shoulders backwards until she was leaning against the wall.

 

Kara dragged the back of her hand across her face and wiped away the blood. Her nose was bleeding and her lip was split. She tilted her head back against the wall, her mouth tasted bitter and coppery.

 

Kara sat next to her, trying to stem the blood flowing from her nose. “I’m sorry,” she said softy, “I didn’t mean to upset you or hurt you, but I think you deserve the truth about where you come from.”

 

“I’m not upset about that,” she snapped. “Quite frankly, that’s the least of my concerns.” Sam said in a hushed tone, her whole demeanour shifted. She sounded heartbroken.

 

“What is it?”

 

“Lena’s already refused two assignments,” her voice was barely above a whisper. “There is no third chance Kara, she’s already as good as dead. And it’s all your fault.”

 

__________

 

Kara’s ears were ringing, the only thought running through her head, Lena’s dead and it’s all my fault.

I failed. I wasn’t good enough.

“You know, the one thing that irritated me the most about Lena-”

 

“Don’t talk about her like she’s gone.” Kara grunted. They were sat side by side, leaning against the wall and staring blankly straight ahead.  

 

“I know what she’s up against remember? I know what Talia’s like: she cruel, unforgiving and she’s a complete and utter control freak. Once she sees that conditioning slip,” Sam snapped her fingers and Kara flinched, “that girl is a write off.” The fact that Sam was able to speak so smoothly about something so callus made Kara sick to her stomach. “I never thought it would be Lena.” Her voice cracked when she said her name.

 

“You don’t know she’s de…” Kara couldn’t even say the word. “You don’t know for sure.” She whispered.

 

Kara wasn’t going to believe it. She couldn’t because Kara didn’t know how she was supposed to live without her. Her eyes welled and she covered her mouth with her hand to stop the escape of her whimpering.

 

“I hate you.” Sam said.

 

“Believe me, I hate myself more. I’ve made some… catastrophic mistakes in my life, but forcing Lena into the position between saving me or saving herself will be a mistake I will never forgive myself for.” Kara was raw and candid, it was a something that Sam hadn’t expected, she was different from the woman she’d met in Cuba.

 

“Lena would choose just about anyone over herself and that’s what I always found so frustrating…”

 

“She can’t comprehend her own worth.” Kara said, she saw Sam nod out of the corner of her eye.

 

“She always had to make the sacrificial play.” Kara rolled her neck, trying to keep her emotions in check. Sam had given up so easily, curled in on herself, utterly hopeless.

 

“No,” Kara slammed her hand against the floor and stood up. “I would know if she was gone, I would feel it.” Sam looked up, Kara had subconsciously began playing with Lena’s necklace. Sam swallowed her gasp, that was the same necklace she’d watched Lena throw away, or thought she’d watched her throw away. It was clear that the pair had reconciled and there were some genuine feelings there, was it love? She wasn’t quite sure just yet.

 

“If you want to sit here and feel sorry for yourself, that’s fine. Wait here and when Interpol storm the place you’ll finally be free. I’m going after to Talia, I’m going to tell the truth and I’m going to bring Lena home.” Kara wiped the tears from her cheeks, “so you can stay here, or you can come with me.”

 

Sam locked eyes with her and searched her face, Kara was determined, there was a fire behind those eyes. “Well, you found The Academy, Talia has called every agent back to HQ, I’m the only one left and now I know why. Lena is my best friend, my family and, on multiple occasions, my saviour,” Kara smiled and watched as Sam stood, “I’m not going to let her down now.”

 

“Every single assassin is at your HQ?”

 

“We’d need an army to get in there.” Sam said.

 

Kara smirked, “I think I can help with that.”

Imma go take a nap but let me know what you think!
