25. Chapter 25

Notes for the Chapter:

Happy Friday!

This was originally meant to be a oneshot and now we're 25 chapters in... that's crazy to me. Thank you all SO MUCH for all the support it's overwhelming and amazing!

Anyways, so here's the final chapter I really really hope you enjoy it.

Warning: there is mention of suicide, I've tried to make it as implied as possible.

When Lena eventually woke up her head was pounding, she was groggy and lethargic. She moved each one of her limbs to make sure nothing was broken. Her wrists were tied behind her back, her ankles and knees were zip-tied, she couldn’t move.

She didn’t want to move.

The last thing she remembered before she passed out was the phone call Talia had made.

Huntress was sent to kill Kara and Lena knew all about her impeccable success rate. Horrible images flashed through her mind: images of what Helena would do to her beloved Kara.

She looked around attempting to take in her surroundings, she had no idea where she was and deep down she knew there was no chance of escape.

She had no hope left.

She’d tried to outsmart Talia, tried to protect Kara but she’d failed.

She didn’t have much time to dwell on all of her mistakes before that all too familiar soundtrack filtered into the room: a cacophony of screaming, drilling, scraping and metal clanging together. Lena didn’t have the energy or the strength to fight it. She didn’t want to fight it, she had done this to herself and she would accept the punishment.

 

__________

 

“So, everyone’s okay?” Kara asked.

 

“We have ninety-seven girls accounted for, the older ones are, understandably, in shock. They’re struggling to come to terms with what’s going on but they all seem to be physically okay.” Kara let out a sigh of relief.

 

“Keep me updated?”

 

“Of course.”

“Thanks, Barry.” She ended the call and turned to Sam. They were at the base of the mountain, having spent the day avoiding the SUVs racing towards the summit. “You didn’t find it a little weird that you were left to take care of ninety-seven children?” Kara asked.

 

Sam shook her head, “not after the article. On a few occasions before, we’ve battened down the hatches to avoid discovery. Talia called every active agent back as part of the damage control, keep them close and she can regain control.”

 

“How did you manage to take care of thirty toddlers by yourself?” Kara said, in complete shock and, mainly, admiration.

 

“When everyone left, all training programs ceased.” She cleared her throat, “the older girls helped out with the kids,” Sam sounded like she wanted to say something else. Kara waited, “those few days were probably the least stressed and anxious I’ve ever felt at The Academy.”

 

“Well, you don’t have to go back ever again.” Kara watched the smile creep onto Sam’s face, she quickly fought it.

 

“It’s not over yet. We still have work to do.” Sam said.

 

“Come on, there’s a safe house not far from here and we have a lot to talk about.” Kara set off towards her car and Sam followed close behind.

 

The drive was silent for the first couple of minutes, Sam closed in on herself and curled up on the passenger seat. “How-” Kara swallowed thickly, “why do you think Lena is… what happens the third time around?” Kara finally finished, she still couldn’t comprehend the thought that Lena was dead.

 

Sam stared out of the window, “I’ve only ever seen one person survive a third reset: Helena Bertinelli was one of us but when she came out of that cell, she was someone completely different. She was apart of the group before Lena and I, but we were close; she became withdrawn, cold, hollow. She was a shell stuck to Nyssa’s side until she was killed and then… they replaced Nyssa with Helena.” Sam explained.

 

“The point I’m trying to make is, each time you go through a reset the process gets worse because your mind is resisting; it either breaks you or turns you into someone else… Lena knows this, she’s seen it first hand. I…” There was a pause before Sam finally looked at her, “I don’t think she’ll put herself through that if she’s going to come out the other side as someone completely different.” Kara’s jaw clenched at the implication.

 

“Well, we just have to work fast.” Kara put her foot down, “then that won’t be an option.” Kara’s determination and optimism was surprising to Sam, but then again she comes from a place where every action is controlled, free thoughts are suppressed and optimism slowly dwindles.

 

“When did you sort things out? The last time I saw Lena she threw that necklace off a cliff, I thought you were both done.” Sam said.

 

“So did I,” Kara said. “When we had that huge fight, I said some horrible things… stuff I said out of anger and pain. No matter how much I tried to deny it, I hated every second that she was gone. She’s my best friend, my confidant… my person.” Kara’s voice wobbled, she covered it well, “we found our way back to each other again and I love her.”

 

“Do you tell her?” Sam asked.

 

“Everyday.”

 

“Good. She deserves someone who loves her.”  

 

“You all do.” Kara said simply.

 

Sam fell silent again, looking out of the window.

 

Kara cleared her throat, “I have another confession.” Sam turned to face her, “I was deployed in the Democratic Republic of Congo and I led a spontaneous and unplanned rescue mission which resulted in the death of Nyssa Al Ghul.” Kara’s eyes stayed fixed on the road.

 

“You killed… You killed Nyssa?” Sam said, not quite believing it.

 

Kara nodded, “I didn’t know who she was, I noticed some suspicious activity and I killed her while rescuing the child she had abducted.”

 

“I mean, it’s kind of hilarious. Talia was desperate to make you one of us and you killed her only remaining family.” Sam bit her lip to stop her from laughing but a small giggle escaped.

 

“It’s not funny!”

 

“It is. Talia’s gonna flip, she prides herself on her intelligence and she has no idea that you…” she was fully laughing now, “you killed her sister!” She wheezed clapping her hands together. Kara sighed, gripped the wheel and stared at the road, allowing Sam to enjoy the moment.  

 

Kara was grateful that she was laughing, she was so focussed on saving Lena she hadn’t really had the time to process everything that Kara had told her. If she had allowed herself to feel everything, Kara might have had another fight on her hands.

 

She pulled up to the safe house and they both got out. Kara tried her code three times and growled when it failed to work. “Are you sure you’re typing it in right?” Sam said, very unhelpfully.

 

“Yes.” Kara growled. “Before I left, I was suspended and they’ve revoked my access.” Kara turned and fiddled with her phone. “S’okay, I reckon I can get another code-” Sam had her own plan, “it’ll just take a minute, but it’s important that we don’t-” Kara heard a loud bang followed by the sound of wood splintering, “force it.”

 

Kara gave her a pointed look and Sam shrugged, “what? At least we’re in.”

 

“Do you know what happens when someone breaks into a CIA safe house?” Kara pinched the corners of her eyes.

 

Sam shrugged, “a curse is placed on their first born child?” She said, clear sarcasm in her tone.

 

Kara clenched her jaw and sighed, “you’re hilarious,” she deadpanned. “The alarms alert the local police force and if you can’t prove you work for the CIA, you’re arrested, extradited and thrown in a CIA black site.” Sam suddenly became very interested in in her nails.

 

“My bad?” Kara groaned, “well I can’t un-kick the door down, Kara!” She yelled as Kara ran into the apartment to grab everything she could get her hands on. She tossed a bag to Sam and they hurried down the stairs towards the car.

 

Kara could already hear the sirens in the distance as she pulled onto the road. She expertly manoeuvred her way through the traffic, putting as much distance as possible between themselves and the safe house. She heard that distinctive click and looked over, Sam was loading a pistol.

 

“Don’t you dare, put that away.” Kara ordered.

 

“Well, what’s your plan?” Sam argued.

 

“This!” Kara gestured to the car.

 

“Remind me not to pick you in a fight,” she muttered.

 

Kara took a sharp right turn and Sam’s head bounced off the window. She yelped and Kara sniggered, “would you like me to warn you next time?” Sam groaned. “Put it away, we don’t need to fight out way out, we just have to be smart.”

 

Kara took another couple of sharp turns, Sam sat arms folded, scowl on her face.  “The sirens are getting closer.” She commented, sucking her teeth.

 

Kara ignored her and continued with her plan. She slowed down to an appropriate speed and they watched as six police cars whizzed past them, “you’ve taken us back to the safe house!” Sam exclaimed, Kara ignored her again. She pulled out into the road and parked up outside a café opposite the apartment building. “Are you kidding?” Sam watched as Kara got out of the car. “Oh, she’s not kidding.”

 

Kara grabbed her backpack from the back seat, “you coming or not?” Sam huffed and joined her.

 

“We’re going to get caught-”

 

Kara turned to her, “can you speak Polish?” she nodded. “Good, you can order. Get me some ice?” Kara pushed her inside and sat down at a table in the corner, she watched out of the corner of her eye as the Polish police raided the building, finding nothing.

 

Sam sat down just as the police were leaving, Kara looked at her expectantly. “Okay, so you’re plan wasn’t that dumb.” Sam said, Kara smiled triumphantly. “So, any ideas as to how we’re supposed to pull this off?”

 

“A few, but to give us any chance of success, I need you to tell me everything.” Kara said, softly.  

 

Sam didn’t hesitate. “The location of the headquarters is in the Bükk Mountains in Hungary.” Sam said, “it’s officially registered as a quaint, little private residential lodge so they could keep unwanted visitors away and get planning permission.” Kara frowned.

 

“That doesn’t seem like something Talia would be particularly bothered about?”  

 

“Well, she’s not. Technically, she owns that land but it sits within the borders of a National Park so she had to get permission. In reality, it’s a huge, state of the art facility.”

 

“How did she manage to get away with that?”

 

“She’s Talia Al Ghul, she can basically do whatever she wants. Most people are terrified of her, and if they aren’t, she just pays them off,” Sam shrugged. “Explains how she’s gotten away with so much.”

 

“I don’t understand how intelligence agencies all over the world believe she’s dead, if she’s out here getting planning permission.” Sam huffed out a laugh.

 

“Well, I expect that she’s careful not to use her own name on anything official. Majority of the people who know she’s still alive are either loyal to her or are criminals themselves. Hell, they pay her for our expertise.”

 

“So, people are either too afraid or too corrupt to stand up to her.”

 

“Exactly. I wouldn’t put it past her to have used one of us to threaten or take out any potential threats.” Kara shook her head and stared at the table. “I’m starting to question just how many assignments really were for, “the greater good” and what was for her own personal gain.” Sam scoffed.

 

“I wouldn’t dwell on that too much right now, the past is the past. You can’t go back, you can’t change what you’ve done, you can only go forward and try to be better.” Sam contemplated her words for a second before giving her a small smile. “Anything else?” Kara asked, swiftly changing the subject.

 

“Well, the whole building is guarded by soldiers deployed by a private army. Not to mention, potentially fifty or more highly trained assassins.” Kara swallowed thickly.

 

“How many entrance and exit points?”

 

“Two: one at the front and one at the back.” Sam said, simply.

 

“Any weak points.” Kara had pulled out her journal and jotted down everything Sam had said.

 

“No. That’s my point Kara, I don’t see any way in which we can get in without being shot on sight.” The waitress came over at that point and placed two cups of coffee and a bag of ice in front of them.

 

“Thank you,” they both said.

 

Kara grabbed the ice and placed it over her eye, her head throbbed and she knew she would have a nasty black eye in the next few hours. The waitress’ brow furrowed in concern, “don’t worry, she’s a boxer. She’s just not very good, always ends up getting her ass beat.” The waitress shot her a sympathetic smile, Kara frowned at Sam who was smirking into her mug.

 

“I hate you.” Sam sniggered and Kara pulled out her laptop and a flashdrive. “I have an idea, it might increase our chances, but it will potentially hurt a lot of people.” Sam nodded for her to continue, “what would turn those women against Talia?”

 

Sam leaned back in her chair, “you want to release their names to the press.”

 

“I do.” Kara watched her reaction.

 

Sam was silent for a few minutes, “it could work and you’re right, they all deserve to know the truth. Or, it could backfire severely and you could piss off a lot of very dangerous people.” Kara moved the ice from her eye to her jaw and Sam winced slightly in sympathy.

“If we release every name, surely they’ll have to believe it. There’s no way they would believe that I just happened to discover the names of every single child and assassin the World Killers have, and then came up with this elaborate lie to place the blame on Talia.” Kara argued.

 

“You’re underestimating the power Talia has, that woman has a silver tongue. She’d paint me as a traitor and tell them I gave their names away.” Sam said.

 

“Well, we have to try something!” Kara didn’t have time to re-think every point of her plan, if she delved too deep into every aspect they’d be here arguing for weeks.

 

“Look, you either release the names and there’s a chance it doesn’t work, meaning you have to take on every assassin, or you don’t go to the press and you’ll definitely have to face all of them.” She took another sip of her coffee. It was clear that Sam didn’t want to make that decision, she didn’t want to have to shoulder the responsibility of crushing so many lives.

 

Kara contemplated the decision: she’d much rather face an opponent she’d tried to save then one who is ignorant to the truth and therefore has no choice in the matter.  

 

She opened a file and showed it to Sam. “I have a list of every baby that was kidnapped, can you identify the girls that are still alive?” Sam nodded, she went through every name, highlighting the names of the girls that were still alive. It didn’t take her long and Kara compiled an email to multiple news desks, she attached each girls file with it.

 

She looked at Sam, who gave her a reassuring smile and pressed send.

 

“Well, there’s no going back now. It terms of breaching the facility, I think I have a plan that will work, but I’m not sure.” Kara said.

 

“Can’t be worse than the plans you’ve come up with before.” Sam said, taking a sip of her coffee.

 

“Thanks for the confidence boost,” she replied, dryly.

 

“Tell me.” Sam sighed. Kara explained everything and Sam added her input. They eventually agreed on a plan they thought would work, it would be risky and they would have to rely on a lot of outside influences and a little bit of luck, but they both agreed it was a risk worth taking.

 

“I have quite a few phone calls to make but then we’ll get going, okay?” Sam nodded. Kara stepped outside onto the street.

 

“Hey Kara, what’s up?”

“Alex, I have a huge favour to ask.” Kara said, biting the pad of her thumb.

 

“Hit me.”

“Do you remember when I talked to you about my girl at the reunion?”

 

“Uh huh.”

“Well, we made up.” Kara smiled at Alex’s whoop of glee, “her name is Lena and she’s in trouble Al.” Kara tried to keep her voice level, of course Alex recognised the name, Lena was the woman who had saved her from certain death.

 

“When and where?”

“Alex, I  wouldn’t ask if I wasn’t desperate, but I’m also well aware that you have a wife and child on the way. I need to tell you all the details before you make this decision.” Kara protested vehemently.

 

“When and where, Kara?”

__________

 

Inside and Sam was forming her own plan, conditioning as deep and damaging as hers doesn’t break so easily as for some random blonde showing up and telling her she has a family somewhere.

 

“I need to speak to Talia.” She said.

 

“Verification.”

“Sierra Alpha 2-0-1-1.”

 

“Reign, I didn’t expect to hear from you.” There was genuine surprise in her voice, so she didn’t know about The Academy.

 

“I don’t have long,” she quickly glanced outside, Kara was still on the phone. “Kara Danvers is still alive and Interpol raided The Academy, they have all of the girls.” Talia let of a litany of curses. “We’re still in Poland, but her plan is to call on some of her old team mates and storm HQ. They’re going to attack the front and while you’re distracted, I’m supposed to slip her in through the back.” Talia hummed thoughtfully.

 

“Very well, go along with the plan and when she’s inside, you’ll bring her to me.” Talia ordered.

 

“Copy that.” Sam said, there was a brief pause. “I know she messed up but… is Lena okay?”

 

“She’s coping, she’ll be okay. I have full faith that she’ll come back stronger than ever.” Talia reported.

 

“Is there any chance that the she can be released once Kara has been dealt with, I think I could get through to her.” Sam said, “Kara’s been planting lies in her head, I’ve convinced her that her feelings are a fantasy before, I can do it again.”

 

“I’ll think about it.” A shiver ran down her spine, it would be more beneficial for Talia to have a broken Lena then the Lena that Sam grew up with.

 

“I have to go.”

 

“You did a good thing, Sam.”

 

“I know, I’ll keep you updated.” she hung up the phone and waited for Kara to come back.

 

“Good news, they all agreed to come,” Sam matched her wide smile.

 

“This just might work, Danvers.”

 

“This has to work. Are you ready to go? It’s gonna be a long drive.” Sam nodded, as soon as Kara’s back was turned Sam texted Talia.

 

SA: En route to Hungary.

 

The pair got into the car and Kara started the long drive. They figured it would be the easiest way to get their weapons into the country, they certainly wouldn’t get passed airport security.

 

Sam stared out the window, “do you want to pick the music?”

 

“Huh?” Kara handed Sam her phone.

 

“Pick anything you want,” Kara shot her a smile and there was a pang in Sam’s chest. She turned on the screen and saw the photo of Lena on her lockscreen.

 

“Um… what’s your password?” Kara told her and she pulled up Kara’s Spotify and chose the Spice Girls.

 

“Interesting,” Kara commented.

 

“What?”

 

“Lena mocked me for playing the Spice Girls.”

 

“That’s because she has the worst taste in music,” Kara snorted.

 

“It is pretty bad.” She agreed. “So, tell me what Lena was like as a kid. I need some ammunition for when we get her back.”

 

When I get her back.

“She was pretty much the same as she is now.” Kara pressed her for more detail. “Um, well she was always really small and so she was given larger portions at meal times, in the hopes that she would grow. I was always hungry and she used to split her food with me. We used to have Krupnik, it’s a kind of soup, and she always gave me her bread roll.” Sam turned away and bit her lip, she hadn’t expected the confession to hurt her so much. “Explains why she was always so fucking small.” She joked.

 

“She’s still fucking small.” Sam snorted and Kara giggled along with her.

 

“She’s always been inherently good. She can be ruthless, cunning and manipulative, but not to people she cares about, only those whose pose a threat.” Sam was wringing her hands and Kara wished she hadn’t asked now. What Sam said only served as a reminder to all the times Lena had done the same for her, without question.  

 

They stayed silent after that.

 

Kara pulled up to a gas station after a few hours, “you want anything?” Sam shook her head. Kara returned a few minutes later, arms full of snacks and bottles of water.

 

They continued the journey, Sam struggled to stay awake as they entered The Czech Republic: her eyes were heavy and her head kept dropping suddenly and waking her up. “Put your seat back and get some sleep.” Kara said softly.

 

“Mm no. I’ll take over the driving soon.”

 

“If you think I’m letting you behind the wheel while you’re like this, then you’re sorely mistaken.” Kara said, “go on,” she nodded her head. “I don’t mind.” Sam paused for a few seconds and then did as she was told.

 

“You’ll wake me in a couple hours?” Kara nodded and switched to her calming playlist. She drove through the night while Sam slept.

 

Sam woke up just as they were entering Hungary, “you said you’d wake me.” She yawned.

 

“You look like you needed it.” Sam had an emotional day, she needed to sleep. Kara needed something to focus on, she was scared, anxious and too pent up to sleep; she needed to get them to Hungary safely.

 

“Pull over, I’ll take over the rest of the way.” Kara nodded, she could use a break, she wouldn’t sleep but she could use a break from staring at the road, her eyes were burning. They swapped over and Kara pulled out her journal, scribbling down notes, thoughts. “What are you doing?”

 

“Just writing stuff down. It’s something I used to do while oversees: I’d write out all the details, my thoughts, how I was feeling, any concerns I had and I’d usually feel better.” Kara explained.

 

“I have to say, you’re very different to how I expected.” Sam said, “honestly, I didn’t expect you to be this detailed or organised.”

 

Kara didn’t look up from what she was writing, “I’m trying to be better… at everything. This is the best way for me to organise my thoughts. I let my emotions get the better of me, but I can’t let that happen any more.” There was a beat of silence and then a whisper, “she means too much to me.”

 

__________

 

Lena didn’t know how long she’d been in the room, it was constantly lit up and the litany of noise continued. Her mouth was dry and rough, her tongue felt too big for her mouth and her lips were chapped.

 

She rolled awkwardly onto her side, pressing her forehead against the cool concrete. Her headache had become a migraine: her head was throbbing, she couldn’t bare to open her eyes and closing them provided no relief. She’d vomited on the floor and had to awkwardly try and shuffle away. She used her dwindling energy to force herself to sit up and lean back against the wall.

 

She winced at the grinding of the lock, shortly after the door was wrenched open and Talia entered the room. Lena raised an eyebrow at the sight, but she didn’t have the words to say anything.

 

Talia crouched down in front of her and opened a bottle of water, she helped Lena to drink. It was quite honestly the best thing Lena had ever tasted. “I never wanted this,” Talia said. Lena hummed, unable to form any kind of response at this point. Talia sat down next to her, “it was Nyssa’s idea, we knew that we’d never be able to adopt babies without visits, identification and records. Nyssa suggested that we just… take them instead. You have to understand I just wanted to do good and just look at all the good we’ve achieved.”

 

“Wh…” Lena croaked and Talia helped her drink some more. “Why continue after Nyssa’s death?” Lena took her time to get her words out.

 

“Because I want to fix the world, Lena! I thought you understood that.” Lena scoffed, it was an immediate, gut reaction and probably the wrong one but, fuck it she probably came to kill me anyway. “Lena,” she warned.

 

“No. Kidnapping and torturing children until they fit your super soldier mould is not fixing anything, it’s making it worse!” Talia growled. “You can’t fix me! You can’t bend me to your will! So you can leave me here to rot because I won’t ever do your bidding ever again!” Lena screamed, her voice was already hoarse and cracking.

 

Talia got to her feet and Lena watched as she poured the rest of the water onto the floor and dropped the bottle. “Fine.”

 

Lena would not lower herself to drinking water from the floor, she just stared straight ahead as the door clanged shut.

 

Lena might have cried if she wasn’t so dehydrated.

 

__________

 

SA: We’ve arrived in Hungary. On the way to get Kara’s team.

 

They pulled up to the airport and got out to greet the team. Even on a twelve hour flight Alex still wore a leather jacket and managed to look like she’d only been travelling for thirty minutes, with her perfectly styled hair and aviators perched on her nose.

 

Clark looked happy and well rested: he usually took a sleeping pill and slept the whole flight; it was probably the longest, consecutive sleep he’d had since Jonathan was born.

 

Ava Sharpe looked pissed, Kara could see the scowl on her face behind the dark glasses, sleep mask perched on her mussed hair and a neck pillow tucked under her arm.

 

Kate Kane was cool as a cucumber, not a hair out of place, shades on her head and her bag slung over her shoulder.

 

Kara pointed out each member of the team as they approached. Sam stood and watched as she greeted them: Alex gave her a tight, reassuring hug and whispered something in her ear, Clark gave her a bear hug, lifting her off the ground, Ava gave her one-armed hug and grumbled something and finally, Kara and Kate engaged in some kind of elaborate handshake.

 

“Sam, this is everyone. Everyone, this is Sam. She’s going to help us with this assignment so be nice.” Kara said. Sam gave the group a small smile and a head tilt, she was quite clearly outnumbered and surrounded by Kara’s friends which meant her next moves needed to be clinically precise.

 

“So, is she as bossy with you as she is with me?” Sam said.

 

“Oh, do I have some stories for you,” Kate linked arms with her and walked her out to the car. Kara was happy that Sam was attempting to fit in, she knew that she was most likely playing a character, but it took Lena months to break that pattern.

 

Kara grabbed Ava’s bag and led the rest of the group to the car, “how you doing Ava?”

 

“I had a sweaty, snoring starfish in my face for twelve hours.” She grumbled, nodding towards Clark. Kara looped an arm around her shoulders.

 

“Don’t worry, you can sleep in the car.” Kara said. They still had just over two hours to travel to get where they needed to be. Kara and Sam had come well prepared with food and drinks for the team. Ava took the seat in the back and was asleep within ten minutes, Alex called shotgun and was upfront. Clark was entertaining himself in the back, Kate and Sam were sat next to each other.

 

“What do you mean, you haven’t seen Back to the Future?” Kate was outraged.

 

“Um, I just never saw it.” Sam said, Kara caught the uncomfortable shift of her body in the rear-view mirror.

 

“Oh, I bet you have strange taste in films, you probably like that independent stuff, right?” She was teasing, but Sam was under pressure now.

 

“Hey,” Kara said. “I have Back to the Future on my laptop, you should watch it now while we have the time. Alex can you?” She nodded to the backpack in the footwell. While Alex was digging through it, she caught Sam’s small, gratuitous smile.

 

__________

 

The car ride was smooth and uneventful, Kara had found an old mechanics workshop, that had gone out of business a couple of years ago. They cut the lock off and set up shop. Sam and Kara gathered the group and talked them through the plan and then they were left to get their equipment ready.

 

Kara’s team were well versed in strange workspaces: Clark checked the weapons, making sure they were all loaded and in working order. “Sam,” he called, “come make your choice,” he already knew what everyone else wanted.

 

Ava was their explosives expert, she was busy making sure they had everything they needed. Alex was the medic and she was checking the gear bags and medical supplies and Kate was busy setting up multiple laptops, she was on logistics. She was researching the schematics of the building, looking for any potential weaknesses or threats.

 

Kara watched her team with pride, she always thought she was alone, maybe all she needed was a little bit of perspective. These guys dropped everything and agreed to come here with little to no detail as to what they would face.

 

“Sam,” she called gently. “Can you work with Kate and give her as much detail about the building as possible. Any places of significance, anywhere you think Lena could be or any places that could be of use: armouries, access points, record archives.”

 

“I’ll do what I can.”  She spent a good amount of time with Kate, pointing out everything she could think of.

 

It all got a little too much for her after a while, Sam stepped outside to take a breather. She pulled out her phone and made a call to Talia, she got straight through this time, “I don’t have much time. The team is made up of four each experts in their field: weaponry, explosives, logistics. The plan hasn’t changed: the four will attack from the front, Kara and I will head in through the back and that’s when I’ll detain her and pass her over to you.” Sam said.

 

“Good, you’re doing extremely well Sam, keep up the good work and we’ll pull this off.”

“I have to ask…”

 

“I understand, but it’s not true Sam, I was there when Nyssa picked you up from that orphanage, when she brought you home.”

She closed her eyes and hummed. “How is she?” Sam couldn’t quite bring her self to say Lena’s name just yet.

 

“She’s resisting,” Sam gnawed on her bottom lip. “I suggest you be quick.” The line went dead and Sam choked on her intake of breath.

 

Kara was checking in on her team as they went through their final preparations, “what does Maggie think about all of this?” Kara said, she leaned against the workbench.

 

Alex huffed lightly, keeping up with her count, “well, she’s not overly ecstatic, as expected, but she understands why I need to do this.” Kara crossed her arms and nodded. She called on Alex because she’s always been Kara’s right hand, but it didn’t feel good by any means. “You buy us dinner when we get back and you’ll be back on her good side.”

 

“That goes for Lois and I also,” Clark chirped from where he was standing.

 

“Done.” Kara chuckled.

 

“So, Lena was looking for you that day?” Alex asked.

 

“Yeah, she’s actually the reason I figured it out. She tried to warn me… well I guess she did warn me.” Kara explained.

 

“Well, that explains why she was so… heartbroken when I spoke to her, she thought you were in there.” Kara nodded. “She’ll be okay, that girl is strong and she is one hell of a fighter.” Kara leant her elbows on the work bench, she pinched the corners of her eyes and took a deep breath. Alex put an arm across her shoulders and rubbed her back. “Hey, everything will be fine, Kar.”

 

“It’s just hard, not knowing where she is, whether she’s okay.” Kara swallowed thickly, pushing those emotions down.

 

“You wanna see something cool?” Kara nodded, head still between her hands. Alex pulled a photo out of her wallet and nudged Kara, she looked up and gasped at the sight of the ultrasound. She put a hand over her mouth and stared at the baby.

 

“Wow, Alex. Look at that! That’s a whole baby!” Kara said excitedly.

 

“Right? You can’t see all of them, but I’m pretty sure she has ten fingers and ten toes.” Kara began squealing and giggling, Alex joined in with the excitement.

 

Kara gasped and stopped, “did you say “she”?” Alex nodded. “Oh my god, you’re having a girl?”

 

“Yeah, we found out a few weeks ago.” Kara squealed again and pulled her into a hug.

 

“I’m so happy for you.” She whispered.

 

“Did it cheer you up?” Kara nodded. “Good, now come on,” she tapped the bench, “I need to look at your face.” She groaned but hopped up anyway. “What happened?”

“It was a gift from Sam,” Kara said, she hissed when Alex checked her eye for a fractures. Kara really didn’t want to go into the reasoning behind it, she’d come to the conclusion that the only way she was going to get through this was to try not to think about Lena directly.

 

“Kara,” Alex sad softly. “Do you really trust her?”

 

“I do.” She said sincerely.

 

“It’s just, she’s one of them and from what you’ve told us, it would be extremely difficult to break that mindset.” Kara listened to Alex’s concerns.

 

“I know, I’ve seen it first hand, but Lena is her best friend, they grew up together, they went through all of that together. I have faith in her, I know she wants the same thing as me: she wants to save Lena and take down Talia, we’re on the same team.” Kara said.

 

“Okay,” Alex nodded, “if you trust her, so do I.”

 

__________

 

Sam knew what kind of physical state Lena would be in, she just hoped that she could get there before her Lena was gone forever. Talia sounded agitated on the phone and she wasn’t known for her patience.

 

Lena was in trouble.

 

She bit her knuckles, “hey.” Her head whipped to the side and she saw Kara stood, leaning against the wall. Kara could see her eyes glistening with tears, “how you holding up?”

 

“I’m okay.” She lied.

 

“Really? I’m terrified.” Kara admitted, “if this doesn’t work. I could lose everything: Clark has a little boy at home, Alex’s wife is pregnant with their first, they’ve put everything on the line for me.” Kara sat on the floor next to her. “Then there’s Lena, I don’t know what I’ll do if I lose her.”  

 

“If you could do it all over again, would you still choose love?” She looked at Kara who was staring into the distance.

 

“It was never a choice, it just happened. God, she’s a pain in my ass.” They both chuckled, “but if I could re-do it all, I wouldn’t change a thing.” Kara clutched the necklace hanging from her neck, Sam almost told her everything when he phone began ringing.

 

“Hello?”

 

“Sam, where the fuck are you? It’s absolute chaos here!” Sara’s voice was full of panic.

 

“What’s going on?” Sam feigned confusion, she looked at Kara.

 

“Everyone knows our names, they’re splashed across every news desk in the world! Every single girl, even the little ones! They keep saying that we were kidnapped as children!” She nodded towards Kara. “Sam?”

 

“I’m here, just take a breath Sara.” Sam took one with her.

 

“Everyone’s gone.”

 

“Everyone?”

 

“Leslie flew off the handle, she attacked Selina! Her and Rhea are attempting to control the damage, Talia’s nowhere to be seen and Helena hasn’t been seen in days. Leslie left first and everyone just followed.”

 

“I’ll text you an address, meet me there, okay?”

 

“Okay.” Sam hung up the phone and turned towards Kara, “well it worked, they’ve all gone.”  Kara squeezed her shoulder.

 

“I’m sorry, it had to happen this way.” She said softly.

 

“Me too, but I don’t think it could have happened any other way.” Kara got up and Sam followed, Kara squeezed her shoulder. “It will work, as long as we stick to the plan, we’ll get Lena back.” Sam nodded and Kara turned to leave.

 

“Kara?“ She turned, “we need to go soon.” She swallowed her confession and went back to staring into the distance.

 

“We will, I just don’t want to rush anything.” Kara said.

 

“She’s been there for what, five- six days? That’s a long time Kara.” Sam’s voice was low, accusatory.

 

“Don’t you think I know that?” Kara said, Sam suddenly became extremely agitated and hostile.

 

“You’re not doing anything! We’re just sat around waiting! Don’t you get it? don’t you understand what’s going on?!” Sam was in her face now.

 

“Of course I understand! Every second I’m here, I’m imagining what’s happening to her and it’s killing me!” Kara bit her lip, “and… I’m trying to hold it together...” she took a shaky breath, “so if you could just trust me,” she pleaded.

 

It was clear they were both struggling to cope with the current situation. “I’m sorry,” Sam whispered. Kara opened her arms, Sam hesitated for a second before stepping into the hug. Kara understood the frustration, Sam was experiencing a whirlwind of emotions and the one person who could understand exactly what she was going through wasn’t there.

 

“Everything will be okay.” Kara murmured.

 

__________

 

Talia was in the middle of a complete meltdown, everything she had worked so hard for was crumbling in front of her. Her control was slipping.

 

Talia decided she was going to inflict as much pain onto Kara as possible.

 

The lock screeched again and Lena cracked her eyes open, her head was still pounding and she was light-headed. She was shivering, suddenly very aware of the fact that her body temperature was dropping, but Lena’s main focus was forcing air into her lungs regularly.

 

Talia cut the ties around her wrists. “You’re free to go.”

 

Lena looked up, Talia placed a bottle of water down in front of her. Lena tried to say something but she couldn’t form the words.

 

Talia tossed something behind her as she shut the door, the bottle rolled to a stop in front of her. She reached out and read the label.

 

Her freedom came at the greatest price.

 

It might not be so bad. All the pain would stop and I could just drift away. Fall asleep dreaming of Kara.

__________

 

A black SUV pulled up, screeching to a stop outside of the workshop. Kara and Alex were immediately on their guard, two women got out of the car: a blonde and a brunette. Sam rushed past the pair and ran over to hug both women.

 

“So, that must be Sara.” Kara muttered.

 

“Who’s the other one?” Alex hissed, Kara shrugged and avoided looking at her. “Great, there’s three of them now.” Kara understood her worry, but ignored the comment because she had faith in Sam.

 

The conversation lasted a few minutes and then the brunette stormed over. Kara was expecting it, she kept her hands glued to her sides.

 

“Andrea!” Sam ran after her, catching her just after she’d slapped Kara across the face. Alex stepped in, but Kara put a hand on her arm.

 

“Andrea Rojas?” Sam nodded. Kara had released her name originally, along with Sam’s, “yeah, I deserved that one.” Then the blonde marched over, “so that makes you Sara?”

 

Sara looked as if she was going to throw her own punch, but Ava stepped in and cut her off.

 

 “You need to calm down,” Ava said.

 

“She’s the reason we’re in this mess!” Sara shouted.

 

“Kara, is the reason you found out the truth.” Ava said.

 

“And who the hell are you?” Sara yelled, she pushed Ava away and that’s when it all got a little hazy: Ava and Sara got into a scuffle, Kate rushed over and tried to break them up, Andrea mistook that for an attack and they started their own fight.

 

Clark got an elbow in the jaw when he tried to intervene, Alex managed to wrench Kate away from Andrea, Sam watched on in horror and Kara was so close to pulling her hair out.

 

“Enough!” Kara bellowed. Everything stopped, “get up!” Ava scrambled to her feet, Sara stayed on the floor defiantly. Ava and Clark hauled her to her feet, Kate helped Andrea to hers. “I get it, you’re angry and I’m sorry you had to find out that way. But, at least you got away! Lena’s still there,” Andrea looked down at the floor and Kara didn’t feel the need to go into any more detail. “I don’t expect you to come with us, I’d understand if you want to get as far away from here as possible. We have bags prepared for both of you. But, if you want, you can come with us and we can tear it all down, together.”

 

Sara stared at the floor, making patterns in the dirt with her feet. Andrea looked over, “Lena would go back for any of us.”

 

Sara took a deep breath, “it can’t hurt to hear the plan”

 

The group went inside and the team had a proper briefing this time.

 

Kate pulled up the schematics, more for Kara’s team than the assassins. “The building itself is a modern day fortress: surrounded by four watch towers, it’s guarded by a private army of highly trained mercenaries. Each entrance is controlled by an individual passcode and biometric scanner, the doors inside are passcode protected. Again, each person has their own individual passcode which is logged onto a system and can identify who is in the building and where they are.” She handed out copies of the blueprints, she marked out the places Sam had told her about.

 

“It’s likely that there will be more hostiles inside. Potential mercenaries, reluctant members of the organisation and at least three particularly dangerous people: Rhea Largand, Selina Kyle and Talia Al Ghul. The aim is to incapacitate and detain all three.”

 

“Once Sam and I are in, we’ll disable the door locks. You’ll work in pairs: Alex and Clarky you’ll meet Sam and I, we’ll find Lena and Talia. Kate and Andrea you’ll go after any kind of records: missions, medical records, locations of safe houses, anything you can get your hands on. Ava and Sara you’ll sweep the building and take out any remaining hostiles.” Kara explained.

 

“Why is she my partner?!” Ava protested, Alex stood between the pair.

 

“’Cos it’s quite obvious that you two have the most frustration to burn.” Kara said, she glared at Ava. She in turn glared at Sara who narrowed her eyes and blew her a kiss, Ava sneered at her.

 

“Play nice, ladies.” Kate smirked.

 

“Gear up, we leave in five.” Kara ordered. Her team began checking their weapons and putting on their vests. Ava, in an attempt to be nice, tossed Sara her own kevlar. Sara just watched as it hit her chest and dropped to the floor. Kara pinched her brow just waiting for that argument to break out.

 

“They don’t wear kevlar,” Kara sighed.

 

“What?” Came the collective response from the Marines.

 

“Kevlar’s for pussies,” Sara snorted.

 

Ava shrugged, “I don’t care if that one dies.”

 

“Ava!”

 

“Oh, you wanna go again, grumpy pants? I’d demolish you!” Sara challenged.

 

“Fine.” Ava pulled her weapon and cocked it, aiming at Sara’s body.

 

She stuttered in her attack, “you win this round.” She relented.

 

“Please just put it on.” Kara pleaded. All three assassins did as she asked, with little to no protest from Sam or Andrea.

 

“How you holding up?” Kara asked, she was getting ready next to Sam who had been oddly quiet since the other two had arrived.

 

“I’m a little nervous,” she glanced at Sara and Ava, who were continuing to bicker. “But, I’m ready.”

 

“Operation: Happily Ever After is a go.” Kara held out her fist and Sam bumped it with a small chuckle.

 

The team headed out to the cars and the three assassins stayed back just a little, Sam finding her place in the middle of Andrea and Sara. “Don’t worry, our plan will work.” She murmured.

 

SA: Heading out now. Be there in twenty.

 

__________

 

The two cars sped up the mountain path, Kara was aiming for a quick, surprise attack while they were vulnerable. They had been through the plan enough times, everyone knew what they were doing, it was time to execute.

 

The cars pulled up in front of the fortress, the two front ends facing each other and creating a barricade. The team climbed out and were immediately met with gunfire from the guard stations, all eight of them took cover behind their makeshift barricade.

 

Alex and Clark moved to the wings, getting an angle on the guard towers, Kate and Andrea took the front, taking out the guards lining the top of the fortress. Ava and Sara were loading the RPG.

 

“You ready?” Kara asked, Sam nodded. They tucked themselves in behind Alex, waiting for the signal. Sara and Ava had already argued in the car about who would get to fire the rocket launcher, Sara having won the game of rock paper scissors.

 

Sara lined up and fired taking out the first watch tower.

 

Sam and Kara moved during the chaos they sprinted across the ground and under the second guard tower. Sara got far too excited and fired the second rocket before they’d cleared the blast zone, Kara dragged Sam to the ground and they covered their heads as debris flew everywhere.

 

The team held their breath until they saw both their heads pop up. Kara held her hands up, clearly saying, “what the fuck was that?”

 

“My bad!” She called, Ava wrenched the weapon away from her.

 

Sam went to climb to her feet, but Kara pulled her back down. Her ears were still ringing but she saw Kara point and watched as a group of heavily armed guards rounded the corner and jogged past them.

 

Kara tapped her twice and the pair scrambled to their feet and sprinted to the back of the building, they took out the last remaining men guarding the back entrance. But, it seemed, the plan had worked so far.

 

Sam typed her passcode in and pressed her thumb into the scanner. The door unlocked immediately.

 

Kara shot Sam a smile and entered the building.

 

She was met with Talia Al Ghul’s cruel smile and guns pointed at her, by who had to be, Selina and Rhea. She felt the cool barrel of a gun pressed against the base of her neck and she closed her eyes in defeat.

 

It was right under her nose and she was to blind to see it.

 

She had failed.

 

“Please, Sam.” She begged.

 

“Don’t make this harder for yourself.” Sam pressed harder into her skin until Kara surrendered her weapon. Sam tied her hands and pushed her towards Talia.

 

“Well done, Reign.” Kara’s shoulders slumped forward and she stared at the ground.

 

“Acrata and White Canary are out front with the others. They have their orders and won’t be a problem for much long.” Kara let out a whimper, the words were fuzzy in her ears and she just felt numb. Her brain was screaming at her, but her body was frozen. She couldn’t move, she couldn’t save Lena, she couldn’t save her friends and she couldn’t save herself.

 

She had failed.

 

“She’s your friend.” Kara mumbled.

 

“I’m doing this for Lena!” Sam yelled.

 

“Don’t be so disheartened Kara, you did well to get this close.” Talia tormented her, she took hold of Kara’s arm and led her down the hallway and into her office. Kara didn’t look up as she was pushed down into a seat.

 

“Kara Danvers,” Talia gripped her chin and lifted her head so she could see Kara’s eyes: dull and soulless. Talia had done it, she had broken Kara, in the same way that she had broken every other girl in her care. Talia had, once again, proven that she was smarter, more cunning and more ruthless than Kara could ever have predicted.

 

Talia tutted, it was a sarcastic coo. “I have to admit, you did better than I expected: mercilessly killing Helena, figuring out the location of The Academy, you killed how many mercenaries? Then, you convinced your friends to come here, risk their own lives and the lives of their families.” She pouted at the look on Kara’s face, it was disingenuous and it made Kara’s blood boil. “And for what? The life of one girl?”

 

“I love her.” Kara whispered.

 

“You love her,” she mocked. “And yet, you couldn’t save her.” Kara’s eyes widened and Talia took a wicked pleasure in the look of fear and despair. “You were about an hour too late.” Talia said it so casually.

 

Kara had taken everything from Talia and she was going to make every second of this excruciating.

 

Kara was a mess, her body was shaking, tears streamed down her face and her nose was running. Without, the use of her hands, she couldn’t clear her blurry vision or wipe her face, she just had to sit there while Talia relished in her pain.

 

“If it’s any consolation, she didn’t suffer.” Kara’s head dropped.

 

“She spent her whole life suffering.” Kara ground out. “I thought she meant something to you, and you speak about her as if she’s just a spare part you can discard.”

 

“Lena was special, from the first time I saw that baby’s eyes, I just knew she would be one of the greatest recruits we would ever have and she was.” Talia said.

 

“So, you thought it was okay to take her away from her mother!”

 

“I made that girl into the woman she is!” Kara twitched and her eyes narrowed.

 

“No, she became that woman despite what you did!”

 

“I gave her everything-”

 

“You took everything from her!” Kara yelled, “and you took someone very precious to me-”

 

“She was always mine, Kara.” Talia voice was soft and gentle, the complete opposite to the dark, hateful look in her eye.

 

“People are not possessions! Lena is not yours to own.” Kara voice was low and dangerous. “And if I can’t get her back, I will make sure that you never do that to anyone ever again!”

 

Talia almost had her convinced, but she’d slipped up. If Lena was dead, why refer to her in the present tense. Lena would have high-fived her for that one.

 

Talia scoffed and turned away, Kara slid the knife Sam had slipped her from her sleeve and cut through the zip tie around her wrists. “You know, I can tell when you’re lying because everything that comes out of your mouth is sick and twisted. You’re so used to lying, that it’s all you can do. I know she’s still alive.”

 

****

 

“I think I have a plan that will work, but I’m not sure.” Kara said.

“Can’t be worse than the plans you’ve come up with before.” Sam said, taking a sip of her coffee.

“Thanks for the confidence boost,” she replied, dryly.

“Tell me.” Sam sighed.

“From what I’ve determined, Talia’s biggest weakness is that she’s a control freak. In her mind, she’s got such a grip on these girls that she doesn’t believe that anything will relinquish that. I want you to convince her that you’re going to betray me.” Sam tilted her head in thought. “I want you to let her in on the whole plan, make her believe she still has that control over you.”

“That is risky. If she figures out that I’m lying-”

“I know, but if she knows the whole plan, then we can figure out her next move. We both know she wants me dead, I’m the biggest threat to this whole fantasy world she’s living in. In her eyes, Lena is her most prized possession, she’ll do whatever it takes to keep her. We have to stop that.” Kara said.

“You don’t think there’s a chance that she’ll figure all of this out?”

“Not if she thinks you’re still under her thumb, her arrogance won’t let her question it. S he thinks she’s smarter than everyone else.” Kara explained.

“You know all of this and you haven’t even met her yet.” Sam said, there was a glint of delight in her eyes. Hope. That they could pull this off.

“Oh, I know everything I need to know about Talia Al Ghul.” Kara said. “Do you think you could get anyone else on our side? Anyone that would want to help take her down?”

“Potentially a few, but they’d have to reach out to me. If I go to them directly and Talia’s control is as strong as you say, they could blow the whole thing.” Sam theorised.

“You’re right.” Kara agreed.

“But, if they contact me first, and I believe one or two might, I reckon I could convince them to help. Kara, the article will piss off a lot of people, if they release your name,” Kara knew what she was implying.

“Huge target, I know, but if it gets us any closer to getting Lena back then I’ll take it.” Kara said. “I’m going to contact some old friends I served with,” Sam looked uneasy. “Don’t worry, no one will hurt you. We could use all the help we can get, Sam.”

“Marines and assassins, that’s a dangerous concoction, Danvers.”

“Pfft, what could go wrong.”

****

 

Sam watched as Talia led Kara down the corridor, Rhea and Selina congratulated her cunning deception. She beamed at the praise, “where’s Lena? Talia said I could talk to her.” Rhea and Selina both exchanged a look and Sam suddenly felt very uneasy.

 

“Come with us, Sam.” They led her into a separate room, Sam grabbed her gun and struck Selina on the back of the head, knowing she would be the hardest one to incapacitate. Rhea whipped around and Sam blocked the right fist, slamming her own into her solar plexus. She grunted and stumbled backwards, Sam struck her in the face with a swift heel kick and knocked her out.

 

“Wow, you guys have been out of the field for too long.” She tied their wrists and ankles together and dragged them to the corner of the room where they could sleep off their headaches.

 

She disabled all the security protocols, “all alarms are disabled and all doors are unlocked. Ready when you are.”

 

“Copy that. Where’s Kara?” Came Alex’s reply.

 

“She’s in Talia’s office.” Sam prayed that Andrea and Sara got them all to their spots without too much trouble.

 

__________

 

The team outside managed to stave off all attacks and battle their way through the front doors. Ava and Sara split off from the group, preparing to sweep the building.

 

The pair made their way down to the basement: Ava pointed to Sara then to herself, swept a circle over her head and then pointed to the right. Sara frowned and tilted her head to the side, “what the fuck does that mean?” She hissed.

 

Ava rolled her eyes, “cover me and go right! Christ, I thought you were a pro!” Ava scoffed.

 

“Why couldn’t you just say that!” Sara whisper-shouted.

 

“Fine, cover me and go right!” They emerged from the corridor and Sara went left, deliberately barging into her. Ava made a throttling gesture towards her, completely missing Sara’s smirk.

 

Sara was only a little impressed when Ava managed to take out six guys without breaking a sweat. She was more than a little impressed with her own skills at spotting the last guy who came from nowhere and ran at Ava, she shot him and he went down easily.

 

Ava spun around. “Thanks,” she breathed.

 

“Come on grumpy, we have like three more floors to check!”

 

Andrea and Kate broke away from Alex and Clark once they reached the door of Talia’s office. They could hear Kara yelling inside, Andrea pursed her lips  and tilted her head in appreciation of the gutsy move.

 

They climbed up a staircase and entered a computer lab. Andrea sat down in front of a desk and started searching the databases. As she expected, any kind of medical records were password protected and no matter what she tried she couldn’t bypass it.

 

“Computers are not my expertise, are you any good?” Andrea asked, Kate gestured for her to move aside.

 

“I’m an expert.” Andrea held her hands up and backed off, she moved over to the filing cabinet that Kate had been trying to unlock. She had clearly been trying to pick the lock, Andrea found brute force was generally the best way. Andrea reached for her knife and wedged it into the cabinet, prying it open with a loud bang.

 

Kate spun round in the chair, “what? I didn’t say I was subtle either.”

__________

 

“So, where’s your tattoo?” Talia frowned, “well Nyssa had “Endure and Thrive” tattooed right here,” Kara gestured to the inside of her arm, “so where’s yours?” She smirked when the realisation dawned on Talia’s face. Kara made her way to the door, greeted by Alex and Clark.

 

“Keep her here and if she tries anything, shoot her.” She left the room, her head popped back round the corner. “You know what, if she even speaks shoot her. Somewhere non-lethal but will hurt like a bitch.”

 

Talia’s jaw dropped and Alex smirked. “That bit-” Clark shot her in the arm and she fell back into her chair, clutching it in pain.

 

Talia glared at him and he shrugged, “Captain’s orders.”

 

Kara sprinted down the corridor and straight into Sam. “Good job, Sammy.” She beamed.

 

“You too, but Kara, I can’t find her anywhere! I’ve checked all the cameras, all the cells and I’ve checked all the rooms Talia’s code was used. I can’t find her anywhere.” Sam said, desperately.

 

“She’s here, there must be somewhere else she could be.” Kara said.

 

“Kara I’ve looked everywhere!”

 

“Close your eyes,” she gripped  Sam’s shoulders. “Think, is there anywhere that was out of bounds or anywhere that didn’t require a passcode.”

 

“The cleaning closets are the only doors without locks.” Sam’s eyes flew open, “there was a… it was like a broom closet, but people used to say that they heard strange noises coming from inside.” She took off in one direction and Kara followed. Sam sprinted along the winding corridors, Kara had absolutely no idea where they were in relation to the blueprints.

 

Sam skidded to a stop and wrenched the door open, but the closet was empty.

 

“Shit!” She yelled, kicking a bucket across the room. Kara looked around the room but there was nothing of significance.

 

She leant in the door frame to catch her breath, “it’s okay, we’ll find her. Keep thinking.”

 

“There’s no where else.” Kara felt a breeze on the back of her neck. She turned and moved the cleaning supplies away from the back wall, there were no windows in the room so she knew there must be a shaft somewhere. She ran her hands around the edges of the wall, there was a slight gap only the width of around four fingers. Kara felt a latch, she lifted and pushed.

 

The wall gave way and revealed a stairwell.

 

“Sam!” Kara called as she ran down the stairs. They were met with a another corridor, cells lining both sides.

 

Kara took the left, Sam the right.

 

Three doors in, Kara found her.

 

“Lena!” She ran to the body on the floor and collapsed onto her knees. The feeling of finally seeing Lena again could only be described as euphoric.

 

She gathered Lena in her arms and brushed the hair away from her face. “I’ve got you, I’ve got you. You’re safe now.” She received no form of response.

 

The relief quickly turned to dread.

 

“Lena?” Her skin was paler than Kara had ever seen it, her features were sharp and gaunt, her body was limp and lifeless, her breathing weak.

 

That was when Kara saw the bottles and the water bottle was empty. “Sam!” She screamed. “Lena? Lena, baby, how many did you take?” Kara sniffled and squeezed her eyes shut, she had no idea how to fix this.

 

Sam came barrelling through the door, “Lena?” She knelt down next to Kara who was rocking back and forth, sobbing.

 

“I’m so sorry. I failed. I’m so so sorry.” Kara buried her face in Lena’s hair.

 

Sam saw the bottle of pills and grabbed them to inspect the label, she cracked open the bottle to see if she could figure out how many were missing.

 

The foil seal was still intact.

 

“Kara, the seal hasn’t been broken! She hasn’t taken any of these.” Sam said, “she’s going to be okay.” She showed her the bottle, her own eyes were glassy.

 

Kara tears of relief came hard and fast, what felt like weeks of pent up emotion came flooding out of her. Sam cut the ties that were still wrapped around Lena’s legs and took her hand squeezing gently.

 

Kara cradled her tightly whispering sweet nothings into her ear and promises of the things they were going to do together, she was trying to coax her into conciousness while Sam fetched Alex. She realised it was mostly for her own benefit, keeping her calm and grounded so she didn’t have to listen to the wheezing breaths. “What took you so long?” Came a soft mumble.

 

Kara let out a wet chuckle, sniffling again and trying to steady her breathing. “You said, you didn’t need saving.” The corners of Lena’s mouth twitched upwards slightly. Her eyes stayed closed and her body was still limp, but for the first time since Lena had left, Kara knew that everything would be okay.

 

__________

 

Kate had finally managed to crack the firewall when they got the confirmation from Sam that Lena had been found alive. “Have either of you heard from the grouchy blondes, I can’t get hold of either of them.”

 

“They’ve probably killed each other.” Andrea commented as she sifted through the filing cabinet.

 

“Dead or alive, just find them for me.”

 

“Well, it’s going to take a while to for this to download,” Kate pushed herself away from the desk and reloaded her gun.

 

They swept the basement and first two floors and found no sign of them. When they reached the top floor, Andrea made the unfortunate choice of walking into one of the rooms without warning. “Ew, oh god, my eyes!” She recoiled and put her hands over her eyes.

 

“What is it?” Kate mistook her disgust for a potential threat and went to investigate. “Whoa,” she turned shielded her eyes. “Way to go, Sharpy!” She called as she slammed the door shut, Andrea glared at her. “I mean… put a damn sock on the handle Ava, you went to college! Jeez!”

 

“Any luck?” Came Clark’s voice.

 

“They’re both still alive.” Kate informed her.

 

“Great can you ask Ava-”

“No. I can’t.”

 

“You don’t even know what I’m going to say.”

 

“There is nothing you could say that will convince either of us to go back into that room.” Andrea cut in.

 

__________

 

Lena woke up a few days later in the medbay of HQ, Kara and Sam had insisted that taking her to a hospital would be too much of a shock to the system. She panicked for a few moments until she noticed the soft snoring next to her: Kara was sat in a chair at her bedside, her body was slumped forward so that her head was pillowed on Lena’s bed, and she had a soft grip on her hand. Her breath caught in her throat and she couldn’t help her eyes filling with tears, she never thought she’d see her again.

 

“I think that’s the first time she’s slept in like three days.” Sam commented from the other side of her, Lena gave her a soft smile and reached her other hand out for Sam to take.

 

“Wha-” Lena tried but her throat was too dry. Sam grabbed the water and helped her to take a few sips, “what happened?” She croaked.

 

“Oh, you have missed so much.” Sam made sure to fill her in on all the shenanigans that she’d missed out on.

 

Kara stirred to the sound of a throaty chuckle, just as Sam was telling Lena about Sara’s poor timing with the RPG. She mumbled something incoherent and Lena squeezed her hand, Kara’s head shot up her eyes were wide and full of life as she beamed at Lena. Kara stood up and cupped her face, putting everything she had behind a kiss that knocked the air from Lena’s lungs.

 

Sam left the room while they got reacquainted, she mumbled something about how she didn’t need to see that. Kara pulled away after a few minutes and rested her forehead against Lena’s, she couldn’t help the tears rolling down her cheeks.

 

Lena kissed the bruises that littered her face before capturing her lips once again. “You just couldn’t stay away, could you?” Kara shook her head, “you can never just do as you’re told.” Kara continued shaking her head, grinning widely. She surged forward and kissed her again, “so fucking stubborn,”  she mumbled, teasingly.

 

Lena broke the kiss and cupped her face, tucking her hair behind her ears and staring at Kara’s face. “I love you,” Lena whispered.

 

“I love you too.” Kara beamed.

 

__________

 

A few days later and Lena was “discharged”, well she was allowed out of the MedBay. She sat on the small hill that overlooked the field of daffodils: knees tucked into her chest, she hugged her legs and rested her chin on her knees.

 

Kara had been directing the team of Interpol agents who were boxing up mountains of evidence. Talia, Rhea and Selina had been arrested and taken away two days ago, Kara didn’t want Talia dead, she wanted her to stand trial and face the consequences of what she’d done.

 

She wandered over to where Lena was sitting. Her gasp gave away her presence, the view was like nothing she’d ever seen before: it was a sea of yellow, which she would usually consider a joyous sight to behold, but there was a plethora of black marble headstones emerging from the calm that brought an overwhelming air of sorrow to what should be a breathtaking scene.

 

Lena looked up, “it’s really quite something, isn’t it?” Kara nodded, words failing her. She took her place behind Lena, long, lean legs bracketing her body and arms snaked around her waist. Lena opened up and leant back into Kara’s body. “None of them are supposed to be there.”

 

“No.” Kara murmured, “but they can all be returned to their families now and they will finally know the truth.” Lena closed her eyes and basked in the moment, Kara’s strong hold and warming presence instantly calmed the torrent of emotions battling inside her.

 

“So, what happens now?” Lena asked.

 

“Well that bit is easy,” Kara said simply, Lena lifted her head and pressed a kiss to the underside of her jaw, “we go home and we live happily ever after.”

 

 

 

Notes for the Chapter:

When I say final chapter... I'll definitely do an epilogue because there are A LOT of loose ends that need to be tied up, but in terms of plot we're done!

I'm hoping to upload next week, but it might be more like a week and a half.

If you got this far, thank you for reading!

26. Epilogue

Kara called in one last favour and managed to obtain a jet to get the team back to the US, she wanted to get them all home as soon as possible; plus they’d been through a lot and a little bit of luxury wouldn’t go amiss. Lena moved onto Kara’s lap as soon as the lights went down, she tucked her legs up and Kara wrapped her arms around her.

 

“Comfy?” She asked, smile clear in her voice.

 

She hummed and tucked herself further into Kara’s hold. Lena was still fragile and delicate, but she was adamant that she wanted to go home as soon as she was cleared by medical officers. Kara kept a close eye on her and made sure that she knew Lena would manage the flight home.

 

“I’m sorry I drugged you. I just didn’t want you to-”

 

Kara shushed her gently, “it doesn’t matter,” she whispered. “You’re here, it’s over.” Kara reassured her. “Just know, I will never accept a drink from you again.” Lena giggled softly.

 

“I’m really grateful for you.” Lena murmured, she kissed Kara’s cheek and leaned her head against her shoulder.

 

Kara pulled a blanket over them and gave one earbud to her, Lena fell asleep relatively quickly and Kara joined her soon after, the events of the past few weeks had taken its toll on both of them. They woke up a few hours later, still exhausted, but they didn’t want to go back to sleep just yet, everyone else was asleep and it felt like they were the only two people in the world; high up in the sky where no one could touch them.

 

Lena tentatively cupped Kara’s face, aching to touch her but almost afraid in case this wasn’t real and she would wake up in that room. Kara leaned fully into her palm and smiled softly, Lena searched her face taking in every inch, she crossed her eyes and stuck her tongue out making Lena smile. They didn’t need to speak to know exactly what the other was thinking, Kara pressed their foreheads together and closed her eyes, Lena leant forward and kissed her so gently that Kara barely felt it.  

 

The pair dozed: that sweet period between consciousness and unconsciousness. Lena’s hands continued to wander: playing with her fingers before slowly moving up her arms and over her shoulders. Lena’s lips trailed up her neck and throat, it was the only skin she could reach without much effort in her sleepy state. Kara nuzzled her neck, dipped her fingertips underneath her shirt and danced across her lower back, drawing mindless patterns.

 

Lena’s fingers ran up and down her neck and across her collarbones. With all the craziness and uncertainty of the past few days, she had forgotten that she was still wearing Lena’s necklace. Kara untangled their limbs to reach back and unclasp the necklace before giving it back to it’s rightful owner. Lena settled back into her arms as soon as the chain was secured and Kara didn’t realise just how much internal peace that would bring her.

 

__________

 

Hero practically launched himself from the floor into Lena’s arms when they finally got back and went to pick him up. He was a yappy, blurry, black fur ball and the pair couldn’t get hold of him through all the excitement. His tail was wagging so hard his whole body moved with it.

 

“See, I told you I’d bring her home,” Kara said.

 

Hero was ecstatic to be back home, running around the apartment and grabbing his favourite toys. Kara was ecstatic that she’d walked in to find a clean apartment with no dead assassin in it: she sniffed the air and there was a distinct hint of industrial cleaner.

 

“It feels good to be home.” Lena said. She turned around and threw her arms around Kara’s neck. “I’m so proud of you,” she whispered. That hit Kara square in the chest like a sucker-punch, her eyes stung and filled with tears. “What’s wrong?” Lena pulled away, clearly worried.

 

“Nothing,” Kara sniffled. “I just didn’t know how much I needed to hear that.” She said and quickly wiped her eyes.

 

Lena leaned up and captured her lips, “well, I’m always proud of you.” She said against her lips. “Do you understand the magnitude of what you did?”

 

“Yeah. Went to Hungary, got my girl back.” Kara said, simply.

 

“So now you’ve learnt what modesty is?” Lena teased, she scratched at Kara’s scalp. Kara dropped her head onto her shoulder, humming at the sensations.

 

“No, still the same arrogant, selfish asshole you fell in love with.” She joked, Lena laughed softly.

 

“You saved all those children from going through the same thing I did,” she pressed a kiss to her lips. “You told the truth no matter the consequences,” another kiss. “You saved my friends.” Kara pulled her closer. “You took down one of the most powerful organisations in the world,” another kiss. “You acted with integrity, compassion and patience. Not to mention, you did it all your own way. The Danvers way.” Kara grinned and Lena kissed her again.

 

“Well, I had some help.” Kara said.

 

“Oh, well I’ll just go and give them the same treatment.” Lena gestured to the door and went to leave, Kara grabbed hold of her hips and pulled her back.

 

“It was all me! Single-handed! No one else was there!” She insisted, Lena laughed and captured her lips once again. “You can just stay here and keep complimenting me, my ego loves it.”

 

Lena frowned, “I don’t think I’ve actually thanked you properly for saving my life.” Her tongue darted out and licked her top lip, Kara moaned and leant forward as Lena slowly walked backwards.

 

“No, I don’t think you have.”

 

“Huh,” Lena pouted. “We should fix that.” Kara lifted her and Lena wrapped her legs around her waist, their lips connected in a desperately passionate kiss. Kara carried her over to the stairs and Lena broke away.

 

“Is that a new coffee table?” Lena frowned, Kara looked over and realised they had in fact changed the coffee table. Well, it was probably for the best.

“You don’t want to know, it will only ruin the mood.” Kara said as she carried her up to bed.

 

__________

 

“No, come on Hero, move. I’m not doing this again, shift it.” Hero turned to look at her and settled back down in his spot, defiantly. The same spot he had occupied every day since they got back, by Lena’s side. Lena chuckled and stroked his head, “don’t encourage him!” Kara protested. Lena was already laid on her side of the bed arm curled around her pillow and Hero had nestled himself in front of her.

 

Kara had this same battle with him every night, she would get ready for bed and he would take Kara’s space. She moved his bed next to Lena’s side but he refused to actually lay in it, eventually she had to pick him up and place him on the floor.

 

Kara climbed into bed and snuggled up to Lena, “you wind him up.”

 

“I do, but look at that face,” she turned and looked into his big, brown eyes. “You’ve had practice in resisting him, I have not.” Lena defended.

 

“Do you want more practice?” Kara said quietly. They were facing each other now and Kara’s hand reached out to brush against her waist.

 

“What do you mean?”

 

“Move in with me.” There was a beat of silence, “officially? I love you, and I hate it when you leave, and I’d just really love it if I got to wake up with you every morning.” Kara said. It was a simple and truthful explanation: no big gesture, no flowery language, that wasn’t really their style, just Kara professing her love and making it clear that having Lena by her side every day was all she really wanted.

 

“You know this means that I’ll be able to resist your pout soon.” Lena grinned.

 

“Is that a yes?” She asked, matching Lena’s wide smile.

 

“Yes.” She pulled Kara into a deep kiss. “I don’t have much stuff to move though, everything I own is back there.”

 

“Does this mean I get to take you shopping and dress you up this time?” She teased.

 

“No way,” she snorted, “you wouldn’t get anything I like.”

 

“That’s not true!” Kara protested. “I know you like expensive, lacy underwear sets and lucky for you, that happens to be the new dress code for this apartment.” Lena giggled, “fortunately, I’m also an expert in lingerie so you are in very safe hands.” Lena shook her head, still laughing and Kara grinned.

 

She leant forward and kissed her, she nibbled on her bottom lip and swallowed Lena’s moans. Lena’s lips were soft and pliant, and their mouths moved perfectly against one another, she rolled them so Lena was on her back and pushed her shirt up so she had access to her warm skin. Her fingertips brushed Lena’s ribcage, she smiled and squirmed at the sensation. Lena’s fingers tangled in Kara’s hair and she tugged slightly, enjoying the groan that escaped her. Lena slipped her tongue into her mouth and grabbed Kara’s butt to pull her closer.

 

“You know, you’re basically wifey now.” Kara panted, breaking the kiss.

 

“I thought I already was.” Lena said outraged.

 

“Well, yeah, but now it’s solidified. Also, you have no job, so now you’re house-wifey. Don’t worry, I’ll show you where I keep the iron tomorrow.” Lena’s eyes widened comically, Kara laughed until she was hit in the face with a pillow.

 

__________

 

The months following the downfall of the World Killers were hectic for Lena and Kara.

 

Because Interpol were the largest international police organisation, they took over the whole case. They had agents from police forces and intelligence services all over the world temporarily seconded to the team, to work on their own missing person’s cases. It was one of the largest investigations in history, some of the World Killers decided to cooperate but most went into hiding.

 

Of course once the press got hold of this huge story, everything spun out of control. Talia’s face was splashed across every news outlet in the world and journalists hounded the investigation teams to get any scrap of information about the case.

 

The only fortunate point was that although they had their names, no one knew what the girls looked like and thankfully, they were able to get away and blend in throughout the world using aliases.

 

Kara quit her job with the CIA and the couple took some time away from everything. Lena read every article and public record she could about the case and Kara was desperately trying to find things for them to do that would take Lena’s mind off of things.

 

“Now, that everything is over, do you wanna find out more about yourself?” Kara produced the DNA kit she’d got for Lena for her Name Day.

 

Lena grinned and nodded, making grabby hands at the box. She registered the kit under Kara’s name, with her name still being in the newspapers she didn’t want it going on any kind of database.

 

It took a few weeks for the results to come back and Lena had almost forgotten about the whole thing.

 

“Hey, wanna find out where I come from?” Kara announced one morning, holding up a letter addressed to herself.

 

“Is that it?” Lena asked, eyes sparkling. Kara nodded, but held the letter out of her reach. Lena jumped up and tried to grab it but Kara refused.

 

“It’s addressed to me remember?” Lena whined and pouted, Kara leaned down and kissed her. “Just kidding, here you go.” Lena tore it open and Kara lifted her onto the counter while she read it. Lena’s eyes darted across the page taking in all the information, Kara rubbed soothing circles on her thighs. “So?” Kara was just as eager to know as Lena was.

 

“46% Ireland and Scotland-”

 

“Of course you are,” Kara scoffed with a shake of her head.

 

“What’s that supposed to mean?” Lena said.

 

“Remember your alias from the first night we met?” Kara raised her eyebrows.

 

“Oh yeah, the accent really does it for you, huh?” Kara closed her eyes and whined when Lena allowed a little Irish twinge to lace her words.

 

“So much.” She rested her head on Lena’s shoulder and groaned, “read the rest.”

 

“21% England, Wales and Northwestern Europe. 13% Germanic Europe, 10% Eastern Europe and Russia. 6% Norway, 2% Sweden and 2% Baltic states.” She reeled off, “you should do one of these, it would be interesting to know if you are actually more Scandinavian than me.” Lena raised her eyebrow and Kara laughed.

 

“Yeah, I’m not taking that bet.” Kara said. “Are you happy you did it?”

 

“Uh huh, it’s not much but it’s a start and at least I also know who my mother is. I don’t think that I’m ready for that just yet, but this was worth it.” Kara brushed her nose against Lena’s cheek and kissed her.

 

“Good.” She whispered. “Well, at least I know one thing,” she said as she pulled Lena to the edge of the counter and into her body.

 

“What’s that?” Lena asked looping her arms around Kara’s neck.

 

“You’re 100% European and I fucking love European chicks. I swear it’s the accent.”  Lena scoffed and rolled her eyes, “what?” Kara smirked.

 

“You’re gross.” Lena deadpanned, she pushed Kara away and slid off the counter, but Kara crowded her back. She leaned in and kissed her: it was hot and filthy, just the way Lena liked it. When she broke the kiss Lena was dazed and more than a little turned on. “Well, that was definitely French.” She murmured.

 

“Mhmm,” Kara captured her lips and nibbled softly. “Good to see all the practice in Annecy paid off.” Lena grinned and kissed her back.

 

“Wait a second,” she leaned away from Kara, “we never went to Annecy?”

 

“I know, I went to Annecy a couple years ago, I got stuck in a cabin in the Alps with three drop-dead gorgeous girls from Lyon.” Lena’s face was like stone, “well, they’d never met an American before and I’m… well me, so we found ways to pass the mphfff,” Lena pushed her face away and went into the living room. Kara barked out a laugh and chased her, she scooped her up bridal style and littered her cheeks and neck with kisses. “You’re so easy to wind up,” she grinned.

 

“Are you saying it’s not true?” She grumbled.

 

“Oh no, it’s true. One of the best-”

 

“Don’t finish that sentence unless you wanna stay on the couch tonight. I’ll happily stay with Hero, it makes no difference to me.” Kara laughed.

 

She sat down on the couch and pinched Lena’s cheeks, “you’re so cute when you’re jealous.”

 

“I’m not jealous,” Lena ground out.

 

“So cute.”

 

__________

 

They had been living together for a few months when it became clear to both of them that their happily ever after wouldn’t be as easy as they first thought.

 

It began when Kara woke up in the middle of the night and Lena wasn’t in bed. Pure panic set in almost immediately, her heart began racing and her breathing became uncontrollable. She sat bolt upright her eyes darted around the dark room, but she couldn’t locate Lena. What could only have been a few seconds felt like a lifetime in her head.

 

She heard the toilet flush and flopped back onto the mattress, she put her hands over her face and let out a deep breath. She flushed with embarrassment at how worked up she had become over nothing. Lena emerged a minute later and Kara pretended to be asleep because she was so humiliated at her body’s over the top reaction. Lena got back into bed and snuggled up to Kara, resting her head on her chest and throwing her leg over Kara’s hips. If she noticed that Kara was awake or that her heart was still racing, she never mentioned it; having Lena in her arms immediately soothed her.
