She ignored it, pushed it to the back of her mind and assumed that it was just a one-off, brought on by stress or lack of sleep. But there was nothing for her to be stressed about and her sleep schedule was better than ever, she ignored those facts and allowed it to spiral out of control.

 

Things gradually got worse. If Kara woke up and Lena wasn’t in close proximity, Kara panicked, but as soon as she could see her or touch her, she calmed down. She never told Lena about it: Kara knew it was stupid, the thoughts she had were completely irrational and she just needed to get over it.

 

One night, Kara woke up and Lena wasn’t in bed. She felt the distinct increasing of her heartbeat, her muscles twitched and trembled. She squeezed her eyes shut and listened out for movement in the bathroom, when she heard nothing she sat up trying to regain control of her breathing.

 

Lena quietly tiptoed up the stairs, glass of water in her hand. “Hey, did I wake you?” She whispered, she wandered around to her side and placed the glass on the nightstand, unaware of the sheer panic Kara was experiencing. Kara swallowed thickly and placed a hand on her chest, trying to calm her racing heart.

 

That was when Lena noticed.

 

“Darling, what’s wrong?” She quickly climbed into bed and knelt next to Kara. “Hey, breathe with me Kar,” she took Kara’s hand and placed it on her chest. It took a few minutes for Kara to match Lena’s breathing, once Lena was satisfied that her breathing was under control she gathered Kara in her arms. “It’s okay, you’re okay,” she murmured. Lena tucked her hair behind her ears and pressed kisses to Kara’s face.

 

“I’m sorry.”

 

“You don’t need to apologise, darling.” Lena clutched her close to her chest and rocked her back and forth. Kara focused on her heartbeat and allowed it to soothe her. Lena handed her the glass of water, Kara took a few sips before handing it back. Lena massaged her shoulders, digging her thumbs into the tense muscles in an attempt to loosen her up.

 

“What happened?” Lena said after a while, Kara was laying on top of her, face pressed into her neck and Lena was playing with her hair.

 

“Hmm?”

 

“What brought that on?” She asked, “did you have a nightmare?”

 

“Yeah.” She breathed. Not technically a lie, it’s a living nightmare. Kara buried it and the episodes escalated over the next few months, Lena didn’t know just how many Kara was experiencing as she kept the majority hidden. She also still didn’t know the truth behind Kara’s panic attacks, she still believed Kara was having nightmares.

 

It all came to a head when Kara woke up one morning and Lena wasn’t in bed and she wasn’t in the apartment either. “Babe?” She called, but received no answer. “Lena?” Hero came to greet her instead. Kara threw the comforter off and opened the bathroom door. No Lena. Her heart rate began to increase rapidly in her panic. She ran down the stairs but there was no sign of her. No note. No text and Kara was really beginning to worry.

 

They had been through a lot together over the past few months and while Lena seemed unaffected by the whole thing, Kara was struggling but she didn’t know why. She kept it all from Lena, she didn’t want to burden her with her problems. After the first panic attack, Kara saw how worried Lena was and she ended up getting really good at channelling her symptoms into something else. Her heart would still race, but she would hold her breath and did her nails into the palms of her hands in an attempt to keep her breathing under control.

 

When Lena wasn’t there, Kara became incredibly anxious that something would happen and she would be powerless to stop it. Rationally, she knew Lena could take care of herself, but she couldn’t seem to get her body to reason with her mind.

 

Kara sat behind the couch and curled up in a ball, Lena wasn’t here and she didn’t know where she was, she didn’t know when she would be back or whether she was okay. She dug her nails into her legs but couldn’t stop the overwhelming feel of panic.  

 

She didn’t hear Lena come in. She didn’t even know she was there until she felt Lena’s arms secure around her body. Kara knew Lena was saying something to her but she couldn’t process the words: her vision was slightly hazy and her ears were ringing. Lena pulled her hands away from her thighs, she ducked under one arm and clutched her hand close to her chest. Lena still wasn’t really sure how to deal with these kind of problems, this was all brand new to her and she’d never seen Kara in this kind of state before.

 

“I’m right here,” she said. “No one is going to hurt you, darling. You’re okay.” Kara knew she was there, could feel her heartbeat, could feel her lips against her cheek. She looked around and saw the takeaway cups and bags of food, she went out for breakfast. Then the crippling embarrassment set in and her cheeks burned.

 

She felt so stupid.

 

Once she’d refocussed her mind she immediately stood up, “I’m gonna take a shower.” She practically sprinted up the stairs to avoid the look of worry Lena was sporting.

 

“Kara, wait.” Lena followed her.

 

“I’m fine.” She shut the door on her, pressing her back against it, she took a deep breath and felt the thud of Lena’s forehead hitting the door on the other side. She shook it off and turned the shower on, standing under the cold water.

 

When she emerged Lena was sat on the bed, “what’s going on, darling?” Her tone was clearly full of concern, her eyebrows knitted together in a frown and she was wringing her hands. Lena was confused and hurt by Kara’s actions and she refused to talk to her about what was going on.

 

“Nothing, I just had a nightmare and I freaked out a little.” Kara brushed it off, Lena didn’t look convinced so Kara turned around to get changed.

 

Lena stood and wrapped an arm around her waist, placing kisses across her shoulder blades. “I know when you’re lying,” Kara sighed. “Darling, we promised no more secrets.”

 

There was a long pause, “I woke up and you weren’t here, I didn’t know where you were and I panicked.” Kara shrugged it off, “it was nothing.” She turned around and smiled at Lena.

 

“I’m sorry, I wanted to let you sleep in-”

 

“It’s fine, you went out to get breakfast. I was being stupid.” Kara brushed it off.

 

“I don’t think it’s stupid.” Lena said softly. She stepped closer, pulling Kara into a hug. “I’ll leave a note or send you a text next time.”

 

Next time.

 

Kara couldn’t understand why that brought so much fear to her heart, but she ignored it. Instead, she smiled and nodded, “good idea.” Kara had become very good at hiding her emotions from Lena over the past few weeks.  

 

But Kara’s anxiety gradually got worse and neither of them knew how to handle it.

 

__________

 

The story died down after a while and the news began reporting on other things. That was until the younger children were returned to their families and the media interest picked up again. The three women were eventually charged and then it got worse, the press continued to hound Interpol for information about the case. This was something that the world had never seen before and people were hungry for whatever scrap of information they could get.

 

Lena couldn’t escape the headlines. There were people who agreed that they were victims and then there were people who believed that they should all be locked up for the crimes they had committed, demanding to know everything that they had done. Others were terrified that assassins were going to break into their homes and slaughter them in their beds. That’s the problem with the press, they’re never unbiased they print whatever will make the most money, even if it instilled fear.

 

It all became too much for Lena, she was withdrawing. She was trying to break the conditioning that was ingrained in her brain and now she had to cope with the people telling her it was all her fault and she too deserved to be punished. They didn’t know where anyone was, that was part of the training and the girls were well hidden, but there was still a slim possibility that something would be leaked and they would be found.

 

Lena began obsessing over these news articles, reading everything that she could find; every minute of the day her nose was buried in her phone, searching for something that wasn’t there. It terrified her but she couldn’t stop, she had to know everything so she could plan for anything that could go wrong. She’d never felt so exposed or so vulnerable in her whole life.

 

Her own anxieties had gotten the better of her, and while Kara was struggling to combat her very visible panic attacks, Lena was suppressing her own symptoms. Lena had picked up the habit of biting the inside of her lip until it bled, pulling at the skin until it was raw and painful. She didn’t even realise she was doing it, her mind focussed on the article in front of her and then she’d feel the rush of liquid and her mouth would taste like copper.

 

Their individual issues had been gradually getting worse and neither woman could see a way out. Nor thought that just talking about it, expressing their thoughts and fears, would solve anything either.

 

Lena wanted time to be on her own but it had gotten to the point now where she couldn’t leave the room without Kara becoming panicked. She couldn’t leave the apartment because she was terrified that someone somewhere would recognise her, she didn’t even want to take Hero out for walks any more. Kara couldn’t cope with leaving Lena on her own, so Lena had to fight her fears in order for Kara to not be uncomfortable, but not without an argument first. That made her own anxieties worse and an ever growing resentment towards Kara.

 

It was a constant, vicious cycle.

 

Their lack of awareness and willingness to confront their problems drove a wedge between them. The affection stopped, the conversation stopped, it stopped being a relationship of love and became a relationship of convenience: they weren’t working together but they couldn’t function apart.

 

They were short, irritable and snappy with each other, even Hero could sense there was a divide. They argued about small stupid things, “I’m going for a walk.” Lena announced after a particularly nasty fight over who knows what at this point.

 

“I-I’ll come with you.” Kara said, fidgeting with her fingers.

 

“Kara,” she sighed, reaching up to rub her hands over her face. “I want to get away from this situation,” she gestured between them, “I need a break.”

 

Kara looked utterly broken and while Lena hated to see her this way she also knew that if she stayed they would have another argument and the cycle would continue.

 

She grabbed the door handle and Kara felt the familiar pounding of her heart, it was a Pavlovian response at this point. “Please don’t.” Kara’s voice had long since been void of it’s usual cheeriness, it was splintered, like all of the happiness had been stripped away.   

 

Tears stung her eyes, “Kara I don’t want to do this again.”

 

“I-I thought you didn’t want to go outside?”

 

Lena whirled around, “I don’t! Don’t you get it, I’m so desperate to get away from this place,” from you, “I’d rather go out there.” Kara hadn’t realised things had escalated that much, that Lena would rather do something that terrified her than stay here with her. “I’ve told you I’m going, that was the deal we made, right?”

 

“What if something happens to you?” Kara said.

 

“I can look after myself!” Lena yelled. Like you did in Hungary?

 

“I know you can, I just want to protect you!” Kara yelled back.

 

“So, we just stay in this apartment for the rest of our lives? Great.” She bit her tongue, holding back everything she wanted to say. The one thing they didn’t do was take cheap shots at each other, they’d done it in the past and learnt from their mistakes but that didn’t mean those thoughts weren’t on the tip of their tongues.

 

Lena turned and opened the door, “please Lee.” Kara was begging now and Lena could hear the desperation in her voice. She turned and saw the look on her face, the last thing she ever wanted to do was hurt Kara so she clenched her jaw and shut the door. She went straight into the kitchen without looking at her. “Thank you,” Kara murmured.

 

“Please, just stay over there.” Lena called and Kara respectfully obliged. While Kara sat on the couch, Lena sat in the corner behind the table, sobbing silently. Kara could see her through the gaps between the treads of the staircase and while it eased her anxiety, to see her in that state brought nothing but pain. She swallowed the lump in her throat and fought the urge to go over there, she didn’t want to make things worse.

 

Hero was beside himself, he looked between the pair whimpering softly before he finally took his own spot halfway between the two.  

 

Their saving grace was their love for each other. While things weren’t right they still had those strong foundations, an unyielding, powerful love. It was just hard to for them to realise that because it was buried so deeply under all their issues.  

 

The couple always slept tangled together, sometimes it wasn’t clear where Lena ended and Kara began. It was strange to think when they first started sleeping together Lena would leave as soon as Kara fell asleep to avoid the intimacy, and now they couldn’t stay away from each other even while unconscious. Even if they rolled away, there was always some part of them that was connected: whether it be their fingertips, legs tangled together, or a palm on any available skin. The point is, they were like magnets no matter how far they moved away they always found their way back to each other.

 

Waking up with Kara used to be the best part of Lena’s day, she would close the distance between them and bury herself in Kara’s arms slowly preparing themselves for the day. Lena would press kisses into Kara’s neck and tangle her fingers into hair to scratch at her scalp. Hero would climb onto the bed to greet them and eventually he would whine and badger them enough that they would have to get out of bed.

 

That had also changed, along with everything else recently.

 

Lena slept on the very edge of the bed and Kara would wait until she fell asleep and reach out to hold the hem of her shirt between her thumb and forefinger, things had become so bad that she could no longer fall asleep without physical assurance that Lena was still there. Kara was terrified to reach out and touch her, if Lena brushed her off Kara was sure that her heart would stop beating altogether. Lena hadn’t shied away from her but she also hadn’t initiated any physical contact recently, then again neither had Kara.

 

They were just two hollowing beings, existing rather than living.

 

Their mornings were also very different, Lena would mumble a “good morning” and then she would immediately get out of bed and start her morning routine.

 

It was awkward and lonely and it hurt. 

 

“Kara, I love you, but I can’t keep doing this.” Lena said one night. They were laid in bed and Kara was waiting for her to fall asleep when her statement cut through the darkness and stabbed her straight through the chest.

 

There was a long period of silence, Lena almost thought she was asleep. Then there was a whisper of acknowledgement, “I know.” Another period of silence, “I understand if you want to leave.”

 

Lena turned over, “I don’t want to leave.”

 

“What about earlier?” Kara said, clearly confused.

 

“Kara, I wanted a break from the arguing, I wanted to sit in the park and cool off because I didn’t want to have another fight. I was coming back.” She said.

 

“Oh,” there was clear surprise in Kara’s voice, she sighed. “This clearly isn’t working any more, ” Lena frowned. “I have no idea what you’re thinking or what you want.” Kara was just softening the blow as she waited for the inevitable, Lena would eventually realise that Kara could no longer make her happy.

 

“So, we went through all of that together and now you’re just gonna give up?” You gave up first. 

 

Then it all clicked in her brain.

 

She was experiencing all of this anxiety when Lena wasn’t around because she was afraid that Lena would make the conscious choice not to come back. Logically, she knew Lena could protect herself from any threats, but she used that as an excuse to avoid confronting her fear of abandonment. She actively pushed Lena away so it would hurt less when she eventually left.

 

“I-I, no, I’m not.” All of the realisations flashed through her brain. Kara had completely frozen and Lena didn’t know what to make of it.

 

“Kara, I don’t want to leave. I just want us to go back to the way we were.” She took her hands and Kara’s eyes snapped up. Lena faltered for a second and pulled away, Kara gripped her hands tightly. “I’m so confused and scared all the time, you won’t talk to me, you keep pushing me away but I can’t go anywhere because I’m so afraid that you’re going to have another panic attack.” Her eyes filled with tears. “I don’t know what to do, I don’t know how to fix this.” She was pleading with Kara, crying out for help but Kara didn’t know how to fix it either. “I want us back.” Her voice cracked and she let go of Kara to cover her face, her shoulders shook as she sobbed. Lena had cried so much recently that it was no longer something she found shameful or embarrassing, in fact it was the only way she’d found to vent.

 

Kara softened immediately and pulled her into a hug, the first hug they’d shared in weeks. “Hey, hey don’t cry,” she cooed. “C’mere,” she pulled Lena into her lap and held her together. “We can fix this, we’ll find a way, I promise.” Kara whispered into her hair.

 

Lena sniffled and wrapped her arms around Kara’s neck, “I’m sorry.” Kara shushed her softly. They laid back and Kara soothed her, she rubbed the back of her neck and her shoulders, “I guess happily ever after isn’t that easy for us.” Lena murmured.

 

“Is anything easy for us?” Lena let out a soft laugh.

 

“I guess not.” There was a long pause before Lena spoke again. “We’ll be okay though, right?” Her voice wavered slightly.

 

“Of course we will. I love you, and as long as we have that, what’s fractured can be fixed.” That night they fell asleep in each others arms, both knowing that they were over the worst of it, they had outwardly acknowledged that something was wrong; but now the hard work really begins. To an outsider, it would seem that it would be irreparable but they had a bond that wasn’t that easy to break: Kara kept her problems from Lena because she knew she was dealing with her own issues and she didn’t want to be a burden. If you asked Lena, she would say the same thing. And, they did it out of love instead of self preservation, but instead, that mentality caused them to hurt themselves and each other in the process.

 

They were complicated individuals, beautifully explosive together and volatile when they were apart. They both knew they worked better together, they were smart people and yet, they were both so fucking stupid sometimes.

 

The next day Kara announced that she was going back to therapy. Lena looked up from her phone, “I’ve thought about it. I’ve tried to deal with this on my own and you’re dealing with your own problems. I can’t fix myself alone, I need help from someone who knows what they’re doing.”

 

“Have you been to therapy before?” Kara nodded.

 

“Yeah, I started seeing my therapist a couple of months after I left the forces. I also went to group sessions with ex-service men and women.” She explained.

 

“Why did you stop going?”

 

“I felt like I hit a wall, I didn’t feel like I was getting anything out of it any more.” She took a deep breath, “but I made an appointment for later this week and if you’re willing to try, then I’m going to work hard to put this right.” Kara shot her a reassuring smile.

 

Lena stood up and threw her arms around Kara’s neck. “I’m proud of you.” She said.

 

“We’ll get through this.” Kara swallowed and pulled away, “Lena if this is going to work…”

 

“I know, I have to put in the work too,” she sighed and turned in Kara’s arms to stare at the phone glaring at her from the kitchen table.

 

“Why do you do it?” Kara asked, curiously. “They never have anything new to report.”

 

“Well, I don’t know that until I’ve read it, do I?” There was a hint of sarcasm in her tone, but it wasn’t malicious. “I like to be- have to be prepared, not just for myself, but for my friends.”

“But, if you live that way, how will you ever be happy?” Kara asked, not in a judgemental way merely out of curious concern.

 

“I won’t be,” she replied honestly. “Content maybe, but not happy.”

 

“You’re not happy?” Kara whispered.

 

Lena shook her head, “I don’t want to be happy.”

“Why?”

 

“Because every time I let myself be happy everything went to shit!” Lena exclaimed.

 

“And, this situation right here and now, you and me, this is better?” She said softly.

 

“This wasn’t all my doing.” Lena defended, Kara knew she was treading on dangerous ground now.

 

She held her hands up, “I didn’t say that. I take full responsibility for the part I played, but this isn’t living. We fought so hard to get here, the difficult part is over, this is the part where we get to spend the rest of our lives together.” Lena looked down but Kara caught her chin and lifted her head back up. “It’s okay to be happy and I promise that I will do everything in my power to stop anything that threatens that.”

 

“Okay,” Lena said.

 

“Good, because “contently ever after” is a shit ending.” She deadpanned, Lena laughed and brushed her lips against Kara’s. Kara moaned, quickly realising how much she missed it, she held Lena’s hips and melted into the kiss. Her teeth grazed Lena’s bottom lip and she recoiled with a hiss. “What’s wrong?” She furrowed her eyebrows.

 

Lena shrunk in on herself, Kara cupped her chin and gently pulled her lip down, she knew better than to berate her or coddle her. “That looks sore.” Lena nodded and Kara kissed her cheek, “stress and nerves related?” Lena nodded again. “I have some gel that will numb the pain and clear it up easily.”  

 

Lena tucked herself into Kara’s body, “I’m sorry.”

 

“Don’t worry, we both know what we’re dealing with now and we can work it out.”

 

__________

 

Kara had been going to therapy for a few months and the couple were starting to get back on track. They were communicating, they were affectionate and Lena had been trying her best to stop reading the news every second of the day. It was good.

 

There was only one thing that her therapist had advised her to do that Kara had refused. Each week he brought it up and each time, Kara said that it just wasn’t the right time. He wanted her to tell Lena the real reason behind her panic attacks, apparently it would, “lift a weight off of her shoulders”. Or Lena would be hurt and then she would get angry and then leave.

She berated herself for thinking so poorly of Lena, but it was hard. While things were getting better at home, there was still a battle that was going on in her head.

 

Lena asked how the session was each time she returned but she didn’t push her for any details. As far as Lena was concerned, those sessions were for Kara to have time for herself and if she wanted to talk about it Lena would listen, but if not, that was okay too because it wasn’t about Lena.

 

“I need to talk to you about some things.” She said out of the blue. Kara hadn’t expected to say it, it just burst out of her one night.

 

Lena looked over, “okay, what’s up?”

 

“Um, well,” Kara squirmed in her seat and Lena took her hand. “I thought my panic attacks and anxiety stemmed from the thought of losing you, but it really stemmed from the thought that you were going to leave.”  Lena squeezed her hand, “I pushed you away because I thought it would hurt less when you eventually got sick of me, but then I couldn’t bare the thought of letting you go and having you next to me calmed me down. I know it was confusing and I’m sorry for lying about it.” Kara was playing with Lena’s hands in her lap, she finally looked up and saw Lena’s reassuring smile. She wasn’t mad, she wasn’t upset, she was grateful.

 

“And, I’m sorry about the part I played the last few months. I bottled things up and I was controlling and I was suffocating you and I’m sorry.”

 

“You weren’t controlling, I know control. You would have let me leave, I made the conscious choice to stay because I love you Kara. I didn’t ever want to leave, I just wanted to know what was going on.”

 

“Thank you for not giving up on me.”

 

“Thank you for telling me.” She wrapped her arms around Kara. “I understand what’s going on now.” She rubbed Kara’s back and kissed her shoulder. Lena pulled away and pushed the hair away from her face, “what do you need from me?”

 

“Are you not angry that I didn’t tell you? We said no secrets.”

 

“I guess I’m a little hurt, but if you weren’t ready to talk about it I’m not going to blame you for that.” Lena kissed her cheek. Yes, it could have helped them solve things earlier, or it could have made things worse because Lena was in no fit state to receive that blow.

 

“The letter you left really struck a chord with me, because although I know you only left to protect me, there is a small part of me that questioned whether that was the truth. I don’t know, I’ve been alone for so long and then you came along and you became a constant and the possibility that you might not be a constant any more, it’s terrifying for me. And, I don’t want to rely on you or force you to stay, but I also don’t want to lose you.” Kara voice cracked towards the end. “I begged you not to go,” Lena sniffled and wiped her eyes.

 

“I know,” she whispered. “Tell me, I can handle it.”

 

“It’s like, I know now that we couldn’t have run but… it felt like you gave up. You made a decision that affected the both of us without me and I’m mad about it, but the thing that makes me the most angry is that you put yourself in danger. I thought about every horrible thing that could have happened to you, even though I tried to block it out, every scenario flashed through my mind in vivid detail. We’re supposed to be a team.” Lena nodded silently, she wiped Kara’s tears and cupped the back of her neck, making eye contact with her.

 

“I’m sorry,” she said sincerely. “We are a team and I’m sorry I made that choice, but I can’t go back and I can’t change it. I thought that she cared about me enough to leave you alone, but I was wrong. I promise that I will include you before making any decisions in the future that will affect the both of us.” Kara dropped her head onto Lena’s shoulder for a moment and let out a deep, shuddery breath; she could feel all of the animosity melt away. “I’m so sorry.”

 

“I forgive you.” Kara said, looking into her eyes. “I didn’t recognise that I was angry. I’ve felt anger before and it’s always been present and undeniable, I think I was so relieved to have you home that I didn’t realise I was still harbouring those feelings. Then, when things started to escalate I displaced that anger and it just got out of control.”

 

“Are you still angry with me?”

 

“No,” Kara said with no hesitation. “Now, I feel something different. We can’t go back to the way things were, too many factors have changed; but the one thing that’s stayed the same is that I love you and I know you love me too. So, we start from there and we build something new, we evolve from our mistakes into something better.”

 

“Do you still have the letter?” Kara nodded. “Can you get it for me?” Kara grabbed her journal from her desk drawer. Lena read through it again, she understood why Kara had that impression. “I didn’t mean to make it seem like our relationship was disposable, I just wanted to keep you safe. We worked so hard to get to this point, and I don’t just mean all the craziness of the last few months. I mean, that we have worked so hard to get to this level of communication and vulnerability with each other. There’s only one person in the world that I trust undoubtedly: with my story, my emotions and my heart. That’s you Kara. I promise to be honest with you if my feelings ever change and I’m sorry if I hurt you or made you question my feelings towards you.”

 

“I love you.” Kara said, burying her face in Lena’s neck.

 

“I love you too,” she replied. Lena continued to hold her, tracing patterns on her back. “Do you wanna burn the letter?” She suggested after a while, she felt Kara nod.

 

“I have something else to burn.” She picked up the journal.

 

“What’s that?”

 

“It’s just all my planning, notes and thoughts I had through the whole thing. Kinda like the ones I wrote while serving, but I don’t want to hold onto this one.” Kara held it out to her, “do you want to read it?”

 

Lena looked at the journal and then back to Kara. “Do you want me to read it?”

 

“There’s nothing in there that I’m ashamed of, but you don’t have to read it.” Lena didn’t want to be intrusive, but she also wanted to understand what Kara was going through and this was a first hand account.

 

She took the journal and gave Kara a reassuring smile. Kara moved to sit next to her, she put her arm around Lena in a gesture of comfort. She saw exactly how Kara figured it all out, mark one, two and three of the final plan and everything that Kara felt while she was at it.

 

I’m afraid that I’m making things worse, I don’t really know what I’m up against, Talia could already know I’m coming, she could be hurting Lena.

Lena might not even want me to come, she’s said multiple times that she doesn’t need saving and I’ve gone against her wishes again. I read the letter again, I know I shouldn’t have but right now it is a source of strength for me. I have everything I want.

I’m deeply, undoubtedly, irrevocably in love and I’ll do whatever it takes to get her back.

Lena turned into Kara’s body and rested her head on her shoulder.

 

I don’t think I’ve ever been this scared or nervous before. It’s not just my life on the line or Lena’s: Sam, Alex, Clark, Ava, Kate, their families, ALL of those women are at risk. I feel so much pressure, I have all these “what ifs?” running through my mind: what if I’m not smart enough? What if I’m not strong enough? What if I fail? What if she’s already (Kara had scratched out whatever she’d written so hard that Lena couldn’t decipher it, but she had a solid guess as to what it had said) I’m desperately trying to cling onto the present because if I think too much I’m sure I’ll break.

I miss her.

I wish I had Lena’s confidence, and her brain, and her tactical awareness. Actually, if I’m wishing for things then I wish for Lena back, for all this to be over and Big Belly Burger.

Reminder: don’t take food from Lena, she gives too much already, let her keep her kung pao chicken.

“I know the way to Kara Danvers’ heart is through her stomach.” Kara felt her face redden and her cheeks burn. “I know what I’m doing.”

 

“You don’t need to give me your food to get me to love you.”

 

“No, but it can’t hurt.” Lena shrugged and went back to reading.

 

I always struggled with an unrelenting feeling of anger, it’s been there since my parents were killed. I thought it had quelled when I finally discovered the truth and got justice for their death. Now, I can feel that raging fire towering inside me, I’m scared that it will consume me entirely. It’s happened before, I’ve hurt people I care about. The worst part is, I knew I was doing it, I knew I was hurting people but I didn’t care I just wanted to protect myself.

If I allow myself to become that person, all-consumed and numb to everything else, I become cruel, selfish, inhuman. I would be no different from Talia.

I think it’s strange that people find it so hard to talk about their good qualities and almost unthinkable to call themselves a good person. I am in no way perfect, I’m flawed, I have done things that some people couldn’t even comprehend, but I think the difference is that I try to be good. I joined the Marines not just for myself, but to protect people who couldn’t protect themselves. I joined the CIA because I thought I was doing the same thing.

What’s so wrong with saying you’re a good person? “Good” is one higher than “Satisfactory” on, like, every single survey ever created. Why is it so wrong to say oneself is slightly better than satisfactory? Well, unless you’re a really shitty person.

I’m trying to be better, everyday I’m trying to be better. I think that warrants one better than satisfactory.

I have to tell myself that I am good, not perfect, but good enough.

I am enough and I deserve to be happy. That’s how I will stay focused, because while I am “good”, Talia is definitely “extremely unsatisfactory”.

I close my eyes and I think of Lena and it hurts so much, but it keeps me present, keeps me balanced and focused. I think of only the good things and not the “what ifs?” And I think of everything we’re going to do together.

Lena wiped away her tears.

 

It’s time to go. I’m getting her back and I’m going to stop them from doing this to anyone else.

I am good enough.

 

Lena ran her thumb over the last sentence. “You are more than good enough.” Lena felt a kiss at the side of her head.

 

“Come on, let’s burn it.” She took Lena’s hand and they went into the kitchen. Kara produced her lighter and Lena went first, she lit the corner of that stupid letter and dropped it into the sink. Kara in turn, sparked the lighter and held up her journal.

 

“Wait!” Lena took it from her and tore out the last page, Kara gave her an odd look, “keep this one, as a reminder to be kinder to yourself. You’re feelings are valid, you’re not stupid for feeling the way you do and you are enough.” Kara gave her a small smile and took the book back, setting it alight. Lena stood in her arms and they watched the items burn.

 

Kara looked down at her, “this symbolizes a fresh start for us, a new beginning where we can be happy.”

 

“How many of those do you think we’ll get?” Lena asked.

 

“As many as we want, it’s our story.” Kara shrugged and leaned down to kiss her.

 

“How do you feel?” Lena asked when all that was left was ash and a few embers.

 

“Better, I’m glad I got it all out and I do enjoy playing with fire.” Lena kissed her jaw.

 

“Do you wanna order Big Belly Burger and cuddle on the couch?”

 

Kara groaned, “my God, I want nothing more.”

 

__________

 

“Are you sure you’re going to be okay?” Lena chewed on her bottom lip. They’d tackled the reasons behind Kara’s separation anxiety and now they were working on combating the physical symptoms: her therapist had told them to start small and work up to bigger things.

 

They started with Lena being out of eyesight for five minutes: she would hang out on the couch while Kara would fidget on the bed. In the beginning, Kara had to call out a few times and make sure that Lena was still there. From there they slowly increased the time apart and Kara was doing really well, but now it was time for the hardest test, Lena was taking Hero for a walk by herself and Kara wouldn’t know how long for.

 

“I’m nervous, but I’ll be okay. I need to do this.” Kara nodded her head as if she was trying to convince herself.

 

“We don’t have to do it today.”

 

Kara shook her head, “I want to, I can do it. Besides, you’ve got your phone right?” Lena held it up, “then I know I can call if I have to.” Lena searched her face for any signs of doubt and then pulled her down into a deep kiss. “I’ll be fine.” Kara said.

 

Lena kissed her once, twice more, “I love you and we’ll be back soon.”

 

“I love you too.” Lena and Hero left, the door clicking shut behind them.

 

Kara immediately felt that nervous bubbling in her belly, “it’s okay, everything is fine.” She reassured herself. Kara had worked hard to compile a list of steps that would help her handle these situations better. They were simple and adaptable to most situations.

 

“Step one: keep/regain control of my breathing.” Breathe in through the nose for three seconds and out through the mouth for three. She focussed on the air entering and expelling her lungs and when she was confident in her breathing, she counted backwards from thirty three times.

 

“Step two: state the facts.” She crossed her hands over her chest and rubbed her arms in a self-comforting gesture. “Lena went out for a walk. She has not left, she would tell me if she wanted to leave. Space is necessary and healthy for everyone. I am enough.”

 

“Step three: find something physical to seek solace from.” Kara took a few extra moments and then went upstairs and got changed into something comfortable: she swapped her t-shirt and jeans for a soft sweater, running shorts and a pair of odd socks because she still hadn’t sorted her laundry.

 

“Step four: find a stimulus to engage with and focus on.” She went downstairs, put her headphones on and got out her colouring book. Honestly, she’d laughed in her therapist’s face when he suggested she start colouring, she’d personally joked about being childish on a number of occasions but that was taking it too far. He encouraged her to try it and if she didn’t find it helpful, she could stop. Lena had gone to the store with her and they had found that there was an extensive collection of colouring books for adults. Lena helped her choose and then picked one for herself so she could join in, she’d also insisted they get a jumbo pack of pens and pencils and suddenly Kara didn’t find it quite so embarrassing any more.

 

The headphones were new as well, they were noise cancelling and when she put them on she could submerse herself in her own world. Kara put on some relaxing music, threw her feet up on the coffee table and focussed on the picture in front of her, only looking away from the page to select a different colour. It was so easy for her brain to just shut off, it wasn’t like drawing where she had to think and make decisions, the only thing she had to think about was what shade of purple she was going to colour the water this time.

 

Lena’s heart swelled with pride when she entered the apartment and saw Kara working quietly. Her mouth was open slightly and her eyes were fixated on the paper in front of her, she looked so serene and beautiful. The messy bun on her head: so cute. The soft, breathy exhales: precious. The mismatched socks, one with pizzas and one with love hearts: both fitting and fucking adorable.

 

Kara didn’t even realise the pair were back until Lena’s hand gently touched the inside of her calf, Kara looked up and met the happy expressions of both Lena and Hero (who Lena held back so as not to knock Kara in his excitement).

 

Kara shrugged the headphones off, “hi,” Lena whispered.

 

“Hey,” Kara smiled.

 

“Was everything okay?” Kara nodded and Lena beamed at her, “I’m so proud of you!” She kissed every inch of Kara’s face.

 

In the spirit of being honest, “I had a bit of trouble at the start but I went through the steps and I got through it.” That earned her even more kisses and Hero joined in, giving her an enthusiastic kiss on the opposite cheek.

 

“So. Proud. Of. You.” Kara couldn’t stop the wide smile, she sat down next to her and leant her head on Kara’s shoulder. “How do you feel?” She said eagerly.

 

Kara was more reserved than she expected, “I feel good, but also a little strange.”

 

“How so?” Lena brushed the little baby hairs away from her face.

 

“Like I’ve accomplished something huge, but also like I never should have let myself get into the state where having you take Hero out for a walk by yourself feels like an accomplishment. It should be a regular occurrence and therefore I still feel a little bit of shame and embarrassment.” Kara spoke honestly, still focussed on filling in the lines in front of her. It broke Lena’s heart a little to hear her talk like that.

 

“Darling,” Lena cupped the side of her head and pressed a kiss to her cheek. “I don’t know whether I even know the right words to say to make you feel better. But, what I do know is that mental health is fragile, complicated and takes the same amount of work to maintain as that six-pack.” Lena patted Kara’s stomach for emphasis and a small smile crept onto her face. “You can focus on how we got into this situation or you can acknowledge and celebrate the progress you’ve made. You don’t berate yourself every time you failed to hit a record in the gym. So, just as you would celebrate getting a new bench press PR, or whatever you jocks do,” Kara snickered, “give yourself some credit. Treat your mind,” Lena tapped her forehead, “with the same respect you treat your body,” she tapped her chest. “Baby steps, we do this right and you’ll be stronger than you were before.” She leaned in and kissed just below her ear. “Celebrate your wins,” she murmured.

 

“Anyway,” Lena said, “all this healthy, positive thinking makes my brain tired,” Kara let out a breathy laugh and Lena joined her. “I’m gonna take a nap, you coming?”

 

“Um, I think I’m going to stay here and finish this,” she pointed to her work in progress. Kara had a lot to think about, to process.

 

Lena gave her a small smile. “Okay, I’ll see you in a bit then.” She gave Kara one last lingering kiss, “you’ll show me when you’re done?” Kara nodded.

 

When Lena woke up, she found Kara cooking dinner. She wandered over and wrapped herself around her, “sleep well?” Lena hummed.

 

“Did you finish?” She asked, kissing the back of Kara’s neck.

 

“Uh huh, it’s on the coffee table.” Lena kissed her again and went to look at it.

 

“Ooo, a purple river this time?” She took the book back into the kitchen.

 

“It’s grape soda.”

 

“Ahh, the superior choice.” Lena said. “I’ll put it with the others,” each page had a perforated edge and Lena tore it out and attached it to the refrigerator with a dinosaur magnet. When Lena suggested they start that displaying their artwork, Kara had an inkling of doubt but now it was their tradition.

 

“We’re gonna run out of space soon.” Kara commented.

 

“I had a few ideas about that actually.” Lena stepped back to admire the masterpiece. “I was thinking we either use the board in the office or we put up a brand new one above the bed and put them there.”

 

“I like the second one,” she said. “Come and try this.” Kara beckoned her over, she handed Lena the spoon and waited for her reaction.

 

“Is-is that Krupnik?” Lena said, in awe.

 

“Yeah, Sam told me about it and I thought it’s something different and it seemed like a good memory for Sam so I thought it would be the same for you.” Lena looked at the floor and then crushed her in a tight hug, “oof! Good idea then.”

 

“What’s this for?” Lena asked.

 

“Celebrating.” Kara lifted her arm and Lena tucked into her side.  

 

“You’re amazing, have I told you that recently?”

 

“Have I told you that recently?” Kara replied.

 

Lena tilted her head sideways, “are we soft?”

 

“A little bit, but no one has to know.” Kara grinned, leaning down to kiss her. Kara served the soup and Lena set the table, “oh hang on,” Kara got back up and tossed Lena another bread roll. “You get two ‘cos you always gave yours away.”

 

“Thanks,” Lena snorted. They ate and made small talk but, towards the end Kara could tell Lena was thinking too hard about something, she could tell that she was biting the inside of her lip again. Before she was able to ask, Lena spoke up, ”what’s therapy like?” Kara wasn’t expecting that, she let out a deep sigh, “that bad?”

 

“No, not at all. It’s just a big question.” Kara paused for a moment, “I guess, it’s different for everyone. It’s hard work. For me, I almost gave up so many times because it was intrusive and intense and I felt vulnerable, but that was my choice. I made the choice to tell my story, and after a while it felt good. I enjoyed going, it was an hour a week where I could talk about whatever I want and there was someone there just to listen. We don’t always have deep conversations, sometimes it’s just like having a conversation with a friend.” Kara explained, “it’s hard to put into words because it depends on what you want out of it.” Lena was staring into her bowl, processing. Kara reached out and brushed her fingertips across her wrist, “are you thinking about going to therapy?”

 

“I don’t know, maybe?” She looked up, “I just- I can see how much it has helped you and I think it would be good to learn how to deal with everything that’s going on.”

 

“How are you processing it right now?”

 

“Processing?” She scoffed, non-maliciously, “I’ve just been pretending that it was an awful nightmare that wasn’t real.” She said, as if it was obvious.

 

“Well that’s…” she giggled softly, “I’m sorry, it’s just so you.” They both laughed. “In all seriousness, I think therapy is a good thing.”

 

“I don’t think I’m ready just yet.” Lena said.

 

“That’s okay too. Whenever you’re ready, I’ll support you.”

 

__________

 

“Hey, when was the last time we did something fun and not work related?” Kara asked. “When was the last time we went out on a real date?” She pondered, Lena looked down to where Kara was laying on her lap.

 

“Um, I don’t really know. I guess when we went out for dinner… last year.” She realised as she combed through Kara’s hair.

 

“We should go out and have fun together, doing something normal.”

 

“What did you have in mind?” Lena replied.

 

“Well, my first thought was something like bowling or mini golf.” Lena scrunched up her nose, a reaction she probably would have hidden at the beginning of their relationship. Kara chuckled, “yeah, we’re not that normal. My second thought: there’s an axe throwing bar near here.”

 

“Now you’re making sense.”

 

They decided to go that night, Kara held her hand throughout the journey. This would be the first time Lena went out without hiding behind a hoodie and dark sunglasses. They sat through the safety briefing, smiling and nodding along as if they weren’t both well versed in throwing sharp objects at targets, moving targets in some instances.

 

“Go on then Miss “I’ve been using an axe since I was five”, show me how it’s done.” Kara said, as soon as they were left on their own. Lena stepped up the the line, picked up the axe and pointed it at the target; she closed one eye and in one swift motion grabbed the handle with both hands, brought it behind her head and threw it.

 

Bullseye.

 

Kara let out a small squeak and Lena quirked her eyebrow. Lena was excellent at it, Kara on the other hand, was pretty terrible.

 

“I thought you’d be better at this,” Lena tilted her head and folded her arms.

 

“This is the first time I’ve held an axe, I’m not a fucking Viking or some kind of crazed lumberjack.” Lena snorted. “Give me throwing knives and I’d wipe the floor with you.” She argued.

 

“I reckon you’d make a good lumberjack,” she commented. “You’re throwing it too late and you keep dropping your head. Keep your eyes on the target and let go a fraction earlier.” Kara begrudgingly accepted the advice and hit the bullseye three throws later.

 

She whooped and swept Lena up in a hug. “Next time, it’s archery.” Kara said when they were leaving.

 

“Oh, I’m great with a bow!” Lena exclaimed.

 

“Did I say archery? What I meant was mini golf.”

 

It was a good night, they laughed and joked and they didn’t think about anything else but living in the moment. They talked about baby steps, but this was a huge step in the right direction for not just Lena but their relationship as a whole.

 

__________

 

A month later, Lena approached Kara and asked for her help. She’d seen how much happier Kara was in the past few weeks, how much progress she’d made.

 

“I think I’m ready…” She scratched the back of her head, “to try the therapy thing.”

 

“Amazing, I’m pleased for you.” Kara pulled Lena onto her lap, “it might take a little while to find a therapist that you’re comfortable with and that you like, but I’ll help you as best as I can.”  

 

Lena went through five different therapists, she had a phone consultation with each one and even decided that she wanted to try a few sessions but they didn’t work out.

 

They had hope for the latest one though, Lena enjoyed the phone consultation and she didn’t seem at all nervous when they were sat in the waiting room. Kara sat back and got her book out ready to wait until she was done; five minutes later and Lena left the room.

 

“Nope,” she said as she walked past Kara.

 

She stood and cleared her throat, “thank you for your time.” Kara said, she awkwardly waved and hurried after Lena. She found her softly banging her head against the car window, Kara slowly turned her around and she dropped her head against Kara’s shoulder.

 

“This isn’t going to work, is it?” She mumbled, defeated.

 

Kara cupped the back of her head, “it will but you can’t give up. It will take time, it will be hard but we’ll figure it out.” Lena sniffled and Kara held her closer.

 

When they got home, Lena silently curled up on the couch and clutched a cushion to her chest, Hero laid down next to her and wallowed empathetically. Kara frowned at her, Lena was giving up, she could see it. Kara kissed her head and went upstairs to make a call.

 

“Kara, it’s been a while, how are you?”

“I’m good, how are you James?”  

 

“I’m well, what can I do for you?” He said.

 

“Well, it’s not so much you. Your sister is a psychotherapist, right?”

 

“Kelly? Yeah, she specialises in trauma.” Kara got her number and thanked James.

 

Kara made two mugs of tea and handed one to Lena, “hey.”

 

“Hey,” Lena said into the mug.

 

“So, I have a friend and his sister is a psychotherapist who specialises in trauma.” Lena continued to stare at the contents of her mug. “Her name is Kelly Olsen and I really think you should give her a shot.”

 

“I’m starting to think that maybe this isn’t for me. Maybe I’m supposed to just figure it out myself,” she said.

 

“Everyone needs a little help sometimes, we just have to keep trying.” Kara reached out and took her hand.

 

“I don’t want to do this again.” Lena shook her head.

 

“It’s ultimately your decision but I have a good feeling about this.” Kara said.

 

Lena looked at her, the woman she trusted with everything. Kara tugged on her hand and gave her a soft smile, she wasn’t just doing this for her, she was doing this for them. “Well, you haven’t been wrong yet.” Kara beamed and leaned up to kiss her.

 

Kelly passed all of Lena vigorous tests and Kara went with her for a the first session. “Lena, can you tell me a little bit about what you want out of these sessions?” Kelly asked.

 

“Um well, I-I don’t really know. The past year has been… life-altering and I’m still not sure how to process everything that’s happened.” Lena said. “I guess, I also want to find some peace of mind. I want to learn how to process my feelings so that I don’t hurt those closest to me.”

 

“I think I can help with that.” Kelly gave her a reassuring smile.

 

__________

 

“I was thinking-”

 

“That’s dangerous,” Kara joked.

 

“Wow. It was a really good idea as well,” Lena said, crossing her arms with a frown.

 

“Wait, no, I’m sorry. Tell me the idea.” Kara said.

 

“No, you ruined it.” Kara squeezed her sides and tickled her.

 

“Tell me!”

 

“You’re such a cheater!” Lena yelled, flailing her limbs in an attempt to get Kara to stop. Kara grabbed a rogue fist and foot, Hero barked along with the commotion. They rolled off the couch and landed on the floor with a thud and multiple grunts, Lena pinned her to the floor. “Get her Hero!” Kara spluttered and struggled against Lena’s hold as Hero licked her face.

 

Lena smiled triumphantly and let Kara go. “You two are the worst,” she groaned. They got up eventually, “so are you gonna tell me?”

 

“Oh yeah, I was thinking we could go back to Midvale and clean up the house properly.” Kara froze, “only if you want to?” Lena added quickly, she squeezed Kara’s hand.

 

Kara shook herself out of the trance, “I’d really like that.”

 

They pulled up to the house a week later, the atmosphere was much better this time; for one they’d brought Hero and he was zooming around the front yard. Lena took Kara’s hand and they walked up to the porch, “you wanna do the honours?” Lena gestured to the door, cheeky grin on her face; Kara stuck her tongue out and dangled the keys in her face.

 

Kara wandered around her childhood home while Lena unpacked the car. “Tea?” She said, offering Kara a mug, she smiled softly and accepted the warm drink. They were standing in the living room, one of the only rooms they’d managed to clear the last time they were here.

 

They sat on the couch and could hear Hero’s claws clicking against the wooden floors as he explored his new surroundings. “I loved this place so much as a kid. I used to have sleepovers with my friends in here, my dad would make these huge blanket forts that we would sleep in and my mum would make the best chocolate chip cookies.” Kara sighed at the memory.

 

“We could do that one night?” Lena suggested.

 

“Can you even bake?” Kara joked.

 

“Afraid I’ll be better than you?” She quirked her eyebrow in a clear challenge.

 

Kara narrowed her eyes, “you don’t have a clue, do you?”

 

“No,” Lena whined. “I’ve had a deprived life,” she sighed dramatically. “Teach me?” She pouted.

 

Kara chuckled, “of course I will.”

 

“You know what I realised?” Lena said, she put her mug on the coffee table.

 

“What?”

 

“I never saw your childhood bedroom last time we were here.” She said it nonchalantly.

 

Kara looked at her and narrowed her eyes, “don’t you dare.” Lena smirked, her eyes full of mirth and mischief. She took off out of the room and up the stairs, “get back here!”

 

Lena got there before Kara could stop her, it was easy to identify as the door had a large wooden “K” nailed onto it. Kara’s bedroom walls were a pale shade of blue with white furniture: a single bed, fairy lights wrapped around the frame, a chest of drawers, a desk in the corner and a bookshelf. There were a few items of clothing strewn across the floor, a bookmark marked the page of a novel that was never finished, a school science project abandoned on the desk. It was like time had just stopped, suddenly and without reason and of course it had for Kara. That was the day everything stopped and Kara was forced onto a new path, her old life abandoned and in search of a place in another.

 

The air was solemn for a moment and then, “you were a fan of the Backstreet Boys?” Lena teased, noting the posters on the wall.

 

“Oh, don’t pretend like you know who they are.” Kara said with a roll of her eyes, they both chuckled.

 

Lena wandered around the room, Kara’s martial arts uniform was draped over the end of her bed, “what belt did you reach?”

 

“I was just about to go for my brown belt. I eventually finished it, but it took longer than I expected.” The wall above the desk was covered with all of Kara’s achievements: medals, certificates and photos.

 

“You were so cute.” Kara had the same, infectious grin on her face in every photo. “And crazy talented.” Kara had medals for karate, judo, swimming, track and soccer.

 

“Were?” She scoffed. “We both know I’m fucking precious.” That outburst left the pair in a fit of laughter.

 

They spent the night in that room, dragging the mattress from the guest bedroom and laying it on the floor. Hero thought it was great fun, he could run over the pair, worm his way in between them with little to no effort at all. Lena hadn’t noticed the ceiling until Kara switched the light off that night, the ceiling was lit up with a sea of glow in the dark stars. “Oh god, I forgot about those.” Kara groaned, closing her eyes and turning to bury her face in the pillow.

 

Lena mindlessly brought a hand up to comb through her hair. “What are they for?” She asked, still staring up in awe.

 

Kara turned to face her slightly, “I suffered from nightmares as a kid and my dad put these up as a less embarrassing night light.” She explained.

 

“I like it.” Lena said softly.

 

Kara rolled and cupped Lena’s face. “You know, thirteen year old me would be freaking out right now. I never had a girl up here.”

 

“What, you mean Kara “Womanizer” Danvers never made out with a girl in her bedroom?” She teased.

 

“I’m not a womanizer!”

 

“Yes, you are.” Lena smirked, she threw her leg over Kara’s hips and climbed on top of her. She ran her hands up Lena’s bare legs and played with the hem of her sleep shorts.

 

“Okay, I was. But, I’m not any more.” Kara pulled her down into a kiss.

 

The next morning Kara decided she wanted to tackle her parent’s study. The floor was littered with papers, the twin desks had been riffled through and the drawers pulled out, the contents tipped onto the floor. Lena gathered up the notes and papers while Kara fixed the desks, putting everything back together again.

 

She looked up and saw Lena shuffling through the papers, clearly she was fully engrossed in what she was reading. Kara held her shoulders and guided her back into the chair, she’d found her parents research into cold fusion. Kara kissed the side of her head, but Lena didn’t notice, too focussed on the words in front of her. Kara continued tidying up and occasionally looked over to see Lena mouthing the words in front of her.

 

When she was done, she leaned back in the chair and put her hands on her head. “You done nerding out?”

 

“Uh huh,” Lena said, it was high-pitched and strange.

 

“How was it?”

 

“Mind blowing.” Lena murmured, “your parents are so smart.”

 

“Yeah.”

 

“How did you…?” Lena trailed off.

 

Kara slowly turned to face her, “were you gonna ask how I turned out like this?”

 

“Well, no. I just- two smartest scientists on the planet,” Lena held up one hand, “child who can’t get her own shirt buttons undone.” Lena held up the other hand.

 

“I was tired!” Kara exclaimed.

 

Lena giggled and tugged her closer by her belt loops, “I’m kidding.” She stood up, “you know I think you’re incredibly smart.” Lena kissed her cheeks and forehead, “but did you never want to follow on from your parents?”

 

“Not really, that was their thing. I was good at science but I wasn’t that passionate about it.” Lena nuzzled her neck and pressed soft kisses there.

 

“You were a jock,” she snickered.

 

“I was not a- yeah, I was a bit of a jock.” Lena ran her hands up Kara’s arms and squeezed her biceps, “okay, still a bit of a jock.” She admitted.

 

“You wanna make cookies this afternoon?” Lena cooed.

 

“Jocks don’t make cookies,” her voice low and gruff. “We get our trophy wives to make them for us.”

 

“Oh great, she can make me some too.” Lena patted her shoulder and moved past her.

 

“Babe, you’re the trophy wife!” Lena left the room with a flick of her wrist. “Wifey? Are you making them?” She called. She grumbled to herself and marched into the kitchen, she was met with a fistful of flour to the face and a smirking Lena perched on the counter. Kara squeezed her eyes shut and blew out a breath, a cloud of flour expelling with it.

 

Lena sniggered, “you look like Casper the friendly ghost.”

 

“Oh, I have the same complexion as you, you mean?” Lena’s mouth dropped open in outrage, “you do realise that I’ll get you back for this?” She narrowed her eyes and bracketed Lena’s hips with strong arms.

 

“Go on then,” Lena said, she handed Kara the bag of flour, Kara just smiled and dumped the rest of the bag over her head. Lena gasped and clenched her jaw, “did you just waste all the flour we were supposed to use for the cookies?”

 

“I have another bag of flour for the cookies,” she grinned.

 

Lena sighed and the flour shifted on her head. “I’ll let you have that one because I know you’re fragile right now.” She tilted her head and the flour dropped from her head to her lap, she then crushed Kara to her in a hug.

 

“This isn’t letting it go!” Kara said squirming, Lena rubbed flour all over her back, hair and neck. They really were like children sometimes and it boiled down to the fact that they had both missed out on having this kind of childish fun. They were carefree, jovial and they didn’t mind clearing up whatever mess they made.

 

“What do you mean? It’s just a hug,” Lena said, ruffling her hair. Kara tried to push her off and Hero came to investigate the noise and rolled in the flour on the floor. Lena snorted and let her go, Kara looked down and saw Hero stood, wagging his tail, covered in a layer of flour.

 

Kara groaned, “oh great,” she said holding her hands up. Lena giggled and covered her mouth with a flour coated hand. “This isn’t funny.”

 

“It is.” She sniggered. Hero barked, “see even Hero agrees.” Kara could never stay mad at her, she tugged Lena off the counter and gave her a dry, powdery kiss. They both grimaced slightly.

 

“Worst kiss ever.”

 

“Agreed,” Lena said, dusting the remaining flour from her clothes. Lena dusted Kara off as well and sent her off to the shower while she cleaned up the kitchen and Hero.

 

Kara came back down to a clean kitchen and flour-free dog, they eventually made cookies without starting another food fight. “Have you ever done anything like this before?”

 

“Baked cookies?” Kara hummed, “no, I’ve never done any kind of baking.” She was balling up the cookie dough to place on the tray, “it’s kinda gross.” Kara laughed and looked at her sticky hands.

 

“It’s not always this messy.” Kara was holding her hips and looking over her shoulder, talking her through the process. Lena washed up and they dragged the mattress down the stairs and into the living room, creating a blanket fort while they waited for the cookies to cool down. Hero “helped” by running in and out and jumping on the sheets.

 

They crawled inside and Kara picked a movie to watch, they ate cookies, laughed, joked and played with Hero. Kara may not have had the picture perfect life, but she had everything she needed now.

 

“As good as your sleepovers?” Lena asked.

 

Kara looked down at Lena and then over at Hero. “Nah,” Lena looked up, “it’s much better.” Kara cupped her chin and kissed her.

 

They had cleaned up the rest of the house and the only place left was Eliza and Jeremiah’s bedroom. Kara had avoided it all week but she knew she would have to face it some time. “Come on, I think it will be good for you.” Lena opened the door and guided Kara inside. The room itself was untouched, just as Kara’s had been, but it was still filled with memories of her parents.

 

Kara tentatively stepped forward and sat down at her mother’s dressing table, Lena sat on the bed behind her. Kara reached out and brushed the photo: her mother cradling her on the day she was born. Her fingers curled around a perfume bottle, she held it to her nose and inhaled deeply. She hadn’t smelt her mom’s perfume since she was a child and it brought back every fond memory Kara had, she sprayed some on her wrist and stood back up.

 

When she went over to bookshelf she easily found her favourite book, she went and sat next to Lena on the bed. “My parents bought me this for my first birthday,” she flicked through the pages. The book was In excellent condition to say it was thirty years old, the pages had browned and the spine was cracked in multiple places, but it had clearly been taken care of while Kara was young and it stayed here, untouched, for decades. Lena watched her hands tremble as she opened the book and turned the first few pages.

 

In her mother’s elegant handwriting:

 

“So come with me, where dreams

are born and, and time is never planned.

Just think of happy things and

your heart will fly on wings, forever, in Never Never Land!”

 

Happy Birthday sweetheart!

May your life be filled mischief and adventure!

All our love,

Mom and Dad

 

Kara ran her thumb over the message, “do you think they’d be proud of me?”

 

“Absolutely.” Lena said, without thought or hesitation. She looped an arm around Kara’s waist and kissed her cheek.

 

“I should have done this sooner,” Kara said.

 

“Maybe. Or maybe you did it at the perfect time. When you were ready to accept it, when you were emotionally able to process it.” Kara smiled and turned to look at her, she leaned in and kissed her gently. She looked over at the closet, “go on. I’ll be here if you need me.”

 

She went into to her parent’s closet and brushed her fingers over the fabrics of their clothing. She opened her fathers storage boxes, he had a vast amount of cuff links and Kara used to help him pick out which ones to wear for all the events he used to go to. She moved onto the next one and a small gasp escaped her when she realised her father’s watch was still in it’s case. She’d always assumed that he was wearing it when he died, she picked it up and turned it over.

 

Here’s to fifteen more years

All my love.

She went back into the bedroom to find Lena still sat on the bed. “Hey, what did you find?” Kara fiddled with the watch strap and held it up to show her.

 

“My dad’s watch, it was an anniversary gift from my mom, he always wore it.” Kara perched on the end of the bed.

 

“Have you tried it on?” Lena rested her chin on Kara’s shoulder, she shook her head. “Well, go on.” She urged. Kara draped it over her wrist and tightened the strap, it fit her perfectly.

 

“I never had anything of my dad’s before,” Kara said. “What do you think?”

 

“It suits you.” Lena kissed her cheek.

 

Kara spent the day clearing out her parents closet, she took her father’s cuff links, a few of his t-shirts and her mom’s perfume. The rest of their clothes they boxed up ready to drop off at good will. Lena made sure that they took all of the photos at the house, insisting that Kara owed it to herself to have pictures of her family.

 

__________

 

Lena gnawed on her bottom lip as she scrolled through her phone, it was late and Kara had fallen asleep hours ago. Lena had a million things running through her mind and she couldn’t shut everything off.

 

Kara stirred and rolled over, “what’re doin’?” She screwed her eyes shut to avoid the artificial light.

 

“Sorry,” Lena murmured, “I’m just reading stuff.” Kara rested her head on Lena’s stomach and she felt Lena’s fingers scratch her scalp.

 

“What kind of stuff?”

 

“My Mom wants me to get in touch.” Kara’s head shot up.

 

“Wow, okay, not what I expected.” She sat up properly, “did she post another letter?” Lena nodded and showed her.

 

My darling Lena,

I can feel that you’re closer than ever and, for once, I feel like I’m not delusional, like everything I’ve ever wanted may finally come to fruition.

I’ve never felt so hopeful yet afraid.

I want nothing more than to see you again one day, but I understand why that may be difficult considering the circumstances.

Just know that I love you, I miss you and you will always have a home here.

All my love,

Your Mother.

 

Kara could tell she was biting the inside of her lip. “Babe,” she cupped Lena’s neck and pressed her forehead against her temple. She reached out and took Lena’s phone gently, allowing her the opportunity to protest if she wanted, she locked it and placed it on the night stand away from her.

 

“I saw the way you were when we went back to Midvale and… am I being stupid? Is it cruel of me to wait this long?” Lena’s voice was barely above a whisper, she almost thought Kara hadn’t heard her.

 

Kara kissed the side of her head and cleared her throat slightly. “It’s true, I would do anything to see my parents one more time. But, you’re not being stupid, you’re just protecting yourself.”

 

“So, I am being cruel.”

 

“I wouldn’t say cruel, but it’s clear she knows, or expects that you’re still alive and that you know who she is. It’s probably just confusing for her, and she’s waited so long to see you again, she’s probably excited and doesn’t want to wait any longer.” Lena sighed and rubbed her hands over her face. “But, you don’t need to feel any pressure whatsoever, it’s your decision. And, if your mom is anything like you, she definitely would have found you by now,” Lena chuckled lightly, “that letter is just her way of reaching out and letting you know that, whenever you’re ready, she’ll be waiting.”

 

“I don’t know what to do.” Lena murmured.

 

“There’s nothing we can do right now, but you need to sleep, so lie down and get comfortable.” Lena did as she was told and Kara moved so they were sharing the same pillow. “Talk to me.” she whispered. Kara nuzzled her cheek and brushed her lips against her skin in a gesture of comfort.

 

“I don’t know what to say.”

 

“What’s holding you back? What’s your biggest fear when you think about meeting your mom?”

 

“She’s spent her whole life making sure that I would feel included. She will have this idealistic view of what I’m going to be like, it would be impossible for her not to imagine what I’m like. I just believe that the fantasy will be better than reality and I’m scared that I can’t live up to that.” Kara kissed her cheek and cleared her throat.

 

“Well, you’re right, the fantasy will always be better than reality. That’s what a fantasy is: imagining something that is impossible, that doesn’t mean that the reality isn’t good as well. If she’s reaching out she’s clearly read the news-”

 

“Exactly!” Lena exclaimed, she sat back up again.

 

“Whoa, hey. Relax for me,” Kara rubbed her shoulders and coaxed her back down, “what I was going to say is, she’s read the news and she still wants to meet you, because she loves you, because you’re her daughter and you were taken from her.”

 

“She doesn’t know everything that I’ve done though.”

 

“She won’t interrogate you about every single thing you’ve done in your life before you’re allowed through the door. I can guarantee she’ll want a hug before your life story. It’s also your story to tell, if you don’t want to tell her, you don’t have to and I’m sure she’ll respect that decision.” She pulled Lena closer. “Besides, the fantasy is just that, it’s not real. Right now, you’re just an undefinable image in her head, having you back will exceed any and all expectations she has.”

 

“Will you come with me?”

 

“Uhh, try and stop me.” Lena chuckled, “are you going to be able to sleep?”

 

“Probably not.” She admitted, even though Kara’s words calmed her slightly, she was still wound up.

 

“I could read to you?”

 

“I’m not a child.” She regretted the statement as soon as it left her mouth. “I’m sorry, darling. I’m so sorry.” Lena rubbed her tired eyes. “I didn’t mean it.”

 

“I know,” Kara said softly, she leaned up on her elbow and combed her finger through Lena’s dark tresses. “If you think about it, it’s really no different from listening to an audio book.” she hummed, “remember when you said you like hearing the sound of my voice?”

 

Lena groaned, “I hate it when you listen to me.” Kara laughed and climbed out of bed, she disappeared down the stairs. Lena sat up when she heard Kara making a lot of noise downstairs, “you better not be making a mess, I just cleaned up today!” She called.

 

There was a loud bang quickly followed by, “ow, shit!” Kara reappeared a moment later, limping up the stairs. “I stubbed my toe,” she pouted. She held up the copy of Peter Pan they’d found in Midvale.

 

“Darling-”

 

“You can’t reject my idea now, babe. It’s my childhood book.” She pouted again, her eyes filled with sadness.

 

Lena could never think of hurting Kara in such a way. “Okay,” she said.

 

Kara’s eyes lit up. “Great!” Kara got back into bed, she held her arm up. “Well, get over here then,” she looked at Lena expectantly, she shuffled over and Kara draped her arm around her. “Good, now shut up and let me take you to Neverland.” Lena snorted.

 

“Are you going to do all the voices as well?” Lena said.

 

“I can’t tell if you’re mocking me, nor do I care, of course I’m going to do all the voices.” Hero got up on the bed to listen to the story. Kara got four chapters in before Lena fell asleep.

 

__________

 

Lillian Luthor lived in a huge almost-mansion in up-state New York. Kara and Lena spent the best part of a day driving to the city. Lena decided that she wanted to go but she didn’t want to let her mom know she was coming in case she ended up letting her down.

 

“Are you excited?” Kara said.

 

“I’m terrified.” Lena bit on her thumb.

 

“It’ll be okay. No pressure, remember.” Kara placed her hand on the inside of her knee and squeezed lightly. Lena raised an eyebrow when Kara didn’t remove her hand right away. “What? We’re on the highway, I don’t need it for anything else.”

 

They made it to the hotel late in the night, Kara was so tired from the driving, she passed out almost as soon as they got into bed. Lena asked Kara to put her phone in the safe so she couldn’t obsess over it… and it made absolutely no difference whatsoever, she was still up half the night worrying.  

 

Kara stumbled out of bed at around 3am to use the bathroom and Lena pretended to be asleep. When she got back into bed, she snuggled up to Lena and threw an arm over her waist, Lena just hoped she’d fall back to sleep soon. “So, how long have you been awake?” Her voice was low and rough, Lena fought the shiver threatening to run through her. Lena stayed silent, foolishly thinking she could get away with it. “You know I can tell when you’re awake,” I only spent weeks waiting for you to fall asleep. Lena continued to fake it, trying to keep her breathing steady, “don’t make me do it, babe.” No response. “Right, fine.” Kara took a deep, exaggerated breath and blew a raspberry into her neck.

 

Lena recoiled and pushed Kara’s face away, “okay, okay I’m awake.”

 

“See that wasn’t so hard, was it?” Lena grumbled something unhelpful. “Aww, come here grumpy.” Kara rolled her onto her back and reached over to switch on the lamp. Kara could see that her lips was rather swollen, she reached up and gently pulled her bottom lip down and fought the urge to gasp when she saw the indentations Lena’s teeth had made as she tore at the skin inside her mouth. “Babe-”

 

“I’m sorry,” Lena said quickly.

 

“Shh, it’s okay. I’m not upset, I just want to make sure you’re alright.” Kara caressed her cheek.

 

“I’m- I don’t know.”

 

“It’s okay to be nervous, you’re not alone. I think even if you had led a saintly life you’d still be nervous about meeting your mother.” Lena hummed, Kara nuzzled her neck. “I’m nervous too.”

 

“Don’t say that! Why are you nervous?”

 

“Lena! I’m meeting the in-laws,” Lena rolled her eyes. “I’m serious! What if she doesn’t like blondes?” Lena huffed out a small laugh, Kara grinned and kissed her. “You want a distraction?”

 

“Please.” Kara swept her up bridal style.

 

“Babe, we’re in the city that never sleeps, so if you can’t sleep we won’t sleep.” Kara placed her down in front of their bags, “so wrap up and we’ll go find something fun to do.”

 

The pair wandered through the bright city lights, hand in hand. They bought pizza and churros from street vendors, Kara kept her close not letting her go for longer than a few seconds. The pair wandered through Times Square that was still bustling even at the late hour, Kara circled her arms around Lena and nuzzled her cheek. “We don’t have to stay, no one knows you’re here. We can go home right now, if that’s what you want?”

 

“I want to stay, I think I can do it.” Lena said, she pressed her cheek against Kara’s shoulder and closed her eyes when she felt Kara kiss her forehead.

 

“I know you can.”  Kara whispered against her skin.

 

They decided that they were up and they might as well drive to the house now so Lena could take the time to compose herself. They sat in the car and waited, it was up to Lena to make the first move and Kara had parked a little ways down the street so they didn’t look suspicious.

 

Lena didn’t get out of the car and she didn’t move, she just stared straight ahead. It must have only been ten minutes before they saw a car pulling out of the drive and they caught a glimpse of a female driver.

 

“I reckon that’s her,” Kara said, “at least you can relax a bi…” Kara trailed off when she turned and Lena wasn’t in the passenger seat.

“Where did you…” Her eyes darted around the car and she located Lena curled up in the footwell behind the drivers seat. She had her arms tucked over her head to hide her face. “How do you move so quickly? You made absolutely no noise whatsoever. Honestly, it’s impressive.” Kara grunted as she climbed awkwardly onto the back seat, “you gonna come up here?”

 

“No.”

 

“Come here, babe.” Kara pulled her arms away and stroked her hair, she bent down and whispered in her ear. “It’s just me baby, there’s no one here but us.” Kara coaxed her head up and caressed her pouty, tear-stained face. Kara took her hand and pulled her up onto the back seat, Lena sat between Kara’s legs leaning back against her body.

 

“I’m a coward.” She whispered.

 

“No you’re not. You’re the bravest person I know.” Kara said, her voice soft and genuine. “This is just a blip.”

 

“I think it’s because I have to be myself and I’ve only ever had to do that with you outside of the World Killers. It’s hard to not use a persona.” Kara littered her neck with kisses. “I’ve only ever played a character, I’m scared to be myself.”

 

“Well, I fell in love with you, not the character you played and you’re my favourite person remember.” Kara reached for her bag in front of them and pulled out her headphones, she placed them on Lena’s head and she turned back to look at her quizzically. Kara pulled her back and started the music. Lena played with her fingers until eventually her body became heavy, her arms limp and her breathing slowed right down. “And, now you’re asleep.”

 

Lena woke up a few hours later, stretching languidly. She pushed the headphones off and turned to face Kara, sleepy and sluggish she clung onto her. “Are we still in the car?” Kara hummed in affirmative and Lena groaned.

 

“Do you want to go?”

 

“No,” she sighed. “I just need a minute.”

 

Kara kissed the side of her head, “okay, well I need to get out and stretch, I have cramp in places I didn’t know I could get cramp.”

 

“I’m sorry, darling.” Kara waved her off.

 

“I’d have pushed you onto the floor if I was that bothered.”

 

Lena giggled, “charming,” Lena pinched her cheek.

 

“I’m not known for my charm.” Kara said, she opened the door and all but fell out, she stretched out her legs, arms and shoulders, shaking out the pins and needles. She groaned when her joint cracked with satisfaction.

 

“Feel better?” Kara bent over and touched her toes and then raised her arms above her head.

 

“So much better. Come on, you’ll feel better too.” She held her hand out and Lena took it, climbing out of the car. Lena joined her, stretching her tense limbs. Kara cleared her throat, “so, now you’re out of the car, do you wanna get a little closer maybe?” Kara nodded towards the house.

 

“Kara Danvers, did you get me out of the car on false pretences?” Lena narrowed her eyes.

 

“Not at all, I seriously think my spine may be permanently stuck in an ‘S’ shape.” Kara stretched her back for emphasis. “Sooo,” she nodded to the house again.

 

“Come with me?”

 

“Always.” Kara locked the car and took her hand, “ready?” Lena nodded briefly. They walked up the drive, Kara just a little further in front, leading the way. “Do you want me to knock?” Lena nodded, trying to swallow the lump in her throat. Kara pulled her closer and gave the door three sharp knocks, “I love you,” she whispered.

 

The door opened and they were met by a tall, bald man with kind eyes. “Hi, can I help you?”
