Kara shot him her widest, most charming smile. “Good evening, sir. My name is Kara Danvers and I’m looking for Lillian Luthor. I- um, well this,” Kara looked towards Lena, “this is Lena.” His eyes widened like saucers. Lena squeezed her hand tighter than she’d ever felt.  

 

“Honey!” He yelled without taking his eyes off Lena.

 

“Yeah?” Lena’s breath caught in her throat and her heart was pounded in her chest as her mother came around the corner into the hallway.

 

Lionel turned to face her, he took her hand and stood in front of her, blocking her view for the moment. Lillian frowned, “honey,” he said gently, “this might come as bit of a shock.” He stepped aside and slipped an arm around her waist just in case. “This is Kara,” he gestured towards Kara who smiled and waved, “and this is- honey, this is Lena.” Kara stepped slightly to the side and Lena looked up from where she had been staring at the floor.

 

As soon as she saw those eyes, she knew it was true.

 

Lillian let out what sounded like a combination of a yelp and a gasp, Lionel held onto her as if he was the only thing keeping her upright. Her hand flew up to her mouth, tears glistening in her eyes. “Le-Lena?” She nodded and Lillian reached her trembling hand out. “My baby,” she whispered, tears streamed down Lena’s cheeks for the second time that day. “C-can I hug you?” Lena stepped forward slightly and Lillian couldn’t help but throw her arms around her. “I’ve waited so long to see you again.” Lena returned the hug.

 

She was still clinging onto Kara’s hand, Lena gave it one last squeeze before letting go; she used her free arm to hug her mother properly. It was the strangest enjoyment Lena had ever experienced, she didn’t know her mom and yet she felt an undeniable connection to her.

 

Lillian eventually pulled away and cupped her face, “you’re so beautiful, my darling.” Lillian pulled her back into the hug, “I’ve missed you so much.” The tears were flowing freely between them, even Lionel and Kara were a little misty eyed.

 

Mother and daughter finally broke apart, Lillian’s face broke into a wide smile and she wiped her eyes before wiping Lena’s cheeks as well. “Come in, come in properly.” She said, rather embarrassed that they were still stood in the doorway.

 

Lionel closed the door behind them, “I’m Lionel.”

 

“Kara.” She smiled and they shook hands.

 

“Just this way.” Lionel led the way through the house into the living room, “I’ll make some tea.”

 

“I’ll help.” Lena turned back, look of concern on her face. “It’s okay,” she whispered. “Go on,” she mouthed, nodding her head towards Lillian who was already sat on the couch.

 

“I can’t believe you’re here,” Lillian said, she reached out her hand cautiously, “may I?”

 

“Yeah,” Lillian cupped her face and stroked her cheeks.

 

“Your eyes are just as I remember.” Lena smiled.  

 

“Really?”

 

“Well, they were more blue than green but I can still see my baby when I look at you.” Kara and Lionel came over with the tea. “I’m so sorry, with all the excitement we haven’t been properly introduced, I’m Lillian.” Kara shook her hand.

 

“Kara Danvers.”

 

“Kara’s my- actually have we come up with a name for this yet?” Kara sat next to Lionel on the couch across from the duo.

 

“Um, no. In simple terms, I’m her girlfriend.” Lillian nodded in understanding.

 

“Kara is the reason I’m here, she discovered the truth about the whole thing.” Lillian stood up and Kara joined her, catching the women who flung herself at Kara.

 

“Thank you, thank you, thank you.” Lillian said, Kara hugged her back.

 

“It was nothing. I’m just happy that Lena finally knows the truth and has a family who loves her.” Lena smiled at the interaction.

 

“You’ve always been a part of this family,” Lillian said when they had returned to their original places. She took Lena’s hand, “I never gave up on you, I knew you were still alive.”

 

“I know, I read all the letters.” Lena said.

 

Lillian chuckled and looked down at her lap. “Sometimes, during my low moments, I was embarrassed by all the times I wrote to you, especially after there had been no news or trace of you.”

 

“Don’t be, I loved reading them and I’m sorry it took so long for me to get in touch.”

 

“I’m sorry I didn’t do more to protect you.” The pair of them were on the verge of tears again, apologising profusely.

 

Kara cleared her throat, “I’m sorry for interrupting, and I don’t want to come across rude, but why are you two apologising to each other? You did nothing wrong, we all know who is really to blame.”

 

Lillian gave her a complex look, “she tends to be blunt with me, I swear she enjoys telling me when I’m wrong.” Lena said a smirk firmly planted on her face. “I kind of love it though.”

 

“She’s right,” Lionel said.

 

“I do enjoy being right.” Kara said into her teacup.

 

Lena smiled and looked down at her mother’s hand clasping her own, she noticed the bracelet on her wrist and gasped. “Is that- is that the bracelet Lionel gave you?” Lena asked. Lillian nodded and took it off, handing it to her daughter. Lena was a little taken aback a seeing her own name permanently engraved into the metal: it was overwhelming to think someone who knew absolutely nothing about her, cared enough to wear her name on their person. “You- you still wear this?”

 

“Of course.”

 

“Everyday.” Lionel confirmed.

 

The group spent the afternoon chatting and getting to know one another. Lillian showed her a box of the few keepsakes she had of Lena: her hospital bracelet, pre-natal scans, a baby blanket and a pair of tiny, knitted baby booties.

 

Kara helped Lionel make dinner while Lena continued talking to her mother.

 

“Um, I have something else I would like to ask.” Lena said when they were around the table.

 

“Go ahead,” Lillian said.

 

“My name, I was always told a story about how I got my name. It was my favourite story and

now I know it was all a lie, I’d like to know the real reason.” Lillian’s eyes widened in surprise and she put down her fork and reached for Lena’s hand.

 

“Well, I don’t know what you were told but, I’m afraid I picked it from a book of names. If I’m being honest, I didn’t really have a clue what I wanted to name you, I read through hundreds of names. Your name has lots of different meanings depending on the translation, but it always revolves around sunlight or light.” Lillian explained. “The most common meaning is “ray of light” and that’s what you were- are to me, you brought joy to me, the hope of a better life and the inspiration I needed to become what I am today. That’s why I chose your name, no exciting story, it just meant something to me.”

 

“I think I like that story better than any other.” Lena smiled.

 

__________

 

Lena was a ball of gittery energy by the time they got back to the hotel, “Darling, I can’t believe it! You were right, she’s incredible.” Lena flopped back onto the bed and sighed.

 

“You can’t believe I was right, or you can’t believe she’s incredible?” Kara teased.

 

“Mostly, the fact that you were right about something.” Lena teased back, Kara pulled her up and into her arms.

 

“Are you happy?”

 

“So happy,” she squealed. Lena and Lillian had planned to spend the day together in the city, just the two of them, “I don’t think I’ll be able to sleep tonight.” Lena was like a child on Christmas Eve, bouncing all over the room.

 

“God,” Kara groaned and collapsed onto the bed. “You better, ‘cos I haven’t slept properly for days.”

 

“Aww, you poor baby.” Lena cooed, she straddled Kara’s hips and bent down to kiss her. “Are you sleepy?”

 

“Yes! You got to have a nap today,” she argued.

 

“I know and I’m very grateful for you.” Lena said, she kissed her again.

 

Kara pulled her closer, kissing her deeply, she rolled so she was on top of Lena. “I’m really proud of you,” she said, breaking the kiss. “You faced your fear today.” Kara tucked her hair behind her ear, “that was very courageous of you.”

 

“Well, I couldn’t have done it without you.” Lena stroked her jaw and pulled her down for another kiss.

 

“I love you.”

 

“I love you too.” Lena picked up the book from the night stand. “Come on, get comfy. I’ll read tonight.”

 

“It’s okay-” Kara was interrupted by her own yawn, “I can read it.” Lena sat back and raised her eyebrow, “okay, you can read it,” Kara said. They got ready for bed and Kara snuggled into Lena, she rested her head over Lena’s heart. The sound of her heartbeat and Lena’s soft voice lulled her to sleep quickly.

 

Lillian took them out for breakfast the next morning. Kara left her with a kiss and reassurance that everything would be okay. “You’re going to have so much fun,” Kara gave her a tight hug. “Call, if you need me,” Kara let her go. “Thanks for breakfast, Lillian.” The woman also gave Kara a hug, “take care of her, she’s more fragile than she lets on.” Kara whispered, she let go and Lillian nodded.

 

“Shall we, my darling?” Lena linked arms with her mom and off they went. Lillian took her to see the sights in the morning, and it was when she saw the look of awe on Lena’s face at The Statue of Liberty that she realised she hadn’t missed quite as much as she thought she had. There were still hundreds of new things Lena had yet to experience and Lillian wanted to be there for as many as possible.

 

“So, I’d love to hear everything.” Lillian said when they sat down to lunch.

 

“Um, everything?” Lena fidgeted nervously, she looked around the busy restaurant. The last thing she wanted to do was talk about everything that happened in such a public setting.

 

“Everything.” Lillian confirmed. “Where did you and Kara meet? When’s the wedding? When should I expect the grandchildren?” Lena almost choked on her water, not expecting this line of questioning. “After everything I read… I just didn’t expect for you to have found someone.”

 

“Uhh no,” Lena chuckled. “It’s a little more complicated than that. I met her through work.” Lillian was a smart woman, she’d seen the way her daughter looked at Kara and vice versa. She wanted to know everything about Lena, but she knew that would be difficult and Kara seemed like the best place to start.

 

Lena told her everything: the truth about how they met, how many time they almost killed each other, how they fell in love and then they gushed over pictures and videos of Hero.

 

They spent the rest of the day exploring the city and Lillian took her to see a Broadway show later in the evening. By the time they got back to the hotel it was late, Kara met them outside.

 

“Hey, I thought you guys were going to dance the night away.” Lena threw her arms around Kara’s neck, “did you guys have a good time?”

 

“Yes,” Lena said, squeezing her tightly.

 

“I half expected to get a call at 3am asking me to pick you up from a club.” Kara joked, letting her go.

 

“Oh, I’m way past my night club days.” Lillian said, she hugged Kara. “Thank you, for looking after her.” She whispered.

 

“Likewise.” Kara replied, she wondered for a second if they would ever communicate about Lena at a normal volume.

 

The newly acquainted family spent the rest of the week together, Lena and Lillian cried on their final day.

 

“Don’t worry, my darling, I’ll come and visit soon.” Lillian said, she wiped Lena’s cheeks. Of course Lillian didn’t want her to go, she just got her daughter back, but they both had responsibilities and too much too soon might not be the best option.

 

“I’ll call you.” Lena sniffled. She didn’t think she was even going to have a relationship with her mother and now she was distraught when it came time to go.

 

Kara held her hand the whole way home.

 

__________

 

Kara and Lena had just woken up when Kara received a message from Alex. Lena sleepily rolled into Kara’s arms, she kissed up and down her neck. “G’mornin,” she mumbled.

 

“Morning babe,” Kara whispered, kissing the top of her head. She reached for her phone and there was a short pause before she squealed loudly. Lena grumbled and moved away, shoving her head under her pillow; Hero got onto the bed to investigate the commotion. Kara cupped his head and kissed his face, she wound him up and watched him run around the room, barking and yipping.

 

“Too early for this shit.” Lena grumbled.

 

“Babe! Baaaabe,” Kara shook her and took the pillow away from her. “Babe! Maggie had the baby!”

 

Lena cracked one eye open, “why didn’t you start with that?” She slowly got up, still tired and groggy. Kara showed her the photo, she blinked and rubbed the sleep out of her eyes. “That’s a cute baby,” she said simply. Just as Kara was about to respond a video came through: the baby girl was dressed in a pink footed onesie, she stretched and kicked her feet slightly while making soft cooing noises. “Okay, that is a very cute baby.”

 

Alex: Ryan Avery Sawyer.

          Born 5:03 this morning

          6lbs 8oz

 

Kara: I love her already.

 

A month later, the new parents invited Kara and Lena over for dinner and game night. “Where the little munchkin?” Kara asked as soon as they were in the house.

 

“Good to see you too Kara. Maggie is just changing her, she’ll be out in a minute.” Alex chuckled.

 

She pulled Lena into a hug, “so how’s parenting treating you?” She asked.

 

“Oh y’know, amazing, challenging and exhausting all rolled into one. Best adventure I’ve ever been on though.” She smiled, it was genuine and full of love. Maggie emerged at the top of the stairs, small bundle in her arms, Kara giddily squirmed on the spot.

 

“Come through,” Maggie said. The group went through to the living room and Maggie handed Ryan over to Kara.

 

“Wow,” Kara said, staring admirably at the little girl, “look at you. You’re beautiful,” Ryan cooed. “Yeah, you are.” Kara looked up, “you guys made a cute baby.”

 

“Thanks.” Maggie said, smug grin on her face, she knew how cute their child was. Lena watched as Kara gushed over the baby, it didn’t make her want one but she had to admit it was kind of adorable.

 

“Hey, Kar?” Kara looked up from where she was tickling Ryan’s ribs, relishing in the small smile and breathy noise.

 

“Yeah?”

 

“Maggie and I were talking and we want to ask you something. We would love it if you would agree to be Ryan’s godmother?” Alex asked, beaming at her.

 

“Really?” Kara said, eyes wide and hopeful.

 

“Uh huh,” Maggie confirmed.

 

“I’d love to!” Kara exclaimed, she lifted Ryan up and kissed her forehead. “Who did you pick to be her godfather?”

 

“Oh, my partner, Mitch. He saved my life during a shoot out two years ago.” Maggie explained.

 

“Mitch,” Kara tested the name out on her tongue. “Yeah, I’m gonna need his full name and social security number.”

 

“Kara-”

 

“Lena.” She shifted Ryan in her arms, so Lena could see the baby’s face. “I gotta make sure I do the proper background checks, so this little munchkin is safe.”

 

“Mitchell Wilbur Croft.” Maggie said, “and you’re on diaper duty for the next week.” She pointed at Alex who groaned.

 

“What?” Lena looked between the couple.

 

“Maggie bet that they would both say the same thing. Kara’s background check came back all clear two days ago.” Lena laughed and looked at Kara who was too busy making faces at the baby to realise what had been said.

 

“What better two people to protect our daughter?”

 

“Hey Lee, do you wanna hold her?” Lena’s eyes widened and all three women were looking at her expectantly.

 

“You know what? Maybe later, spend some time with your new god-daughter.” Lena was proud of herself for avoiding that one so smoothly. Maggie eventually took Ryan back so she could feed her and Alex went to serve the food.

 

They finished dinner and were halfway through the first game of Exploding Kittens when Ryan decided she was clearly unhappy and screaming the house down was the only way to get what she wanted, the problem was no one knew what she wanted. Alex tried changing her, Maggie tried feeding her, Kara tried cuddling and bouncing and playing with her, but that didn’t work either.

 

“Aww, baby girl.” Kara cooed, “why are you so unhappy? Huh?” Ryan coughed and spluttered, her chubby cheeks tear stained and a small, miserable pout on her face. She looked at Lena who was looking anywhere but Kara and Ryan, “Your turn, babe.” She thrust the crying baby into Lena’s hands.

 

“Wait what?” Lena held the screaming child at arms length.

 

Kara plopped down next to her and put her arm around Lena, she eased the baby into her body. “There you go, support her head.” Lena cupped the back of her head, “just do what feels natural,” Kara whispered, Lena tentatively rubbed her back. Ryan squirmed, kicking her feet; Lena stood up and walked around the room, shushing her softly; Maggie and Alex shared a look. Ryan calmed down after a few moments, her cries turned into soft mewls and then she stopped altogether, her tiny fists gripped Lena’s shirt tightly.

 

Kara turned back for a moment and then took a sip of her drink, she observed the look of shock on the new mothers’ faces. “She’s a natural at everything,” Kara shrugged. Lena rejoined them on the couch after a few minutes when the baby had calmed down fully. Kara scooted up to her and kissed the top of Ryan’s head.

 

“Where were we?” Lena said, Kara handed her the cards she was holding before Kara gave her the baby and helped her play the game while her arms were full.

 

Alex leaned forward, mouth still agape, “will you move in with us?”

 

__________

 

“The trial of the century”, as it was dubbed, was set to begin in the next few days, Lena had spoken about it with Kara, Sam, Andrea, Sara, her mother, everyone she trusted. Sam and a few of the others had decided they were going to go to The Hague to watch her get what she deserved. Lena had spoken about it with Kelly and Kara, she decided that it would be best for her own self-preservation if she avoided all of it. So, Lena, Kara and Hero decided they would spend the duration of the trial at the cabin in the mountains, away from everything.

 

“Did you ask them?” Kara said as she heaved their bags up the stairs.

 

“Sam said she was going to watch the trial with some of the others, Leslie is testifying, Sara is still with Ava they’re still doing the bounty hunter thing, apparently they’re really good at it and Andrea’s in Spain.” Lena replied, “they were thankful but declined.”

 

“Ouch.” Kara said, throwing their bags on the bed. “I’m hurt that they don’t want to spend time with me and I thought we’d bonded.” She said, sarcasticly.

 

“Oh, like you want a house full of ex-assassins.”

 

They spent the first couple of days exploring the woods surrounding the cabin, allowing Hero to roam free in his natural habitat, a field full of sticks. The pair were cooking dinner together, fooling around as usual, when there was a knock at the door. Kara frowned, “stay here. I’ll get it,” she kissed Lena’s head and went to answer it.

 

“Hey, Kara.”

 

“Sam!” Kara exclaimed, “it’s good to see you again. Come on in, Lena’s in the kitchen.” She stepped aside and welcomed her inside.

 

“I got lost twice on the way up here, thought I’d never find this place.” Sam joked weakly, even Kara could see that there was something wrong: her shoulders were slumped, her eyes were dark and trained on the floor, she was closed off, arms hugging her body.

 

“Well, you’re here now. Come on,” Kara led her through to the kitchen.

 

“Sammy, hey.” Lena dropped what she was doing and gave Sam a hug. “What are you doing here?”

 

“I changed my mind.” Sam said simply, she spotted Hero over Lena’s shoulder. “Hey, is this the famous Hero?” Sam let go of Lena and rushed over to greet the curious puppy.

 

Lena frowned at Kara, “I don’t know,” she mouthed shrugging her shoulders. “Go on,” she mouthed, nodding towards Sam who was petting an enthusiastic puppy, ecstatic that he now had three people to love.

 

“I’m starting to think he’s gone soft,” Kara commented, keeping her voice low. They both leaned against the counter observing the situation.

 

“Not at all, he didn’t like that girl you tried to replace me with.” She raised her eyebrows, Kara’s jaw dropped and she narrowed her eyes. “He just has good taste in people,” she said smugly.

 

“Hey, she was a nice girl.” Kara hissed, Lena turned to her, a frosty glare on her face, “of course what I meant to say was, she was nothing compared to you and I can’t even remember her name.” She backtracked quickly, she turned and noted the smug smile on her face, she rested her forehead on Lena’s shoulder.

 

“Not fun being teased, is it?” Lena grinned, Kara huffed out a laugh and pressed multiple kisses to her cheek.

 

“Touché.” Kara grinned, she stepped in front of her and squeezed her sides. Kara kissed the side of her head, “go talk to her,” she mumbled into her hair, Kara pulled three mugs from the cupboard and started making tea.  

 

“Hey, Sammy.” She crouched down and joined her on the floor next to her new best friend, Hero got up to kiss her face. “What happened?” Sam looked over at Kara and worried her bottom lip. “Don’t worry about her, she doesn’t listen to anything.”

 

“Fuck you, Luthor.” She called over her shoulder.

 

“If you’re lucky, Danvers.” She shot back, Sam chuckled. She looked down still stroking Hero’s head, “you won’t be judged here.”

 

“I couldn’t do it,” she whispered. “Everything we went through, everything we’ve trained for and I lasted a day.” Sam shook her head.

 

“Come here,” Lena pulled her into a tight hug.

 

“It was awful, I should have listened to you.” Lena shushed her gently.

 

“It’s okay, don’t worry. Hey, I wouldn’t have even got on the plane, you’re braver than me.” Lena said.

 

Sam huffed, “or you’re just smarter than me.”

 

“Well, we’ve always known that.” They both laughed. “The point is, you tried. You’re here now, you’re taking care of yourself and that’s all that matters. It’s not always about proving how brave or how strong you are, sometimes it about putting yourself first.”

 

“Does the offer still stand?” Sam sniffled, Lena looked over at Kara.

 

“Of course!” Kara said. “I’ll get your bags.” Sam tossed her the car keys and Kara took her stuff up to the second bedroom, Lena had moved Sam to the couch where she was comforting the distraught woman. Kara came back down, she placed two cups of tea in front of them and continued making dinner.

 

Kara gave them their space, she went up to bed a few hours early with Hero so Sam would feel more comfortable. She was just finishing up on another picture when Lena entered the room and climbed onto the bed next to her. “That looks good,” she said planting a kiss on Kara’s jaw.

 

“Thanks,” she turned to give Lena a proper kiss. “How’s Sam?”

 

“Um, she’s… better,” she tilted her head, not looking convinced at all. “She’s getting ready for bed now.” Lena cleared her throat, “would it be okay if I stayed with her tonight?”

 

“Yeah, of course.” Kara said without hesitation, Lena looked slightly taken aback. “You don’t have to ask. You know that, right?”

 

“Yeah, I just- I thought it would be polite to ask… with everything we’ve been through over the past year.” Lena stroked her cheek.

 

“I appreciate the thought but, she’s your best friend and she needs you right now.” Lena kissed her deeply before kissing her cheeks and down her neck. Kara watched as Lena got ready for bed, slightly regretting her decision when she realised she wouldn’t get to share a bed with Lena. She also looked really, really good in those small sleep shorts.

 

“Good night, darling.” Lena kissed her and rubbed her thumb over her pouty lips. “I love you.”

 

“I love you too, sleep well, babe.”

He and Kara watched as Lena left the room, he waited a few seconds for her to come back and then he began to realise she wouldn’t be back tonight. He sighed deeply which trailed off into a soft whine, he looked at her, puppy dog eyes on display. “I know, it sucks, but you’ll see her in the morning.” She said the words, but it didn’t stop the sad expression fixed on her own face. Yet again, they were two pouting puppies waiting for Lena to come back, “Sam needs her more than we do right now.”

She got to sleep in the early hours of the morning and managed to get a couple of hours rest before Lena crawled into bed.

Kara scoffed, “he’s our dog. And when he’s acting like this, he’s your responsibility.” She squeezed Lena’s sides until she turned to greet him.

“I think I’m gonna take Sammy for a hike, show her the woods and stuff.” Lena said.

 

“Sounds like fun, is Hero going too?”

 

“He can if he wants?” Hero’s head perked up from where he was laid on her lap. “You wanna come with me and Sam today?” His tail wagged excitedly. “I’ll take that as a yes.”

 

“Good, I have some errands to run today and I don’t want him to be alone.” They finished up and Kara went upstairs to get changed, Lena followed her up.

 

“Hey,” Lena said, she looped her arms around Kara’s waist and hugged her. “Are you okay? I’m not making you feel left out, am I? Because, that wasn’t my intention.”

 

Kara chuckled and turned around, kissing her softly, “I don’t feel left out, I’m just giving you and Sam space. She was really upset last night and the last thing she needs is to feel like a third-wheel.” Kara tucked Lena’s hair behind her ear. “I’m okay.”

 

“You promise?” Lena said, they swayed gently.

 

“I promise.”

 

“You don’t want to have Hero as company?”

 

“Nah, I really do have errands to run, we need more food. Hero would be here on his own anyway.” Lena kissed her again. “Spend some time with Sam, I’ll be here when you get back.” Kara held her for a few minutes until it was time to get ready.

“Are you ready to talk about what happened?” Lena said, she turned her head and watched as Sam kicked a stone along the pathway.

 

“She pleaded not guilty.” They had been told that Talia was advised to plead guilty to avoid the lengthy trial but Lena wasn’t shocked as she would have expected.

 

Lena laughed lowly, “she wants her time in the limelight, she was never going to give up her last ounce of control.”

 

“Maybe, I’m the stupid one. I thought she would at least give us the courtesy of not having to sit through every horrible thing we ever had to do.” She kicked the stone as hard as she could and watched as it soared through the trees.

 

“You’re not stupid Sam, she’s just an entirely different breed of monster.” Lena linked arms with Sam, “in a few weeks it will be old news, something they only talk about every so often until the sentencing.”

 

“What if they find her not guilty?” Sam voiced her fears out loud and they then became very real.

 

“That won’t happen.” Lena said forcefully, “I don’t care what fancy lawyer she’s hired, there’s no way she’s getting away with it. She’s going to prison for the rest of her life and so are Rhea and Selina.”

 

“This is going to follow us around for the rest of our lives.” Sam mumbled.

 

“You’re right, because it was, and still is, a huge part of our lives. We can’t forget it, we can’t go back, we can’t pretend it never happened and trust me I’ve tried. We just have to accept it and try to be happy.” Sam looked at her as if she had three heads, “what?”

 

“Since when did you become so… enlightened?” Lena chuckled.

 

“I’ve been going to therapy.” She confessed, Sam raised her eyebrows in surprise.

 

“What’s that like?”

 

“It’s… good.”

 

“You sound convinced,” Sam scoffed.

 

Lena shoved her playfully, “it’s hard to explain. It took me so long to find a therapist that I liked and then it took me a while to get comfortable with her, but even I can see the difference it’s made. Have you thought about contacting your family?” She asked.

 

Sam shook her head. “They have a whole new life now, I don’t want to ruin that.”

 

“So, you’re going to let them think you’re one of those unidentified bodies scattered around the world?” Sam shifted uncomfortably.

 

“Well, when you put it like that.”

 

“Listen, you don’t have to meet them, you don’t have to have anything to do with them, but having a child taken from you is not something a person ever gets over. Even if they had another child, it doesn’t mean they forgot about you.” Sam rested her head against Lena’s while they.

 

“Have you met your mom?”

 

“Yeah,” Lena breathed.

 

“What’s she like?”

 

“She’s amazing and we talk everyday now. It took me a while though, I was scared that once she heard about where I really was all those years, she wouldn’t want to know me. I was wrong.”

 

“I bet that hurt your ego.” Sam muttered.

 

Lena laughed, “it did. I had to admit Kara was right, it was horrible.”

 

Sam chuckled, “at least that seems to be going well.”

 

Lena hummed, “it is. Don’t get me wrong, it wasn’t as easy as we initially thought but we got through it and we’re happy.”

 

“Good. And, although it hurts, I’m happy to admit that I was also very wrong. It’s clear there’s a lot of love between you two.” Sam said, at that moment Hero came bounded over with what looked like half a tree in his mouth. “I mean, you have a child together,” she gestured to the eager to please puppy, “it’s clearly serious.” Lena chuckled and Sam bent down to play with him, tugging the log away.

 

“I’ll go with you, if you don’t want to go alone.”

 

“Really?”

 

Lena nodded. “Of course, it’s incredibly difficult, terrifying and there’s no way I would have been able to do it on my own.” Sam looked uneasy, “I know I didn’t paint it in the best light, but I won’t lie to you. It will be hard, but I guarantee it will be the best thing you’ve ever done.”  

 

“Thank you.”

 

“How’s the house hunt going?” Lena asked, changing the subject before Sam got too uncomfortable.

 

“Good, I think I found the one. It’s a nice cabin in the mountains, kinda like this one but with more land… It’s in Colorado though.” She trailed off.

 

“Oh.” Lena said, it was her turn to kick a rock along the floor this time. “Well, it sounds nice. It’s just gonna be weird not seeing you all the time.”

 

“I know, I guess it won’t be that much different from before. We didn’t see each other every day.” Sam reasoned.

 

“No, that’s true. But, you were always there when I needed you.” Lena admitted, still kicking the stone.

 

“I’ll only ever be a phone call away.” Lena hummed, Sam sighed softly, “it’s not the same though, is it?” After all, they’d always planned to live together when they were free.

 

“No.” She stopped and Lena turned to face her.

 

“I’m gonna miss you so much,” Sam murmured.

 

“I’m gonna miss you too.” There was a brief pause and then they launched into a hug, squeezing each other tightly. They both cried, hot tears rolling down their cheeks. Since they were kids they’d been each others support system, they’d grown up together, looked after one another. They were family.

 

“You won’t tell anyone I cried, right?” Sam sniffled.

 

“I’ll take it to my grave,” Lena promised and they both laughed.

 

Sam fell asleep on the couch almost as soon as they got back, Hero laid in front of her like a giant teddy bear. Lena had just covered them with a blanket when Kara came home, “where have you been?” Lena whispered, greeting her with a peck.

 

“Firewood.” She answered. Kara looped her arms around Lena’s waist and swept her up in a tight hug, “how was your day?” Lena breathed in her comforting scent.

 

“Good.” She leaned back slightly and cupped Kara’s face, “what about you? Any problems?” Kara shook her head.

 

“No, it was good. Peaceful.” Kara kissed her again, nibbling slightly on her bottom lip. “I missed you though and Hero.” She looked around for him, “I see some things never change.” She said when she saw Hero was cozied up to Sam.

 

“I think it’s sweet.” Lena cooed.

 

“It is. I just mean he’s always been drawn to lost souls.” Lena smiled and then frowned when she realised.

 

“Hey! Are you saying I was a lost soul?”

 

“Umm duhh, Lena when we first met your party trick was reciting the plots of films you’d never seen. If that’s not a prime example of a sad, lonely human I don’t know what is.” Lena kissed her deeply.

 

“You may have a point there,” she mumbled against Kara’s lips.

 

“You’re not alone, I was sad and lonely too when I got him. Not any more though.” Lena smiled. “So, I was thinking of making Krupnik tonight and then, introducing Sam to the wondrous world of s’mores.”

 

Lena groaned, “I’ve missed s’mores.”

 

“Me too. You want to help with dinner?” Lena nodded, she hadn’t seen Kara all day and so any excuse to spend time with her was worth it. Lena had never made it before, but Kara talked her through it. Lena enjoyed cooking but there was something that was plaguing her mind and Kara could tell, she caught the slight tremble in her hand while she was chopping the vegetables. “What’s going on?” Kara said, bumping her hip.

 

Lena froze and Kara saw as her shoulders tense, “Talia pleaded not guilty.” Lena switched to  stirring the soup, “what if she gets off?” Kara switched off the stove and looped her arms around Lena’s waist.

 

“That’s not going to happen.” Kara said.

 

“How do you know?” Lena spun in her arms, she was visibly shaking; Kara held her close and stroked her hair.

 

“Because there is overwhelming evidence to prove her guilt. Lena nodded, “thank you.” Kara kissed the side of her head.

 

“Have you spoken to your mom today?” Lena shook her head, “go call her now, I’ll finish this off.”

 

“I’ll be back soon,“ Lena kissed her before leaving the room. She came back half an hour later looking much happier.

 

“Feel better?”

 

“Much.”

 

“Try it,” Kara whispered. It was just as good as when Kara made it the first time.

 

“It’s really good.” Lena said.

 

“Great, you finish that off and I will get the fire started.” Kara said, Lena’s eyes widened with fear.

 

“Don’t leave now, what if I ruin it?” She hissed, Kara grinned and cupped her face before kissing her softly.

 

“You’ll be fine, just let it simmer.” Kara left her to potentially ruin dinner, but Lena handled the pressure well and she kept a close eye on the soup.

 

Kara lit the fire pit on the porch and Lena gently shook Sam. “Hey, Sammy. Dinner’s almost ready.” Sam grumbled and stretched, Hero kissed her face enthusiastically.

 

She rolled off the couch and stumbled sleepily into the kitchen. Sam immediately stopped, suddenly wide awake. “Is that?” She pointed at the pot.

 

“Uh huh,” Lena nodded. “It was Kara’s idea.” They both heard the door open.

 

“I need a minute, I don’t want to cry in front of Captain Barbie,” she whispered, it was said with fondness. Lena laughed and watched as Sam scurried away to compose herself.

 

“Should I be worried?” Kara said when she entered the kitchen, she got the bowls down from the cupboard.

 

“Nope,” Lena replied, popping the ‘p’. They served the soup, Sam and Lena sat next to each other and Kara sat on the couch next to them, Hero curled up on her lap. Lena tore her bread roll apart and handed half to Sam, she looked at her quizzically. “It’s tradition,” Lena shrugged, Sam laughed and took it.

 

“Well, if we’re going by tradition, you owe me the other half as well.” Sam joked.

 

“Ooo, can’t do that I’m afraid, Captain Barbie will be on my ass,” she muttered, they both snickered and Kara looked up with a confused noise. “Don’t worry, darling. It’s nothing for you to worry about.” Kara accepted the answer and carried on eating.

 

It was times like this where Lena yearned to be next to her, touch her: Kara was bathed in the golden light of the fire, her blue eyes glistening, soft and warm under a blanket with a puppy on her lap.

 

Perfect.

Kara was completely oblivious to the fact Lena felt giddy and her stomach swooped every time she looked at Kara. The same woman who doing everything she could to help, not just Lena, but also her best friend through the toughest time in their lives.

Lena was conflicted: on one hand she wanted to spend as much time with Sam while she had the chance but on the other, she wanted to curl up in Kara’s arms and waste the night away staring at her.

 

Kara stood and gathered the empty bowls, “I’ll give you a hand with dessert.” Lena announced.

 

“Urghh, you don’t have to make up an excuse to go and make out with her.” Sam groaned, Hero got up on the couch next to her.

 

“No, we really do have a plan for dessert.” Kara said.

 

“Oh, well forget I said anything then.” Sam went back to cooing over Hero while Lena followed Kara into the kitchen.

 

“So, I’ll get the ingredients,” Kara said, “can you get the skewers in the…” she trailed off when Lena cupped her face. “What?”

 

“I really did only come in here to make out with you.” Lena admitted, a little sheepishly. Kara giggled and bent down to capture her lips, she gripped Lena’s hips and turned her around to pin her against the counter. Kara’s lips were soft and warm and it was moments like this that Lena cherished. She moaned and Kara’s tongue darted out to gloss over Lena’s lips, she opened her mouth allowing Kara to slip her tongue inside.

“Mm-” Kara moaned, “you’re-” Lena kissed her when she pulled away, “very- mm,” Lena nipped her lips, “affectionate-” Lena pecked her lips and continued up her jaw and down her neck, “-tonight,” she finally finished.

 

“You’re just particularly irresistible tonight,” Lena said into her neck before continuing her assault.

 

“I mean, I can’t argue with that.” Kara lifted her onto the counter, “but we should probably get back before Sam figures out we lied.” She kissed Lena again and grinned at the slight mewl she made.

 

“Just a little longer?” Lena pleaded, wrapping her limbs around Kara’s body and holding her close. Kara just held her, her towering presence made Lena feel small and safe. When Lena didn’t let go, Kara carried her around the kitchen gathering everything they needed and Lena finally let go just before they went back to join Sam.

 

Kara perfectly toasted the marshmallow and carefully made the perfect s’more with the same intricacy and concentration as she did when she made Lena’s first one all that time ago. She presented it to Sam who didn’t understand why the two of them were eagerly waiting with excitement and anticipation.

 

Sam took her first bite and moaned, “my god, this is incredible!” She exclaimed, “seriously, why am I only trying these now?” Lena held up her hand and Kara high-fived her before starting Lena’s s’more.

 

Eventually, when they were full and Hero was snoring loudly, Kara kissed Lena goodnight and led him up to bed. Lena threw some more logs onto the fire and she and Sam stayed up half the night talking until the fire went out, they were too tired to dream and Lena had to carry her up to bed.

 

Lena stayed with Sam for the rest of the week and Kara looked forward to the early mornings when a soft, sleepy Lena would crawl into bed with her. Lena looked forward to not only time with Kara, but Kara had also got into the habit of doing shirtless sets of push-ups, pull-ups and sit-ups before breakfast and Lena’s sleep muddled brain couldn’t handle the glorious imagesand she was sure Kara was doing it on purpose.

 

Sam had become less reserved and more like herself, Kara would rather endure the teasing than have to watch her sit sullen and gloomy on the couch. Kara spent more time with them when Sam was more comfortable, but she still occasionally gave them their space. To Kara, it was kind of like watching the beginning of their relationship, except the roles were reversed- and there was no fighting- and they weren’t sleeping together- in that way. The point is, watching Lena’s delight as she introduced Sam to everything she loved was a beautiful sight to see.

 

Lena was lying on Kara who was tracing patterns on her lower back, waiting for the moment where Lena would say goodnight and leave. Hero was lying at the foot of the bed, keeping a watchful eye on things to make sure Lena didn’t go anywhere without acknowledging him. Kara could tell she was minutes away from falling asleep, she stopped her ministrations and smiled at Lena’s grumble of protest. “Are you staying with Sam tonight?”

 

Lena shook her head, “no need, nightmares stopped.” She lifted her hips up into Kara’s hand and let out a soft whine, she chuckled but accepted the prompt.

 

“Oh, so you’re planning to sleep in my bed tonight?” She teased playfully.

 

“Your bed? I thought it was our bed, our dog.”

 

“it was, until you decided to shack up with someone else for a week.” She continued her teasing, “then all owners rights reverted back to me.”

 

Lena was too tired and too comfortable to tease back properly, “m’okay all yours, you deal with him when he’s bad and needy.”

 

Kara paused for a second, “I take it all back, fifty-fifty split?”

 

“Deal.”

A year later and things had never been better between them: Talia, Rhea and Selina were sentenced to life behind bars, they would never hurt anyone else ever again; Lena went with Sam to meet her family who, coincidentally, also lived in Colorado; they were wonderful and welcomed her with open arms. They both continued with therapy and it did wonders for their relationship and their own well-being. Lena spoke to her mom everyday, they visited each other regularly and Kara spent as much time with Ryan as she possibly could.

 

Then one day, Kara got a call from Barry, her contact at Interpol: they were setting up a new team in Oslo, specialising in organised crime groups operating across Europe. He offered her a spot on the team.

 

The couple were happy, but they were both active people and sitting at home twiddling their thumbs all day wasn’t what they wanted to do for the rest of their lives. It was nice to have the time to decompress, deal with everything that had happened and spend time with each other. Now, seemed like the perfect time to get back to doing what she was best at. The job offer still came as a shock to her, even though she had almost single-handedly uncovered the deception of the World Killers, Winn doesn’t need a job okay.

 

Kara couldn’t take the position without talking to Lena first. They would be leaving a lot behind, but a fresh start would be nice and it was a fantastic opportunity for Kara. They agreed that if it didn’t work out, they would move back and start again.

 

So, the couple packed up their lives, sub-let the loft and moved to Norway. Lillian had missed out of the entirety of her daughter’s life, she wasn’t going to let her move halfway around the world without her. To Lena’s surprise, her mother and Lionel uprooted their entire lives and moved to Norway with them, intending to start their own practice. It put Lena’s mind at ease, she didn’t know anyone and Kara got to go to work everyday so it was nice to have her family close by.

 

They bought a house and a small bit of land just outside of the city: it was a quaint, little house, oak furnishings and a view to die for, with a large garden for Hero to frolic in and a vegetable patch for Lena to grow whatever she wanted. They made sure to decorate their home with every photo they could: pictures of them together, Hero, Kara’s family, Lena’s family, photos of Kara during deployment, pictures of Sam, Alex, Maggie and little Ryan. They made sure to surround themselves with the comforts of home. Their home was surrounded by a thick forest of trees that they happily spent their weekends exploring. Her mom and Lionel came over every week for dinner, they had game nights with Alex and Maggie over Facetime. They even managed to keep up with their weekly therapy sessions over Zoom.

 

It was everything Kara described and more.  

 

Kara loved her new job and her new team consisted of multiple people from different organisations around the world, all experts in their field and Kara was enjoying working with majority of them.

 

Her new boss, Cat Grant, is tough, no nonsense and extremely good at her job; she’s a great leader, forceful and commanded the attention of the room without even trying. She’s stern and yet Kara could tell that she cared deeply about the members of her team and the work that they were doing. Kara admired her greatly, but she was also terrified of her most of the time.

 

She’d known Barry Allen for a while: he’s a laid back guy but he’s smart and passionate about his work. While they had fun in the office, pulling pranks and avoiding Cat’s wrath, when it came to the job he was committed to fighting for justice.

 

Querl Dox, or Brainy as he was referred too, was a technological genius and Kara didn’t understand the majority of what he was saying most of the time. He’s quirky, a little awkward and he didn’t understand a lot of the cultural references Kara made but he was sweet and fun to be around and he reminded her a lot of Lena. She was sure he had a thing for another member of the team, Nia Nal, it was cute and Kara gave him advice which he didn’t always understand, but he was trying his best.

 

Nia Nal had somehow become her protégé: she was new to the job but she’d worked hard and earned her spot on the team. She’s a kind-hearted, shy girl and Kara had taken the young woman under her wing after the first few days of meeting her.

 

Life was almost perfect.

 

But of course, it was Lena and Kara, and life wasn’t without its problems.

She was brand new to this team and she didn’t feel she had the right to demand a new partner so soon. Plus, they worked incredibly well together and Kara finally had a sparring partner who could give her a run for her money, so she put up with the flirting for the good of the team.

 

Their partnership started off friendly, they would talk, share inside jokes and they worked well together. Then, things slowly started taking a turn that Kara didn’t quite expect: she began by complimenting her outfits, tugging on the fabric, squeezing her biceps while they talked. Then came the flirty smiles, lip bites and inappropriate touching that made Kara’s underwear uncomfortable for the rest of the day.

Kara grabbed the inside of her elbow and dragged her into the stationary cupboard. “This ends today,” she growled. “Stop with the teasing, and the touching, and the comments. I’m trying to work.”

 

That didn’t deter her at all, the woman slowly backed her up against the wall and leaned up to whisper in her ear. “What’s wrong, darling?” Kara shivered at the name and the roll of the “r”. It turned her on and made her feel dirty at the same time. She sucked Kara’s earlobe into her mouth and a small whimper escaped her, “don’t you enjoy it?”

 

Kara didn’t respond and the alluring woman took the opportunity to unbuckle Kara’s pants and slip her delicate hand into her underwear. “Oh, you do enjoy it,” she purred, Kara moaned when her fingers slid through her wet folds and over her throbbing clit.

 

“I really shouldn’t do this,” she groaned.

 

She licked around the shell of Kara’s ear, “you’re already doing it, you might as well enjoy it.” Kara pushed the woman away from her and she looked surprised at the sudden rejection. Kara looked at her, her eyes raked over her partner’s irresistible body and she saw the smirk plastered on her face.

 

Kara’s resolve failed.

 

She turned her partner around and slammed her against the wall, she captured her lips in a fiery kiss. Kara’s hands ran over her body: she pulled her blouse out of her skirt and slid her palm up the inside of her thigh, she broke the kiss and groaned when she realised she was wearing thigh high stockings. She felt soft lips press up and down her neck and she knew she would be covered in bright, red lipstick stains.

 

Well, I’ve ruined it now, I may as well go all out.

Kara got down on her knees and pushed the tight skirt up to her waist. “Fuck, are you trying to kill me?” She groaned when she saw the woman wasn’t wearing any underwear.

 

Half an hour later and Kara was a dishevelled mess, covered in lipstick. She got dressed as quickly as possible, shoving her shirt into her pants, combing her fingers through her hair. “This can never happen again,” she said firmly and her new lover just hummed while buttoning her shirt, they both knew it was going to happen again. It wasn’t underwhelming, it was fucking mind-blowing and Kara was in far too deep now.

 

Kara pulled out her pocket square and wiped her face and neck, getting rid of the guilty red stains, the ones on her stomach and the inside of her thighs were hidden for now. “Did I get it all?” She asked.

 

“Yes,” her partner said, giving her another quick peck on the lips, “apart from that bit.” Kara scowled and wiped her lips with the back of her hand. “Don’t blame me, Kara. You made your choice, now you just have to live with it.”

 

“You’re gonna get me in so much trouble.” Kara said, she grabbed something off the shelf and left the room.

 

“Danvers!” Lemarc called, she whipped around. “Where have you been?” He was a grumpy, older man who mostly worked on the paperwork. He was about six months away from retirement and hadn’t bothered to learn much about his co-workers.

 

“Getting staples.” She said simply, holding up the box of staples she’d taken.

 

He narrowed his eyes at her, “where’s Prince?”

 

“I don’t know!” She exclaimed, he gave her a strange look. Kara looked left and right, “um, I mean I haven’t seen her, recently.” She swallowed and fiddled with the box in her hand.

 

“You’re being weird.” He said, Kara nervously scratched the back of her neck. “Well, the boss has an assignment for you, her and um,” he clicked his fingers, trying to remember. “Oh, I don’t know, the other one. So, just find her.” He ordered.

 

Kara ignored the request and went back to her desk. Her phone lit up with a notification, she stared at the photo of Lena and Hero on her lockscreen. She looked up when she heard the office door open and her eyes snapped up to see Diana enter the room, she shot her a small, wry smile and Kara returned a brief upturning of her lips. She bit the pad of her thumb and turned her phone over.

 

Well, I’ve done it now. I can’t go back, I can’t change it.

 

“Luthor, there you are! Where have you been?” Lena sat down at the desk opposite Kara, that fucking smirk plastered on her face. She looked prim, proper, pristine; like she hadn’t just come on Kara’s fingers three times in half an hour. God she’s infuriatingly perfect.

 

“Inquires. I have a few contacts to help with the Almstedt case.” She said casually.

 

Did she mention that she was completely and utterly in love with her new partner? Lena was maddening and it was a pleasure to watch her excel in her work, but that also meant that Kara was distracted almost all of the time.

 

Oh, and she’d just lost the bet which meant she was on coffee duty for the next month.

 

Lena had become bored after a few months into their new life, Kara went to work everyday and Lena stayed at home. She had become the dutiful house-wifey that Kara had joked about and she hated it, Kara could see it too. Although she went to see Lillian, she was lonely and she wasn’t a person who could just sit around and grow carrots, she wanted to be out in the world making a difference.

 

Cat had asked Kara way back when she first started whether she knew any of the women involved in the World Killers, apparently Cat Grant was one who liked to take risks. Lena didn’t want to get the job because she was living with Kara, she wanted to do it by herself and therefore, no one knew Kara and Lena were together when she was interviewed for the job. It was a happy coincidence that they were assigned to each other.

 

A dynamic partnership that no one really understood but them. It came as a shock to the rest of the team just how well they worked together, considering how much they bickered. Half the team were betting on them getting together and the other half had a wager on which one would kill the other first.

 

They’d laid out their ground rules and Kara said they weren’t allowed to fool around at work, they had to be professional and resist temptation, she’d also said that it would be easy. Lena saw that as a challenge and turns out it was easy to accomplish.

 

“Luthor, you will be going undercover to meet our contact at the casino in Paris. I need you to get him to talk by any means necessary.” Kara frowned, understanding the implication.

 

Lena opened her mouth to answer, “wait, no. Why does she have to do that?” Kara said. The pair looked at her, the outburst was unusual, Kara was usually quiet and docile unless Lena was winding her up. “Um, I mean, why does Lena get to go and I don’t?”

 

Cat cleared her throat, “well, if you had let me finish, I would have explained your assignment. Is that lipstick on your neck?” Kara’s eyes widened and her hand flew up to her neck. Sorry darling, Lena mouthed with a small shrug.

 

“Um, no. This- um, my collar is tight it’s rubbing against my neck, she wiped the remaining lipstick away. Lena’s head dropped to hide her smile, oh she fucking knew! Kara sent her a murderous glare and missed the rest of what she was being told.

 

Cat looked at her closely, then she turned and stared directly at Lena’s scarlet painted lips. She looked between the two: Kara swallowed hard and Lena looked more nervous then Kara had ever seen her. “Right,” she announced. “Who had three months?” There was whooping and hollering from all over the office, combined with groaning and grumbling. Kara watched, mouth gaping as Barry wheeled out a whiteboard from behind the main one they used to map out their cases.

 

“Klaus, Monroe and Elin all wagered three months but, Lemarc actually wagered this would be the day they finally, and I quote, “get their heads out of their asses”.” Nia explained, Lemarc grumbled something about how knew all along.

 

Kara and Lena looked at one another, “you were betting on us!” Kara exclaimed.

 

“Since the first day Lena walked in here and you spilt coffee in your lap.” Nia said, Lena snorted at the memory, Kara winced and subconsciously rubbed her thigh where the skin had been red and painful for days.

 

“I’ve come to expect things like this from you Barry but Brainy, I thought we were closer than that.” Kara crossed her arms and pouted.

 

“I was unfortunately sworn to secrecy,” he gave a side-ways glance to Nia.

 

“That’s cold, dude.” Kara aimed at Nia.

 

“Well, I wanted to win,” she grumbled. “Honestly, I thought it would take you longer. I bet six months.”  

 

“Well, jokes on you because Lena and I have been together for well over two years. We have a house an-and a dog. Tell them, Lee!” Lena’s jaw dropped and she struggled to find her words for a second.

 

“W-we have a house and a dog.” She confirmed, clearly just as bewildered as Kara.

 

Cat clasped her hands together, “you all owe me two hundred spenn.” She announced and there was a collective groan. “Oh, be quiet. I promise to put it towards the office Christmas party.”

 

Cat Grant was a smart woman. She’d had her suspicions from the very beginning: the pair were tough on each other when they sparred but Cat had caught the glances when one of them landed too hard, the soft touches on the injured body part before Lena shoved Kara away with a cheeky smile and a challenging look.

 

She’d watched Kara tense up when Lena had been sent on an assignment without her and the look of relief when Lena had come back unharmed. And anyone with eyes in their head could see the loving looks Lena shot Kara or the fact that Kara couldn’t take her eyes off her “partner” for more than a few seconds.

 

To their credit, they had done a good job at concealing their true feelings but Cat saw through them, the love between them was clear as day.

 

“What is going on?” Kara groaned, rubbing her hands over her face.

 

“You two,” Cat pointed at the pair, “my office, now. You have so much paperwork to fill in, HR is gonna have a fucking field day with all of this.” Cat sighed.

 

__________

 

Kara never believed in soulmates, she never believed that there was meant to be one person in the world who was perfectly suited for her. Now she was with Lena and she didn’t believe there was anyone else she could ever want more.

 

They weren’t perfect people but she believed they were perfect for one another.

 

So things didn’t work out the way they had planned, but when does life ever go as planned? It didn’t matter what they went through, they would always find their way back to one another because they were unbreakable. Kara gave Lena a life, her freedom and created a safe haven for her to be herself. Lena gave Kara the truth, she gave her a chance at happiness and the opportunity to have a family.

 

The truth is, they love each other unconditionally: they embrace each other’s flaws and help each other to be better.

 

Neither woman could ask for anything more.
